p.seg: B The Commentary
B1 Duke Huì's first consort was Mèngzǐ.
When Mèngzǐ died,
Shēngzǐ succeeded her as consort
and gave birth to Duke Yǐn.
Duke Wǔ of Sòng had a daughter named Zhòngzǐ.
Zhòngzǐ was born with characters on her hand,
which read "Lady of Lǔ,"
so Zhòngzǐ was married to our state.
She gave birth to Duke Huán, and then Duke Huì passed away.
Therefore, Duke Yǐn was established to serve him.
A1.1 The Spring and Autumn Annals, First Year of Duke Yǐn
A1.1.1 In the first year, spring, the royal first month.
A1.1.2 In the third month,
the Duke and Zhū Yífù made a covenant at Miè.
A1.1.3 In summer, the fifth month,
the Earl of Zhèng defeated Duàn at Yān.
A1.1.4 In autumn, the seventh month,
the Heavenly King sent the steward Xuǎn to present burial gifts for Duke Huì
and Zhòngzǐ.
A1.1.5 In the ninth month,
a covenant was made with a man of Sòng at Sù.
A1.1.6 In winter, the twelfth month,
Zhài Bó came.
A1.1.7 The nobleman Yìshī died.
B1.1 The Commentary, First Year of Duke Yǐn
B1.1.1 In the first year, spring,
it was the first month of the Zhōu royal calendar.
The record does not mention his accession,
because he was acting as regent.
B1.1.2 In the third month,
the Duke and Zhū Yífù made a covenant at Miè.
This was Zhūzǐ Kè.
As he had not yet received royal appointment,
he is not recorded with his rank.
He is called "Yífù"
as a mark of respect.
The Duke, acting as regent, wished to establish good relations with Zhū,
hence the covenant at Miè.
B1.1.3 In summer, the fourth month,
Fèi Bó led troops to fortify Láng.
This is not recorded
because it was not done on the Duke's orders.
B1.1.4 Formerly,
Duke Wǔ of Zhèng married a woman from Shēn,
named Wǔ Jiāng.
She gave birth to Duke Zhuāng and Gòngshū Duàn.
Duke Zhuāng was born feet-first,
startling Lady Jiāng,
so he was named Wùshēng ("Awake Birth"),
and she came to dislike him.
She favored Gòngshū Duàn
and wished to establish him.
She repeatedly requested this of Duke Wǔ,
but the Duke would not allow it.
When Duke Zhuāng ascended the throne,
she requested the fief of Zhì for Duàn.
The Duke said:
"Zhì
is a strategic city;
Guó Shū died there.
Any other city I will grant as you command."
She requested Jīng,
and he had Duàn reside there,
calling him the Grand Master of Jīngchéng.
Zhài Zhòng said:
"A capital city
with walls exceeding a hundred zhì
is a danger to the state.
According to the regulations of the former kings:
a major capital
should not exceed one-third the size of the royal capital;
a medium capital,
one-fifth;
a minor capital,
one-ninth.
Now Jīng does not conform to regulations,
it is not according to rule,
and you, my lord, will not be able to bear it."
The Duke said:
"Lady Jiāng desires this;
how can I avoid the harm?"
He replied:
"How could Lady Jiāng ever be satisfied?
It would be better to deal with this early,
and not let it grow and spread!
Once it spreads,
it will be difficult to manage.
Even spreading weeds cannot be eradicated,
how much more so your honored younger brother?"
The Duke said:
"He who commits many wrongs will surely bring about his own ruin;
you, sir, may wait and see."
Soon after, the Grand Master ordered the western and northern border regions to give dual allegiance to him.
Gōngzǐ Lǚ said:
"The state cannot bear dual allegiance;
what will you, my lord, do about it?
If you wish to give the state to the Grand Master,
I request to serve him;
if not,
then I request to eliminate him,
so as not to stir the people's hearts."
The Duke said:
"There is no need;
he will bring it upon himself."
The Grand Master further took the dual-allegiance regions as his own territory,
reaching as far as Lǐnyán.
Zǐfēng said:
"It is time.
With great resources, he will gain the masses."
The Duke said:
"Without righteousness,
he will not have close bonds.
With great resources, he will collapse."
The Grand Master completed his walls, gathered his people,
repaired his armor and weapons,
prepared his foot soldiers and chariots,
and planned to attack Zhèng.
The lady (Wǔ Jiāng) was to open the gates for him.
The Duke learned the date
and said:
"It is time."
He ordered Zǐfēng to lead two hundred chariots to attack Jīng.
Jīng rebelled against the Grand Master Duàn.
Duàn fled into Yān.
The Duke attacked him at Yān.
On the xīnchǒu day of the fifth month,
the Grand Master fled to Gòng.
The record says:
"The Earl of Zhèng defeated Duàn at Yān."
Duàn did not act as a younger brother,
so he is not called "younger brother";
it was like two rulers,
hence "defeated";
calling him "the Earl of Zhèng"
criticizes his failure in teaching;
it is said to reflect Zhèng's intention.
Not mentioning his flight
makes it difficult for him.
Then he placed Lady Jiāng in Chéngyǐng
and swore to her:
"Not until the Yellow Springs
shall we meet again!"
Soon after, he regretted it.
Yǐng Kǎoshū was the border official of Yǐnggǔ.
Hearing of this,
he had something to present to the Duke.
The Duke gave him food.
When eating, he set aside the meat.
The Duke asked him about it.
He replied:
"I have a mother
who has tasted all my food,
but she has never tasted the meat broth of a lord.
I request to give this to her."
The Duke said:
"You have a mother to give to,
but I alone have none!"
Yǐng Kǎoshū said:
"May I ask what you mean?"
The Duke told him the reason
and also told him of his regret.
He replied:
"What trouble is there in this, my lord?
If you dig the earth until you reach the springs,
and meet in a tunnel,
who can say it is not so?"
The Duke followed his advice.
The Duke entered and chanted:
"Within the great tunnel,
how joyful and harmonious!"
Lady Jiāng came out and chanted:
"Outside the great tunnel,
how joyful and carefree!"
Thus, mother and son were as before.
The gentleman says:
"Yǐng Kǎoshū
was of pure filial piety.
Loving his mother,
he extended it to Duke Zhuāng.
The Book of Songs says:
'The filial son's bounty is never exhausted;
forever he confers it on his kind.'
Is this not speaking of him?"
B1.1.5 In autumn, the seventh month,
the Heavenly King sent the steward Xuǎn to present burial gifts for Duke Huì
and Zhòngzǐ.
This was late,
and furthermore, Zǐshì (Zhòngzǐ) had not yet died,
hence the naming.
The Son of Heaven is buried after seven months,
and all within the same realm arrive.
The feudal lords after five months,
and their allies arrive.
The senior officials after three months,
and those of equal rank arrive.
The officers after one month,
and relatives by marriage arrive.
To present gifts for the dead after the body is interred,
or to offer condolences to the living after the mourning period,
is to anticipate inauspicious events,
and is contrary to ritual.
B1.1.6 In the eighth month,
the people of Jì attacked Yí.
Yí did not report it,
therefore it was not recorded.
B1.1.7 There were flying insects.
They did not cause a disaster,
therefore they were also not recorded.
B1.1.8 In the latter years of Duke Huì,
he defeated the Sòng army at Huáng.
When the Duke came to the throne, he sought peace.
In the ninth month,
he made a covenant with the people of Sòng at Sù,
beginning diplomatic relations.
B1.1.9 In winter, on the Gēngshēn day of the tenth month,
Duke Huì was reburied.
The Duke did not attend the ceremony,
therefore it was not recorded.
When Duke Huì died,
there was a Sòng army,
the crown prince was young,
and the burial was therefore incomplete,
so he was reburied.
B1.1.10 The Marquis of Wèi came to attend the burial,
but did not meet with the Duke,
therefore it was also not recorded.
B1.1.11 During the rebellion of Gòngshū of Zhèng,
Gōngsūn Huá fled to Wèi.
The people of Wèi attacked Zhèng on his behalf,
and captured Línyán.
The people of Zhèng, with the king's army
and the Guó army, attacked the southern borders of Wèi.
They requested troops from Zhū,
and the Viscount of Zhū privately sent Gōngzǐ Yù.
Yù requested to go,
but the Duke did not permit it,
so he went anyway,
and made a covenant with the people of Zhū
and Zhèng at Yì.
It was not recorded,
because it was not by the Duke's command.
B1.1.12 The south gate was newly built,
but it was not recorded,
also because it was not by the Duke's command.
B1.1.13 In the twelfth month,
Jì Bó came,
but it was not by the king's command.
B1.1.14 Zhòngfù died,
and the Duke did not attend the minor dressing ceremony,
therefore the day was not recorded.
A1.2 The Annals of Duke Yǐn, Year Two
A1.2.1 In the second year, in spring,
the Duke met with the Róng at Qián.
A1.2.2 In summer, in the fifth month,
the people of Jǔ entered Xiàng.
A1.2.3 Wú Hài led an army and entered Jí.
A1.2.4 In autumn, on the Gēngchén day of the eighth month,
the Duke and the Róng made a covenant at Táng.
A1.2.5 In the ninth month,
Jì Lièxū came to meet the bride.
A1.2.6 In winter, in the tenth month,
Bó Jī went to Jì.
A1.2.7 Jì Zǐbó
and the Viscount of Jǔ made a covenant at Mì.
A1.2.8 On the Yǐmǎo day of the twelfth month,
the lady Zǐshì died.
A1.2.9 The people of Zhèng attacked Wèi.
B1.2 The Commentary on Duke Yǐn, Year Two
B1.2.1 In the second year, in spring,
the Duke met with the Róng at Qián,
to renew the friendly relations of Duke Huì.
The Róng requested a covenant,
but the Duke declined.
B1.2.2 The Viscount of Jǔ married a woman from Xiàng,
but Xiàng Jiāng was not content in Jǔ and returned.
In summer,
the people of Jǔ entered Xiàng,
and brought Jiāngshì back.
B1.2.3 Minister of Works Wú Hài entered Jí,
and Fèi Qínfǔ defeated it.
B1.2.4 The Róng requested a covenant.
In autumn,
they made a covenant at Táng,
again renewing friendly relations with the Róng.
B1.2.5 In the ninth month,
Jì Lièxū came to meet the bride,
as a minister acting for his lord.
B1.2.6 In winter,
Jì Zǐbó
and the Viscount of Jǔ
made a covenant at Mì,
because of Lǔ.
B1.2.7 The people of Zhèng attacked Wèi,
to punish the rebellion of Gōngsūn Huá.
A1.3 The Annals of Duke Yǐn, Year Three
A1.3.1 In the third year, in spring, in the king's second month,
on the Jǐsì day,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
A1.3.2 In the third month, on the Gēngxū day,
the Heavenly King passed away.
A1.3.3 In summer, in the fourth month, on the Xīnmǎo day,
the lady Jūnshì died.
A1.3.4 In autumn,
Wǔshìzǐ came to request funeral gifts.
A1.3.5 In the eighth month, on the Gēngchén day,
Duke Hé of Sòng died.
A1.3.6 In winter, in the twelfth month,
the Marquis of Qí
and the Earl of Zhèng made a covenant at Shímén.
A1.3.7 On the Guǐwèi day,
Duke Mù of Sòng was buried.
B1.3 The Commentary on Duke Yǐn, Year Three
B1.3.1 In the third year, in spring,
in the king's third month,
on the Rénxū day,
King Píng passed away.
The announcement reported the Gēngxū day,
therefore it was recorded as such.
B1.3.2 In summer,
the lady Jūnshì died.
— — This was Shēngzǐ.
No announcement was sent to the feudal lords,
there was no returning to weep in the ancestral temple,
and she was not enshrined with her mother-in-law,
therefore she was not called
"passed away."
She was not addressed as a wife,
therefore her burial was not mentioned,
and her surname was not recorded.
For the Duke's sake,
she was called
"the lady Jūnshì."
B1.3.3 Earl Wǔ and Earl Zhuāng of Zhèng
were ministers of King Píng.
The king favored Guó.
The Earl of Zhèng resented the king.
The king said:
"It is not so."
Therefore Zhōu and Zhèng exchanged hostages.
Prince Hú was sent as a hostage to Zhèng,
and Prince Hū of Zhèng was sent as a hostage to Zhōu.
When the king passed away,
the people of Zhōu were about to give power to the Duke of Guó.
In the fourth month,
Jì Zú of Zhèng led an army to take the wheat of Wēn.
In autumn,
he also took the grain of Chéngzhōu.
Zhōu and Zhèng became hostile.
A gentleman said:
"If trust does not come from the heart,
hostages are of no benefit.
Act with clear understanding and consideration,
bound by ritual,
even without hostages,
who can come between?
If there is clear trust,
even the plants by the streams, valleys,
ponds, and islets,
the duckweed, artemisia,
and waterweed vegetables,
Baskets and hampers,
tripods and cauldrons as vessels,
puddle and ditch,
roadside puddle water,
can be offered to ghosts and spirits,
can be presented to kings and lords,
so how much more when a gentleman forges trust between two states,
acting with ritual,
why then use hostages?
The "Airs" have "Gathering White Southernwood"
and "Gathering Duckweed,"
the "Elegantiae" have "The Rushes by the Path"
and "Distant Dipping,"
all to illuminate loyalty and trust."
B1.3.4 Wǔshìzǐ came to request funeral contributions,
as the king had not yet been buried.
B1.3.5 Duke Mù of Sòng fell ill,
summoned the Grand Marshal Kǒng Fù
and entrusted Duke Shāng to him,
saying:
"Our former ruler passed over Yǔyí and established me,
I dare not forget.
If, through the good fortune of you, Great Officer,
I am able to preserve my head and die;
if our former ruler asks about Yǔyí,
what words shall I have to answer?
I beg you, sir, to support him,
to be master of the altars of soil and grain.
Though I die,
I will have no regrets."
He replied:
"The ministers wish to support Féng."
The duke said:
"That will not do.
Our former ruler considered me worthy,
and made me master of the altars of soil and grain.
If I abandon virtue and do not yield,
this is to overturn the selection of our former ruler,
how can it be called worthy?
To glorify and illuminate the excellent virtue of our former ruler,
should we not strive for it?
My son, do not overturn the achievement of our former ruler!"
He sent the duke's son Féng to go out and reside in Zhèng.
In the eighth month, on the Gēngchén day,
Duke Mù of Sòng died,
and Duke Shāng took the throne.
The gentleman says:
"Duke Xuān of Sòng may be said to have known men.
He established Duke Mù,
and his son enjoyed it,
his command was righteous indeed!
The "Eulogies of Shāng" says:
'The Yīn received the mandate, all was fitting,
they bore all blessings.'
Is it not speaking of this?"
B1.3.6 In winter,
Qí and Zhèng made a covenant at Shímén,
renewing the covenant of Lú.
On the Gēngxū day,
the chariot of the Earl of Zhèng overturned in the Jǐ River.
B1.3.7 Duke Zhuāng of Wèi took a wife from Qí, the younger sister of Déchén, heir apparent of the Eastern Palace,
named Zhuāng Jiāng.
She was beautiful but bore no sons,
the men of Wèi composed "The Tall Lady" about her.
He also took a wife from Chén,
named Lì Guī.
She gave birth to Xiàobó,
who died young.
Her younger sister, Dài Guī,
gave birth to Duke Huán,
and Zhuāng Jiāng regarded him as her own son.
The duke's son Zhōuyù
was the son of a favored concubine.
He was favored and fond of arms,
the duke did not restrain him.
Zhuāng Jiāng disliked him.
Shí Què remonstrated, saying:
"Your servant has heard that to love a son,
one should instruct him with righteous principles,
and not lead him into depravity.
Arrogance, extravagance, dissipation, and excess
are the paths to depravity.
The coming of these four
is due to excessive favor and emolument.
If you intend to establish Zhōuyù,
then decide it now;
if not yet,
it will become a step to disaster.
For one who is favored yet not arrogant,
arrogant yet able to step down,
stepped down yet without resentment,
resentful yet able to restrain himself,
is rare indeed.
Moreover, the base obstructing the noble,
the younger overriding the elder,
the distant alienating the close,
the new alienating the old,
the small encroaching on the great,
the depraved destroying the righteous,
these are the so-called six perversities;
the ruler righteous,
the minister dutiful,
the father kind,
the son filial,
the elder brother loving,
the younger brother respectful,
these are the so-called six conformities.
To abandon conformity and imitate perversity
is the way to hasten disaster.
He who rules men,
should strive to remove disasters,
yet you hasten them,
is this not unacceptable?"
He did not listen.
His son Hòu associated with Zhōuyù,
he forbade it,
but could not stop it.
When Duke Huán was established,
he then retired.
A1.4 "The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Yǐn Year 4"
A1.4.1 In the fourth year, spring,
the king's second month,
the men of Jǔ attacked Qǐ,
and took Móulóu.
A1.4.2 On the Wùshēn day,
Wèi's Zhōuyù assassinated his ruler, Wán.
A1.4.3 In summer,
our duke and the Duke of Sòng met at Qīng.
A1.4.4 The Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the men of Cài,
and the men of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
A1.4.5 In autumn,
Huī led troops to join the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the men of Cài,
and the men of Wèi in attacking Zhèng.
A1.4.6 In the ninth month,
the men of Wèi killed Zhōuyù at Pú.
A1.4.7 In winter, the twelfth month,
the men of Wèi established Jìn.
B1.4 "The Commentary of Zuǒ, Duke Yǐn Year 4"
B1.4.1 In the fourth year, spring,
Wèi's Zhōuyù assassinated Duke Huán and took the throne.
B1.4.2 Our duke and the Duke of Sòng were to hold a meeting,
intending to renew the covenant of Sù.
Before the scheduled date,
men from Wèi came to report the disorder.
In summer,
our duke and the Duke of Sòng met at Qīng.
B1.4.3 When Duke Shāng of Sòng took the throne,
the duke's son Féng fled to Zhèng.
The men of Zhèng wished to install him.
When Wèi's Zhōuyù took the throne,
he intended to settle the former ruler's grievance with Zhèng,
and to seek favor among the feudal lords,
in order to pacify his people.
He sent word to Sòng, saying:
"If you, my lord, attack Zhèng
to remove your harm,
with you, my lord, as the leader,
our humble city will supply troops and follow along with Chén
and Cài,
this is the wish of Wèi."
The men of Sòng agreed.
At that time, Chén
and Cài were on good terms with Wèi,
so the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the men of Cài,
and the men of Wèi attacked Zhèng,
besieging its eastern gate,
and withdrew after five days.
Our duke asked Zhòng Zhòng, saying:
"Will Wèi's Zhōuyù succeed?"
He replied:
"Your servant has heard of using virtue to pacify the people,
but not of using disorder.
To use disorder,
is like trying to untangle silk but only tangling it further.
As for Zhōu Xū,
he relies on military force and is content with cruelty.
Relying on military force will lose him the masses,
and being content with cruelty will lose him his kin.
When the masses rebel
and kin turn away,
it will be difficult to succeed.
Military force
is like fire;
if not restrained,
it will consume oneself.
Zhōu Xū assassinated his ruler
and tyrannized his people.
Thus, not cultivating virtuous governance
but attempting to achieve success through disorder
will inevitably lead to his downfall."
B1.4.4 In autumn,
the feudal lords again attacked Zhèng.
The Duke of Sòng sent a messenger to request troops,
but the Duke (of Lǔ) declined.
Yǔfǔ requested to lead troops to join them,
but the Duke did not permit it.
He insisted on the request and proceeded.
Therefore, the record says
"Huī led the troops,"
criticizing him.
The armies of the feudal lords defeated Zhèng's infantry,
took their grain, and returned.
B1.4.5 Zhōu Xū was unable to bring harmony to his people,
so Hòu (Shí Hòu) consulted Shí Zǐ (Shí Què) about stabilizing the ruler.
Shí Zǐ said:
"An audience with the King would be advisable."
(Hòu) asked:
"How can we obtain an audience?"
(Shí Zǐ) replied:
"Duke Huán of Chén is currently favored by the King.
Chén and Wèi are currently on good terms.
If you go to court in Chén and have them make the request,
it will certainly be granted."
Hòu followed Zhōu Xū to Chén.
Shí Què sent a message to Chén, saying:
"Wèi is a small and narrow state,
and I, an old man, am aged and feeble.
I am incapable of action.
These two men
are indeed the ones who assassinated our ruler.
I venture to request that you deal with them."
The men of Chén seized them
and requested that (Wèi) come to oversee (their punishment).
In the ninth month,
the men of Wèi sent Yòuzǎi Chǒu to oversee the execution of Zhōu Xū at Pú.
Shí Què sent his steward Nòu Yángjiān to oversee the execution of Shí Hòu in Chén.
The gentleman remarks:
"Shí Què
was a pure minister.
He detested Zhōu Xū and (his own son) Hòu was involved with him.
'Upholding great righteousness to eliminate one's kin' —
is this not what it refers to!"
B1.4.6 The men of Wèi welcomed Prince Jìn from Xíng.
In winter, in the twelfth month, Duke Xuān ascended the throne.
The record says
"The men of Wèi established Jìn,"
because it was the will of the multitude.
A1.5 *The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Yǐn Year 5*
A1.5.1 In the fifth year, spring,
the Duke shot fish at Táng.
A1.5.2 In summer, the fourth month,
Duke Huán of Wèi was buried.
A1.5.3 In autumn,
the army of Wèi entered Chéng.
A1.5.4 In the ninth month,
the temple of Zhòngzǐ was completed.
For the first time, six rows of dancers were presented.
A1.5.5 The men of Zhū and
the men of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
A1.5.6 There were caterpillars.
A1.5.7 In winter, on the xīnsì day of the twelfth month,
Prince Kōu died.
A1.5.8 The men of Sòng attacked Zhèng and besieged Chánggé.
B1.5 *The Commentary of Zuǒ, Duke Yǐn Year 5*
B1.5.1 In the fifth year, spring,
the Duke intended to go to Táng to observe the fishermen.
Zāng Xībó remonstrated, saying:
"In general, if things are not sufficient for discussing major affairs,
and their materials are not sufficient for preparing implements,
then the ruler should not engage with them.
The ruler
is one who guides the people into norms and
proper things.
Therefore, discussing affairs
to measure norms and standards is called 'norms';
selecting materials to display the elegance of things is called 'things'.
Acting outside norms and things
is called disorderly governance.
When disorderly governance is frequently practiced,
it is the cause of ruin.
Thus, the spring hunt,
summer hunt,
autumn hunt,
and winter hunt
are all conducted during agricultural breaks to discuss affairs.
Every three years, troops are drilled,
and upon returning, the ranks are reviewed.
Upon returning, a victory feast is held,
to count the military spoils.
To display insignia and patterns,
clarify nobility and baseness,
distinguish ranks and orders,
arrange the young and old in proper sequence,
and practice dignified rituals.
As for birds and beasts, if their meat
is not fit for the sacrificial stand,
and their hides, teeth, bones, horns, feathers, and down are not fit for implements,
then the lord does not shoot them—such is the ancient rule.
As for the products of mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes,
the materials for implements,
these are the affairs of petty officers and servants,
the duties of officials in charge,
not something the ruler should involve himself with."
The Duke said:
"I intend to inspect the territory."
He then went,
displayed fish, and observed them.
Xībó pleaded illness and did not follow.
The record says
"The Duke shot fish at Táng,"
because it was contrary to ritual,
and also indicates it was a distant place.
B1.5.2 Zhuāng Bó of Qūwò used the men of Zhèng and
the men of Xíng to attack Yì.
The King sent the Yǐn clan and
the Wǔ clan to assist him.
The Marquis of Yì fled to Suí.
B1.5.3 In summer,
Duke Huán of Wèi was buried.
Because of the disorder in Wèi,
it was delayed.
B1.5.4 In the fourth month,
the men of Zhèng invaded the pastures of Wèi,
in retaliation for the battle at the Eastern Gate.
The men of Wèi attacked Zhèng with the army of Yān.
Zhài Zú,
Yuán Fán,
and Xiè Jià of Zhèng
led the three armies to face them head-on,
while sending Màn Bó and Zǐ Yuán to secretly lead troops to attack their rear.
The men of Yān feared Zhèng's three armies
and did not anticipate the men of Zhì.
In the sixth month,
the two princes of Zhèng used the men of Zhì to defeat the Yān army at Běizhì.
The gentleman remarks:
"Without preparation and without anticipating the unexpected,
one cannot command an army."
B1.5.5 Qūwò rebelled against the King.
In autumn,
the King ordered Duke Guó to attack Qūwò,
and established Āi Hóu in Yì.
B1.5.6 During the disorder in Wèi,
the men of Chéng invaded Wèi,
therefore the army of Wèi entered Chéng.
B1.5.7 In the ninth month,
the temple of Zhòngzǐ was completed,
and they intended to perform the wàn dance there.
The Duke asked Zhòng Zhòng about the number of feather rows.
He replied:
"The Son of Heaven uses eight,
feudal lords use six,
great officers use four,
and officers use two.
The dance
is to regulate the eight musical tones
and manifest the eight winds,
therefore it descends from eight downwards."
The Duke followed this.
Thus, for the first time, six rows of dancers were presented,
beginning the use of six rows of dancers.
B1.5.8 The men of Sòng took fields from Zhū.
The men of Zhū reported to Zhèng, saying:
"We ask you, my lord, to vent your grievance against Sòng,
and our humble state will serve as your guide."
The men of Zhèng joined them with the King's army,
attacked Sòng,
entered its outer walls,
in retaliation for the battle at the Eastern Gate.
The people of Sòng sent a messenger to report the situation.
The Duke heard that they had entered the outer walls,
and was about to rescue them.
He asked the messenger:
"How far has the army advanced?"
The messenger replied:
"They have not yet reached the capital."
The Duke was angry,
and so stopped.
He dismissed the messenger, saying:
"Your lord commanded me to share in the concern for the difficulties of the altars of soil and grain.
Now I ask the messenger,
and he says:
'The army has not yet reached the capital.'
This is not something I dare to know."
B1.5.9 In winter, in the twelfth month, on the xīnsì day,
Zāng Xībó died.
The Duke said:
"My uncle had resentment toward me,
and I dare not forget it."
He was buried with one grade higher in rank.
B1.5.10 The people of Sòng attacked Zhèng,
surrounding Chánggé,
in retaliation for the campaign of entering the outer walls.
A1.6 "The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 6 of Duke Yǐn"
A1.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring,
people from Zhèng came to renew peace.
A1.6.2 In summer, in the fifth month, on the xīnyǒu day,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí,
and made a covenant at Ài.
A1.6.3 In autumn, in the seventh month.
A1.6.4 In winter,
the people of Sòng took Chánggé.
B1.6 "The Commentary of Zuǒ, Year 6 of Duke Yǐn"
B1.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring,
people from Zhèng came to renew peace,
which was to re-establish an agreement.
B1.6.2 Jiāfù, son of Qǐngfǔ, the leader of the nine clans and five officials of Yì,
welcomed the Marquis of Jìn in Suí,
and installed him in È.
The people of Jìn called him the Marquis of È.
B1.6.3 In summer,
they made a covenant at Ài,
beginning peace with Qí.
B1.6.4 In the fifth month, on the gēngshēn day,
the Earl of Zhèng invaded Chén,
and achieved a great capture.
In previous years,
the Earl of Zhèng had requested an agreement with Chén,
but the Marquis of Chén did not consent.
Wǔfǔ remonstrated, saying:
"To be close to the benevolent
and friendly with neighbors
is the treasure of a state.
May you, my lord, consent to Zhèng!"
The Marquis of Chén said:
"Sòng
and Wèi are truly difficult;
what can Zhèng do?"
Thus he did not consent.
The gentleman said:
"Goodness must not be lost,
evil must not be allowed to grow.
Is this not speaking of Duke Huán of Chén?
To allow evil to grow without repentance
is to bring harm upon oneself.
Even if one wishes to save it,
how can it be done?
The 'Shāngshū' says:
'The ease with which evil spreads
is like a fire spreading across the plains.
One cannot approach it;
how can it be extinguished?'
Zhōurén had a saying:
'Those who govern a state,
when they see evil,
should be like farmers who must remove weeds:
cut them down and pile them up,
sever their roots,
and not let them propagate.
Then the good will flourish.'"
B1.6.5 In autumn,
the people of Sòng took Chánggé.
B1.6.6 In winter,
the capital came to report famine.
The Duke on their behalf requested grain from Sòng,
Wèi, Qí,
and Zhèng,
which was according to ritual.
B1.6.7 The Earl of Zhèng went to Zhōu,
for the first time paying court to King Huán.
The king did not treat him with courtesy.
Duke Huán of Zhōu said to the king:
"When our Zhōu moved east,
we relied on Jìn and Zhèng.
To treat Zhèng well so as to encourage others to come
still leaves us fearing it is not enough;
how much more if we do not treat them with courtesy?
Zhèng will not come again."
A1.7 "The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 7 of Duke Yǐn"
A1.7.1 In the seventh year, in spring,
in the king's third month,
Shū Jī went to Jì.
A1.7.2 The Marquis of Téng died.
A1.7.3 In summer,
they walled Zhōngqiū.
A1.7.4 The Marquis of Qí sent his younger brother Nián on a courtesy visit.
A1.7.5 In autumn,
the Duke attacked Zhū.
A1.7.6 In winter,
the Heavenly King sent Fán Bó on a courtesy visit.
The Róng attacked Fán Bó at Chǔqiū and took him back.
B1.7 "The Commentary of Zuǒ, Year 7 of Duke Yǐn"
B1.7.1 In the seventh year, in spring,
the Marquis of Téng died.
His personal name was not recorded,
because he had not made a covenant with us.
Whenever feudal lords made a covenant together,
they would then be referred to by their personal names.
Therefore, when they died,
they would be announced by their personal names,
to report the end and announce the successor,
in order to continue good relations and give rest to the people.
This is called the constant rule of ritual.
B1.7.2 In summer,
they walled Zhōngqiū.
It was recorded because it was not the proper season.
B1.7.3 The Marquis of Qí sent Yízhòng Nián on a courtesy visit,
to consolidate the covenant of Ài.
B1.7.4 In autumn,
Sòng and Zhèng made peace.
In the seventh month, on the gēngshēn day,
they made a covenant at Sù.
The Duke attacked Zhū,
to campaign on behalf of Sòng.
B1.7.5 Earlier,
the Róng paid court to Zhōu,
and presented gifts to the dukes and ministers.
Fán Bó did not treat them as guests.
In winter,
the king sent Fán Bó on a courtesy visit.
On his return,
the Róng attacked him at Chǔqiū and took him back.
B1.7.6 Chén and Zhèng made peace.
In the twelfth month,
Chén Wǔfǔ went to Zhèng to attend the covenant.
On the rénshēn day,
he made a covenant with the Earl of Zhèng,
but when he smeared the blood, he seemed forgetful.
Xiè Bó said:
"Wǔfǔ will surely not escape misfortune,
for he does not rely on covenants."
Zhèng Liángzuǒ went to Chén to attend the covenant.
On the xīnsì day,
he made a covenant with the Marquis of Chén,
and also knew that Chén was about to fall into disorder.
B1.7.7 The Zhèng prince Hū was at the king's court,
so the Marquis of Chén requested to give him a wife.
The Earl of Zhèng consented,
and then the marriage was completed.
A1.8 "The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 8 of Duke Yǐn"
A1.8.1 In the eighth year, in spring,
the Duke of Sòng
and the Marquis of Wèi met at Chuí.
A1.8.2 In the third month,
the Earl of Zhèng sent Wǎn to come and return Bēng.
On the gēngyín day,
we entered Bēng.
A1.8.3 In summer, in the sixth month, on the jǐhài day,
the Marquis of Cài, Kǎofù, died.
A1.8.4 On the xīnhài day,
the Earl of Sù died.
A1.8.5 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gēngwǔ day,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Qí,
and the Marquis of Wèi made a covenant at Wǎwū.
A1.8.6 In the eighth month,
Duke Xuān of Cài was buried.
A1.8.7 On Xīnmǎo day of the ninth month,
the Duke and a man from Jǔ made a covenant at Fúlái.
A1.8.8 There were borers.
A1.8.9 In winter, in the twelfth month,
Wúhài died.
B1.8 The Commentary of Duke Yǐn, Year 8
B1.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
the Marquis of Qí was about to bring peace between Sòng and Wèi.
A meeting date was set.
The Duke of Sòng, using gifts, made a request of Wèi,
asking to meet first.
The Marquis of Wèi agreed,
so they met at Quǎnqiū.
B1.8.2 The Earl of Zhèng requested to discontinue the sacrifices at Mount Tài
and instead sacrifice to the Duke of Zhōu,
exchanging the Bēng district of Mount Tài for the fields of Xǔ.
In the third month,
the Earl of Zhèng sent Wǎn to come and hand over Bēng,
as he would no longer sacrifice at Mount Tài.
B1.8.3 In summer,
Duke Jìfù of Guó began serving as a Minister at the Zhōu court.
B1.8.4 On Jiǎchén day of the fourth month,
Zhèng's prince Hū went to Chén to meet his bride, Guī.
On Xīnhài day,
he brought Lady Guī back.
On Jiǎyǐn day,
they entered Zhèng.
Chén Qiánzǐ escorted the bride.
They cohabited first and then performed the ancestral temple ceremony.
Qiánzǐ said:
"This does not make them husband and wife,
it deceives his ancestors,
it is contrary to ritual,
how can they produce offspring?"
B1.8.5 The men of Qí finally brought peace between Sòng
and Wèy with Zhèng.
In autumn,
they met at Wēn,
and made a covenant at Wǎwū,
to resolve the campaign at the Eastern Gate,
which was according to ritual.
B1.8.6 On Bǐngxū day of the eighth month,
the Earl of Zhèng, with the men of Qí, had audience with the King,
which was according to ritual.
B1.8.7 The Duke and a man from Jǔ made a covenant at Fúlái,
to cement the good relations with Jǐ.
B1.8.8 In winter,
the Marquis of Qí sent a messenger
to report the peace achieved among the three states.
The Duke sent Zhòngzhòng to reply, saying:
"You, my lord, have abandoned the schemes of the three states,
to bring order to their people,
this is your grace.
My humble ruler has heard your command,
how dare he not receive and accept your brilliant virtue."
B1.8.9 Wúhài died.
Yǔfǔ requested a posthumous name and a clan name for him.
The Duke asked Zhòngzhòng about clan names.
Zhòngzhòng replied:
"The Son of Heaven establishes those with virtue,
and bestows surnames based on their birth,
grants them land
and commands their clan names.
The feudal lords use the courtesy name as the posthumous name,
and thereby form the clan.
If an office has hereditary merit,
then it becomes an official clan.
The same applies to fiefs."
The Duke commanded that the courtesy name be used to form the Zhǎn clan.
A1.9 The Spring and Autumn Annals of Duke Yǐn, Year 9
A1.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
the Heavenly King sent Nán Jì to come on a friendly mission.
A1.9.2 On Guǐyǒu day of the third month,
there was heavy rain,
with thunder and lightning.
On Gēngchén day,
there was heavy snow.
A1.9.3 Xié died.
A1.9.4 In summer,
the walls of Láng were built.
A1.9.5 In autumn, in the seventh month.
A1.9.6 In winter,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Fáng.
B1.9 The Commentary of Duke Yǐn, Year 9
B1.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year, in the royal third month, on Guǐyǒu day,
there was heavy, continuous rain with thunder,
the record notes the beginning.
On Gēngchén day,
there was heavy snow,
and it was the same.
The record
indicates the season was out of order.
Generally, for rain,
if it lasts for three days or more it is called 'continuous rain',
and if it accumulates to a foot on level ground it is called 'great snow'.
B1.9.2 In summer,
the walls of Láng were built.
The record
indicates it was not the proper season.
B1.9.3 The Duke of Sòng did not pay court to the King.
The Earl of Zhèng, serving as the King's Minister of the Left,
used the King's command to punish him.
He attacked Sòng.
Sòng, because of the campaign when the outer walls were entered, bore a grudge against our Duke,
and did not report the command.
The Duke was angry,
and cut off diplomatic relations with Sòng.
B1.9.4 In autumn,
the men of Zhèng, using the King's command, came to report the attack on Sòng.
B1.9.5 In winter,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Fáng,
to plan an attack on Sòng.
B1.9.6 The Northern Róng invaded Zhèng.
The Earl of Zhèng defended against them,
but was worried about the Róng army,
saying:
"They are on foot, we are in chariots,
I fear they will outflank and penetrate our lines."
Prince Tū said:
"Send brave but not stubborn men,
to test the enemy and quickly withdraw.
You, my lord, prepare three ambushes to await them.
The Róng are careless and undisciplined,
greedy and not close-knit;
when victorious they do not yield to each other,
when defeated they do not rescue each other.
Those in front seeing gains,
will certainly press forward;
advancing and encountering an ambush,
they will certainly flee swiftly.
Those behind will not rescue them,
then they will have no support.
Then we can achieve our aim."
He followed this plan.
The Róng men in front who encountered the ambush fled,
Zhù Dān pursued them,
cut the Róng army in two,
attacked them front and rear,
and annihilated them.
The Róng army fled in great disorder.
On Jiǎyǐn day of the eleventh month,
the men of Zhèng greatly defeated the Róng army.
A1.10 The Spring and Autumn Annals of Duke Yǐn, Year 10
A1.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year, in the royal second month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí
and the Earl of Zhèng at Zhōngqiū.
A1.10.2 In summer,
Huī led troops to join the men of Qí
and Zhèng in attacking Sòng.
A1.10.3 On Rénxū day of the sixth month,
the Duke defeated the army of Sòng at Jiān.
On Xīnwèi day,
he took Gào.
On Xīnsì day,
he took Fáng.
A1.10.4 In autumn,
men of Sòng
and Wèi entered Zhèng.
Men of Sòng,
Cài,
and Wèi attacked Dài.
The Earl of Zhèng attacked and took it.
A1.10.5 In winter, on Rénwǔ day of the tenth month,
men of Qí
and Zhèng entered Chéng.
B1.10 The Commentary of Duke Yǐn, Year 10
B1.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year, in the royal first month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí
and the Earl of Zhèng at Zhōngqiū.
On Guǐchǒu day,
they made a covenant at Dèng,
to set the date for the army.
B1.10.2 In summer, in the fifth month,
Yǔfǔ first joined the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng in attacking Sòng.
B1.10.3 On Wùshēn day of the sixth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng at Lǎotáo.
On Rénxū day,
the Duke defeated the army of Sòng at Jiān.
On the gēngwǔ day,
the army of Zhèng entered Gào.
On the xīnwèi day,
they returned it to us.
On the gēngchén day,
the army of Zhèng entered Fáng.
On the xīnsì day,
they returned it to us.
The gentleman says of Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng
"In this matter, he can be called righteous.
He used the king's command to punish those who did not attend court,
yet he did not covet their lands.
Instead, he labored for the king's enfeoffments,
which is the essence of righteousness."
B1.10.4 The men of Cài, Wèi, and Chéng
did not comply with the king's command.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gēngyín day,
the army of Zhèng entered Jiāo,
and was still at Jiāo.
The men of Sòng
and Wèi entered Zhèng,
and the men of Cài followed them to attack Dài.
In the eighth month, on the rénxū day,
the Earl of Zhèng besieged Dài.
On the guǐhài day,
he captured it,
and took the three armies there.
Sòng and
Wèi, having already entered Zhèng,
then summoned the men of Cài to attack Dài.
The men of Cài were angry,
so they were not harmonious and were defeated.
B1.10.5 In the ninth month, on the wùyín day,
the Earl of Zhèng entered Sòng.
B1.10.6 In winter,
the men of Qí
and Zhèng entered Chéng,
to punish them for disobeying the king's command.
A1.11 *The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 11 of Duke Yǐn*
A1.11.1 In the eleventh year, in spring,
the Marquis of Téng
and the Marquis of Xuē came to court.
A1.11.2 In summer,
the duke met with the Earl of Zhèng at Shílái.
A1.11.3 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the rénwǔ day,
the duke, together with the Marquis of Qí
and the Earl of Zhèng, entered Xǔ.
A1.11.4 In winter, in the eleventh month, on the rénchén day,
the duke passed away.
B1.11 *The Commentary of Zuǒ, Year 11 of Duke Yǐn*
B1.11.1 In the eleventh year, in spring,
the Marquis of Téng
and the Marquis of Xuē came to court,
and contended for precedence.
The Marquis of Xuē said:
"Our state was enfeoffed first."
The Marquis of Téng said:
"I
am the Divination Officer of Zhōu;
Xuē is a common surname,
I cannot be placed after him."
The duke sent Yǔfǔ to make a request to the Marquis of Xuē, saying:
"You and the Lord of Téng have graced me with your presence.
'There is a Zhōu proverb that says:
'When the mountain has trees,
the craftsman measures them;
when the guest has propriety,
the host selects it.'
In the ancestral covenants of Zhōu,
those of different surnames come after.
If I were to go to court in Xuē,
I would not dare to rank with the various Rén clans.
If you would grace me with your favor,
then I wish to make this request on behalf of the Lord of Téng."
The Marquis of Xuē agreed,
and so gave precedence to the Marquis of Téng.
B1.11.2 In summer,
the duke met with the Earl of Zhèng at Lái,
to plan an attack on Xǔ.
The Earl of Zhèng was about to attack Xǔ.
In the fifth month, on the jiǎchén day,
he distributed weapons at the Grand Temple.
Gōngsūn È and Yǐng Kǎoshū contended for a chariot.
Yǐng Kǎoshū tucked the shaft under his arm and ran off,
and Zǐdū drew a halberd and chased him.
When they reached the great thoroughfare,
he did not catch up,
and Zǐdū was angry.
B1.11.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
the duke, together with the Marquis of Qí
and the Earl of Zhèng, attacked Xǔ.
On the gēngchén day,
they arrayed against Xǔ.
Yǐng Kǎoshū took the Earl of Zhèng's banner, Máohú,
and was the first to ascend,
but Zǐdū shot him from below,
and he fell.
Xiá Shūyíng then took the Máohú and ascended,
waved it all around and shouted:
"Our lord has ascended!"
The army of Zhèng all ascended.
On the rénwǔ day,
they then entered Xǔ.
Duke Zhuāng of Xǔ fled to Wèi.
The Marquis of Qí offered Xǔ to the duke.
The duke said:
"You said that Xǔ was not respectful,
so I followed you in punishing it.
Now that Xǔ has admitted its crime,
even though you have given the command,
I dare not hear of it."
He then gave it to the men of Zhèng.
The Earl of Zhèng sent the grand officer of Xǔ, Bǎilǐ, to escort Xǔ Shū
to reside in the eastern part of Xǔ,
saying:
"Heaven brought calamity upon the state of Xǔ.
The ghosts and spirits were indeed displeased with the ruler of Xǔ,
and borrowed my hand.
I have only a few elders and brothers, and cannot satisfy them all.
How dare I take Xǔ as an achievement for myself?
I have a younger brother,
with whom I cannot live in harmony,
and who must beg for food in all directions.
How much less could I long possess Xǔ?
You, sir, shall escort Xǔ
Shū to pacify and soothe this people.
I will send Huò to assist you.
If I am able to die and be buried,
and Heaven, in accordance with propriety, repents of the calamity upon Xǔ,
would it not be that this Duke of Xǔ may again serve his altars of soil and grain?
Only if our state of Zhèng has requests to make,
as in old marriage alliances,
may he condescend to comply.
Do not let other clans press in and dwell here,
to contend with our state of Zhèng for this land.
My sons and grandsons will have no leisure even to avert their own destruction,
how much less could they offer sacrifice to Xǔ?
The reason I have you, sir, dwell here
is not only for the sake of the state of Xǔ,
but also to secure our borders."
He then sent Gōngsūn Huò to reside in the western part of Xǔ,
saying:
"All your vessels, wealth, and valuables,
do not place them in Xǔ.
When I die,
then hasten to leave!
Our former lord newly established his city here.
The royal house has already declined,
and the descendants of Zhōu daily lose their order.
Now Xǔ
is the descendant of Dàyuè.
Since Heaven has already wearied of the virtue of Zhōu,
how can we contend with Xǔ?"
The gentleman says of Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng
"In this matter, he acted with propriety.
Propriety
governs the state and the family,
stabilizes the altars of soil and grain,
orders the people,
and benefits posterity.
Xǔ,
having no law, he attacked it;
when it submitted, he spared it;
he assessed virtue to deal with it,
and measured his strength to act.
He observed the times and moved,
without burdening later generations.
He can be said to know propriety."
B1.11.4 The Earl of Zhèng made each squad contribute a boar,
each platoon contribute a dog
and a chicken,
to curse the one who shot Yǐng Kǎoshū.
The gentleman says of Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng
"He failed in governance and punishment.
Governance is to rule the people,
punishment is to correct evil.
Having neither virtuous governance,
nor awe-inspiring punishment,
is how he fell into evil.
To curse evil,
what good will it do!"
B1.11.5 The king took the fields of Wū,
Liú, Wěi,
and Yú from Zhèng,
and gave to the men of Zhèng the fields of Sū Fènshēng:
Wēn, Yuán,
Chī, Fán,
Xíchéng,
Cuánmáo,
Xiàng, Méng,
Zhōu, Xíng,
Tuí, and Huái.
Thus, the nobleman knew that
King Huán had lost Zhèng.
To act with forbearance
is the principle of virtue,
the constant rule of ritual.
What one cannot possess oneself
yet gives to others—
if others do not come,
is it not fitting?
B1.11.6 Zhèng and
Xī had words of discord.
The Marquis of Xī attacked Zhèng.
The Earl of Zhèng fought with him within his borders,
and the army of Xī was greatly defeated and returned.
Thus, the nobleman knew that Xī was about to perish:
"They did not assess virtue,
did not measure strength,
did not cherish kin,
did not examine words,
did not investigate guilt.
Committing these five wrongs
and thereby attacking others—
their loss of the army,
was it not fitting?"
B1.11.7 In winter, the tenth month,
the Earl of Zhèng attacked Sòng with the army of Guó.
On Rénxū,
they greatly defeated the army of Sòng,
in retaliation for their entry into Zhèng.
Sòng did not report the command,
therefore it was not recorded.
In general, when the feudal lords have commands,
if reported, they are recorded;
if not, then they are not.
Whether an army's campaign is good or bad,
it is also like this.
Even if it reaches the point of destroying a state,
if the destruction is not reported as a defeat,
or victory is not reported as a success,
it is not recorded on the bamboo slips.
B1.11.8 Yǔfǔ requested to kill Duke Huán,
intending to seek the position of Grand Steward.
The Duke said:
"Because he is young,
I am about to hand it over to him.
Have him build Tùqiú,
and I will grow old there."
Yǔfǔ became afraid,
and instead slandered the Duke to Duke Huán and requested to assassinate him.
When the Duke was a prince,
he fought with the people of Zhèng at Húrǎng,
and was detained there.
The people of Zhèng imprisoned him with the Yǐn clan.
He bribed the Yǐn clan,
and prayed to their deity Zhōng Wū.
Then he returned with the Yǐn clan,
and established their deity.
In the eleventh month,
the Duke sacrificed to Zhōng Wū,
fasted at Shèpǔ,
and lodged at the Wěi clan.
On Rénchén,
Yǔfǔ had a ruffian assassinate the Duke at the Wěi clan,
established Duke Huán,
and then punished the Wěi clan,
and there were deaths.
It was not recorded that he was buried,
because the mourning was not completed.
A2.1 "The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Huán Year 1"
A2.1.1 First year, spring,
the royal first month,
the Duke ascended the throne.
A2.1.2 Third month,
the Duke met with the Earl of Zhèng at Chuí,
the Earl of Zhèng used a jade disc to borrow the fields of Xǔ.
A2.1.3 Summer, fourth month, Dīngwèi,
the Duke and the Earl of Zhèng made a covenant at Yuè.
A2.1.4 Autumn,
great flood.
A2.1.5 Winter, tenth month.
B2.1 "The Commentary, Duke Huán Year 1"
B2.1.1 First year, spring,
the Duke ascended the throne,
and repaired good relations with Zhèng.
The people of Zhèng requested to restore the sacrifices to the Duke of Zhōu,
finally exchanging the Bēng fields.
The Duke agreed.
Third month,
the Earl of Zhèng used a jade disc to borrow the fields of Xǔ,
for the sake of the Duke of Zhōu,
and the Bēng fields.
B2.1.2 Summer, fourth month, Dīngwèi,
the Duke and the Earl of Zhèng made a covenant at Yuè,
to conclude the Bēng agreement.
The covenant said:
"If the covenant is violated,
may they not enjoy the state!"
B2.1.3 Autumn,
great flood.
In general, when the plains produce water, it is called a great flood.
B2.1.4 Winter,
the Earl of Zhèng came to acknowledge the covenant.
B2.1.5 Huáfǔ Dū of Sòng saw the wife of Kǒngfǔ on the road,
followed her with his eyes as she came and went,
and said:
"Beautiful and radiant."
A2.2 "The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Huán Year 2"
A2.2.1 Second year, spring,
the royal first month, Wùshēn,
Dū of Sòng assassinated his ruler Yǔyí and his minister Kǒngfǔ.
A2.2.2 The Viscount of Téng came for an audience.
A2.2.3 Third month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí,
the Marquis of Chén,
and the Earl of Zhèng at Jì,
to settle the disorder in Sòng.
A2.2.4 Summer, fourth month,
took the great tripod of Gào from Sòng.
On Wùshēn,
placed it in the Grand Temple.
A2.2.5 Autumn, seventh month,
the Marquis of Qǐ came for an audience.
A2.2.6 The Marquis of Cài
and the Earl of Zhèng met at Dèng.
A2.2.7 Ninth month,
entered Qǐ.
A2.2.8 The Duke and the Róng made a covenant at Táng.
A2.2.9 Winter,
the Duke arrived from Táng.
B2.2 "The Commentary, Duke Huán Year 2"
B2.2.1 Second year, spring,
Dū of Sòng attacked the Kǒng clan,
killed Kǒngfǔ and took his wife.
The Duke was angry,
Dū became afraid,
and then assassinated Duke Shāng.
The nobleman considered Dū as having a mind without a ruler,
and then moved to evil,
therefore it was first recorded that he assassinated his ruler.
They met at Jì,
to settle the disorder in Sòng,
for the sake of bribes,
and to establish the Huá clan.
When Duke Shāng of Sòng was established,
in ten years there were eleven wars,
and the people could not bear the commands.
Kǒngfǔ Jiā was the Minister of War,
Dū was the Grand Steward,
so taking advantage of the people's inability to bear the commands,
he first declared:
"The Minister of War is like this."
After killing Kǒngfǔ and assassinating Duke Shāng,
he summoned Duke Zhuāng from Zhèng
and established him,
to be close to Zhèng.
He bribed the Duke with the great tripod of Gào,
Qí, Chén,
and Zhèng all had bribes,
so he then became minister to the Duke of Sòng.
B2.2.2 Summer, fourth month,
took the great tripod of Gào from Sòng.
On Wùshēn,
placed it in the Grand Temple,
which was contrary to ritual.
Zāng Āibó remonstrated, saying:
"A ruler of men
should make virtue manifest and block transgressions,
to illuminate the hundred officials,
and still fear there may be loss,
therefore he makes clear fine virtue
to show to his descendants:
Thus, the Pure Temple has a thatched roof,
the great carriage has rush mats,
the grand soup is not fully seasoned,
the millet food is not finely polished,
to manifest frugality.
The dragon robe, crown, knee cover, and scepter,
the belt, lower garment, leg bindings, and shoes,
the cap crosspiece, earplugs, chin strap, and cap covering,
manifest the measures.
The tassels, bands, dagger-ornaments,
scabbard-tips, girdle pendants, banners, and horse-trappings
display their prescribed numbers.
The fire and dragon symbols,
the axe and bow patterns,
display their prescribed emblems.
The five colors arranged in their proper forms
display their prescribed appearances.
The bells on the horse's brow, the bells on the yoke, the bells on the carriage, and the bells on the banner
display their prescribed sounds.
The banners bearing the sun, moon, and stars
display their prescribed brilliance.
Now virtue,
tempered by frugality and regulated by measure,
with gradations and fixed numbers,
is marked by emblems and appearances,
and manifested by sounds and brilliance,
in order to oversee and illuminate the hundred officials.
The hundred officials, thereupon, are warned and awed,
and dare not neglect the rules and regulations.
Now, you have cast aside virtue
and established what is contrary,
and placed this bribe-vessel in the Grand Temple,
to clearly show it to the hundred officials.
If the hundred officials take this as their model,
what then can be punished?
The ruin of a state
arises from the corruption of its officials.
The loss of virtue by officials
occurs when favor and bribery become conspicuous.
If the Gào tripod is placed in the temple,
what could be more conspicuous than this?
When King Wǔ conquered the Shāng,
he moved the Nine Tripods to Luòyì.
Even righteous men still criticized him for this;
how much more so when you are about to display in the Grand Temple a bribe-vessel that proclaims what is contrary and disorderly?
What is to be done about this?"
The Duke did not listen.
The Zhōu court historian heard of this
and said:
"Zāng Sūndá will surely have descendants who flourish in Lǔ!
When his lord acted contrary,
he did not forget to admonish him with virtue."
B2.2.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
the Marquis of Qǐ came to court,
but was disrespectful.
After the Marquis of Qǐ returned home,
(the Duke) then planned to attack him.
B2.2.4 The Marquis of Cài
and the Earl of Zhèng met at Dèng,
beginning to fear Chǔ.
B2.2.5 In the ninth month,
(Lǔ) invaded Qǐ,
to punish its disrespect.
B2.2.6 The Duke and the Róng made a covenant at Táng,
renewing the former friendship.
B2.2.7 In winter,
the Duke arrived from Táng,
and reported (the event) at the ancestral temple.
Whenever the Duke went on a journey,
he reported it at the ancestral temple;
when he returned from a journey,
there was the drinking ceremony upon return, the setting down of cups, and the recording of merits—
this was according to ritual.
When two rulers met alone,
the record of their going and coming mentioned the place—
this indicates they yielded precedence to each other.
When three or more met,
then the record of the going mentioned the place,
and the record of the coming mentioned the meeting—
this indicates the business was concluded.
B2.2.8 Formerly,
when the wife of Duke Mù of Jìn, Lady Jiāng,
gave birth to the heir apparent during the campaign at Tiáo,
he was named Chóu ("Enemy").
His younger brother was born during the battle of Qiānmǔ,
and was named Chéngshī ("Complete Army").
Shī Fú said:
"How strange
is the way our ruler names his sons!
Now, names are for defining appropriateness,
appropriateness gives rise to ritual,
ritual embodies governance,
governance is for rectifying the people.
Thus, when governance is accomplished, the people obey.
To deviate from this gives rise to disorder.
A harmonious match is called 'consort,'
an antagonistic match is called 'enemy'—
this is the ancient rule.
Now, our ruler has named the heir apparent 'Enemy'
and his younger brother 'Complete Army.'
This is the beginning of portents of disorder.
The elder brother will likely be supplanted!"
In the 24th year of Duke Huí (of Lǔ),
disorder first arose in Jìn.
Therefore, Huán Shú was enfeoffed at Qūwò.
Luán Bīn, a grandson of Duke Jìng, served as his tutor.
Shī Fú said:
"I have heard that when a state is established,
if the root is large and the branches are small,
then it can be secure.
Therefore, the Son of Heaven establishes states,
the feudal lords establish families,
the high ministers establish collateral branches,
the great officers have secondary clans,
the officers have subordinate sons and younger brothers,
and the commoners, artisans, and merchants
each have their graded kinship relations,
all with degrees of distinction.
Thus, the people serve their superiors,
and those below have no presumptuous ambitions.
Now Jìn
is a marquis within the royal domain,
yet it establishes a state (within itself).
Since the root is already weak,
can it last long?"
In the 30th year of Duke Huí,
Pān Fǔ of Jìn assassinated Marquis Zhāo
and set up Huán Shú (in his place),
but did not succeed.
The people of Jìn established Marquis Xiào.
In the 45th year of Duke Huí,
Zhuāng Bó of Qūwò attacked Yì,
and assassinated Marquis Xiào.
The people of Yì established his younger brother as Marquis È.
Marquis È begot Marquis Āi.
Marquis Āi encroached upon the fields of Xíngtíng.
The southern border of Xíngtíng opened the way for Qūwò to attack Yì.
A2.3 The Text of Duke Huán's Third Year
A2.3.1 In the third year, in spring, in the first month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Yíng.
A2.3.2 In summer,
the Marquis of Qí
and the Marquis of Wèi made a verbal agreement at Pú.
A2.3.3 In the sixth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qǐ at Chéng.
A2.3.4 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day (rényín),
there was an eclipse of the sun,
which was total.
A2.3.5 The nobleman Huī went to Qí to meet the bride.
A2.3.6 In the ninth month,
the Marquis of Qí escorted Lady Jiāng to Huān.
A2.3.7 The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Huān.
A2.3.8 The lady, Lady Jiāng, arrived from Qí.
A2.3.9 In winter,
the Marquis of Qí sent his younger brother Nián on a courtesy visit.
A2.3.10 There was a plentiful harvest.
B2.3 The Commentary of Duke Huán's Third Year
B2.3.1 In the third year, in spring,
Wǔ Gōng of Qūwò attacked Yì,
and encamped at Xíngtíng.
Hán Wàn drove the war chariot,
and Liáng Hóng served as the right-hand guard.
They pursued the Marquis of Yì to the lowlands of the Fén River.
His team became entangled and stopped.
He was captured at night,
along with Luán Gòngshū.
B2.3.2 (The Duke) met at Yíng
to conclude the marriage alliance with Qí.
B2.3.3 In summer,
the Marquis of Qí
and the Marquis of Wèi made a verbal agreement at Pú—
they did not make a blood covenant.
B2.3.4 The Duke met with the Marquis of Qǐ at Chéng,
because Qǐ sought peace.
B2.3.5 In autumn,
the nobleman Huī went to Qí to meet the bride.
As he was renewing the friendship of the former rulers,
he is therefore called
"the nobleman."
B2.3.6 The Marquis of Qí escorted Lady Jiāng to Huān—
this was contrary to ritual.
Whenever a duke's daughter
married into a state of equal rank,
if she was a sister (of the duke),
then a high minister escorted her,
to show respect to the former rulers;
if she was a daughter,
then a lower minister escorted her.
For a marriage into a great state,
even if she was a daughter,
a high minister also escorted her.
For a marriage to the Son of Heaven,
then all the ministers went,
but the duke did not escort her in person.
For a marriage into a small state,
then a senior great officer escorted her.
B2.3.7 In winter,
Zhòng Nián of Qí came on a friendly mission,
to present gifts to the lady (the wife of Duke Zhuāng of Lǔ).
B2.3.8 The mother of Ruì Bó Wàn, Ruì Jiāng, disliked Ruì Bó's having many favorites,
so she drove him out,
and he went out and dwelt in Wèi.
A2.4 The Text of Duke Huán's Fourth Year
A2.4.1 In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month,
the duke hunted at Láng.
A2.4.2 In summer,
the king by Heaven's grace sent his chief minister, Qú Bó Jiū, on a friendly mission.
B2.4 The Commentary on Duke Huán's Fourth Year
B2.4.1 In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month,
the duke hunted at Láng.
The record
is according to the season,
which is according to rule.
B2.4.2 In summer,
the chief minister of Zhōu, Qú Bó Jiū, came on a friendly mission.
His father being alive,
therefore his name is given.
B2.4.3 In autumn,
an army of Qín made an incursion into Ruì,
but was defeated there,
because it despised the enemy.
B2.4.4 In winter,
an army of the king and
an army of Qín laid siege to Wèi,
and made prisoner Ruì Bó, carrying him back with them.
A2.5 The Text of Duke Huán's Fifth Year
A2.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring, in the first month, on
Jiǎxū and
Jǐchǒu,
the marquis of Chén, Bào, died.
A2.5.2 In summer,
the marquis of Qí and
the earl of Zhèng went to Jǐ.
A2.5.3 The king by Heaven's grace sent the son of Réng Shū on a friendly mission.
A2.5.4 There was the burial of Duke Huán of Chén.
A2.5.5 The walls of Zhùqiū were repaired.
A2.5.6 In autumn,
men of Cài,
men of Wèi, and
men of Chén followed the king in an invasion of Zhèng.
A2.5.7 There was the great sacrifice for rain.
A2.5.8 There were locusts.
A2.5.9 In winter,
the duke of Zhōu went to Cáo.
B2.5 The Commentary on Duke Huán's Fifth Year
B2.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring, in the first month, on
Jiǎxū and
Jǐchǒu,
the marquis of Chén, Bào, died.
There were two announcements of his death.
At this time there was disorder in Chén,
and Wén's son, Tuó, killed the heir-son Miǎn
and took his place.
The marquis was dangerously ill when the disorder broke out,
and the people of the State were dispersed,
and therefore there were two announcements.
B2.5.2 In summer,
the marquis of Qí and
the earl of Zhèng paid a court-visit to Jǐ,
wishing to make a surprise attack on it.
The people of Jǐ knew of it.
B2.5.3 The king deprived the earl of Zhèng of his share in the government,
and the earl of Zhèng did not go to court.
In autumn,
the king, with the princes, invaded Zhèng,
and the earl of Zhèng resisted him.
The king commanded the center army;
Guó Gōng Línfǔ commanded the right army,
to which the men of Cài and
Wèi were attached;
Zhōu Gōng Hēijiān commanded the left army,
to which the men of Chén were attached.
Zǐ Yuán of Zhèng requested to form a left square,
to oppose the men of Cài and
Wèi;
and a right square,
to oppose the men of Chén,
saying:
"In Chén there is disorder,
and the people have no heart to fight.
If we first attack them,
they are sure to flee.
The king's troops will look to them,
and will be thrown into confusion.
The troops of Cài and Wèi cannot sustain an attack,
and will certainly be the first to flee.
We can then concentrate our forces on the king's troops,
and we shall succeed."
The earl followed this advice.
Màn Bó commanded the right square,
Zhài Zhòngzú the left square,
Yuán Fán and
Gāo Qúmí, with the center army, supported the earl,
forming the 'fish-trap' array,
with the chariots in front and the footmen behind them,
the footmen filling up the intervals between the chariots.
The battle took place at Xūgě.
The earl gave orders to the two squares, saying:
"When you see the flag move, then beat the drums!"
The troops of Cài, Wèi, and
Chén all fled,
the king's troops were thrown into confusion,
and the army of Zhèng closed upon and attacked them,
so that the king's troops were greatly defeated.
Zhù Dān shot the king and hit him on the shoulder,
and the king was unable to maintain his army.
Zhù Dān requested to pursue him,
but the earl said:
"A superior man does not wish to be above others,
how much less would he dare to insult the son of Heaven? If
we have only saved ourselves,
and the altars are not overthrown,
that is enough."
At night,
the earl of Zhèng sent Zhài Zú to condole with the king,
and to inquire after his officers.
B2.5.4 The son of Réng Shū
was young.
B2.5.5 In autumn,
there was the great sacrifice for rain.
The record
is because it was not at the proper time.
In all sacrifices,
that in the suburbs should be when the insects begin to stir;
that for rain when the dragon stars appear;
that of尝 when the killing time begins;
and that of 烝 when the insects are dormant.
When these sacrifices are performed out of season, they are recorded.
B2.5.6 In winter,
the duke of Chúnyú went to Cáo.
Considering that his State was in danger,
he did not return.
A2.6 The Text of Duke Huán's Sixth Year
A2.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring, in the first month,
he actually came.
A2.6.2 In summer, in the fourth month,
the duke had a meeting with the marquis of Jǐ at Chéng.
A2.6.3 In autumn, in the eighth month, on Rénwǔ,
there was a great review of the chariots.
A2.6.4 The men of Cài killed Chén Tuó.
A2.6.5 In the ninth month, on Dīngmǎo,
Zǐ Tóng was born.
A2.6.6 In winter,
the marquis of Jǐ came to Lǔ on a court-visit.
B2.6 The Commentary on Duke Huán's Sixth Year
B2.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring,
(the duke of Zhōu) came from Cáo to Lǔ on a court-visit.
The record says
"he actually came,"
because he did not return to his State.
B2.6.2 King Wǔ of Chǔ invaded Suí,
and sent Wěi Zhāng to seek peace,
halting his army at Xiá to wait the issue.
The people of Suí sent a junior tutor to manage the negotiations.
Dòu Bóbǐ said to the viscount of Chǔ:
"We have not been able to accomplish our wishes east of the Hàn,
and we ourselves have made it so.
We have displayed our three armies,
and put on our mail and arms,
and by force of arms have overawed them,
so that they are afraid and combine to scheme against us,
and therefore it is difficult to separate them.
Among the States east of the Hàn,
Suí is the greatest.
If Suí grows proud,
it is sure to cast off the smaller States.
If the smaller States separate from it,
it will be for the advantage of Chǔ.
The junior tutor is arrogant;
I beg you to weaken your army, so as to make him more so."
Xióng Lǜjūbǐ said:
"With Jì Liáng in Suí,
what good will it do?"
Dòu Bóbǐ said:
"We should plan for the future,
for the Junior Tutor has gained his lord's favor."
The King of Chǔ then disbanded his army
and welcomed the Junior Tutor.
The Junior Tutor returned
and requested to pursue the Chǔ army.
The Marquis of Suí was about to agree.
Jì Liáng stopped him,
saying:
"Heaven is now favoring Chǔ.
Chǔ's apparent weakness
is a trick to lure us.
Why is Your Lordship in such a hurry?
I have heard that the small can withstand the great
when the small follows the Way
and the great is depraved.
What is called the Way
is being loyal to the people
and faithful to the spirits.
The ruler thinks of benefiting the people—
that is loyalty;
the invocators and scribes use honest words—
that is faithfulness.
Now the people are starving
while you, my lord, indulge your desires;
the invocators and scribes offer false praises in sacrifice—
I do not see how this can succeed."
The lord said:
"My sacrificial animals are plump and flawless,
the grain offerings are abundant and complete—
why would this not be faithful?"
He replied:
"The people
are the masters of the spirits.
Therefore, the sage kings first attended to the people
and only then devoted effort to the spirits.
Thus, when presenting the animals, they would announce:
'Broad, large, fat, and flawless'—
meaning that the people's strength is universally preserved,
meaning that their livestock are large and flourishing,
meaning that they are free from disease and pestilence,
meaning that they are fully provided for and all are present;
when presenting the grain offerings, they would announce:
'Pure grain, abundant offerings'—
meaning that the three farming seasons are unharmed
and the people are harmonious and the harvest plentiful;
when presenting the sweet wine, they would announce:
'Excellent, sincere, and fine wine'—
meaning that both high and low possess fine virtue
and have no rebellious hearts.
What is called fragrance
is the absence of slander and wickedness.
Therefore, they focused on the three farming seasons,
cultivated the five teachings,
drew close to the nine clans,
and only then performed the solemn sacrifices.
Thus, the people were harmonious
and the spirits bestowed blessings upon them,
so every action met with success.
Now the people each have their own minds,
and the spirits lack masters;
even if you, my lord, alone have abundance,
what blessings can there be!
You, my lord, should first improve governance
and draw close to fraternal states,
so as to perhaps avoid calamity."
The Marquis of Suí, alarmed, improved his governance,
and Chǔ did not dare attack.
B2.6.3 In summer,
a meeting was held at Chéng,
because Jì came to consult about the difficulties with Qí.
B2.6.4 The Northern Róng attacked Qí.
The Marquis of Qí sent to Zhèng to request troops.
Zhèng's crown prince Hū led troops to rescue Qí.
In the sixth month,
they greatly defeated the Róng army,
capturing its two commanders, Dàliáng
and Shǎoliáng,
and three hundred armored heads,
which they presented to Qí.
At that time, the great officers of the various states were garrisoning Qí.
The people of Qí provided them with provisions,
and had Lǔ arrange their order of precedence.
Zhèng was placed last.
Zhèng Hū, because he had rendered meritorious service,
was angry,
hence the later campaign at Láng.
Before the Duke had married into Qí,
the Marquis of Qí wished to give Wén Jiāng in marriage to Zhèng's crown prince Hū.
Crown prince Hū declined.
People asked him the reason.
The crown prince said:
"Each person has his own match.
Qí is great,
and is not my match.
The Odes say:
'Seek much blessing for yourself.'
It depends on myself alone—
what has a great state to do with it?"
The gentleman says:
"He was good at planning for himself."
When he had defeated the Róng army,
the Marquis of Qí again requested to give him a wife.
He firmly declined.
People asked him the reason.
The crown prince said:
"When I had no dealings with Qí,
I still did not dare.
Now, having rushed to Qí's aid on my lord's orders,
and to take a wife home with me—
that would be to use the army for marriage.
What would the people say of me?"
He then declined through Zhèng Bó.
B2.6.5 In autumn,
a grand review was held,
to inspect the chariots and horses.
B2.6.6 On Dīngmǎo of the ninth month,
Zǐ Tóng was born.
They performed the rites for the birth of a crown prince:
he was received with a grand sacrifice,
a divined officer carried him,
the officer's wife suckled him,
and the Duke, together with Wén Jiāng
and the wives of the ducal house, named him.
The Duke asked Shēn Xū about naming.
He replied:
"There are five kinds of names:
those based on trust,
those based on righteousness,
those based on resemblance,
those based on borrowing,
and those based on classification.
To name based on birth circumstances is trust;
to name based on virtue is righteousness;
to name based on resemblance
is image;
to borrow from objects is borrowing;
to take from the father
is classification.
Do not use a state name,
do not use an official title,
do not use mountains or rivers,
do not use hidden ailments,
do not use domestic animals,
do not use vessels or ceremonial silks.
The Zhōu people serve the spirits with avoidance of taboo names.
A name
will eventually become taboo.
Therefore, using a state name would abolish the name,
using an official title would abolish the office,
using mountains or rivers would abolish their sacrifices,
using domestic animals would abolish their sacrifices,
using vessels or ceremonial silks would abolish the rites.
Jìn abolished the office of Sītú because of Marquis Xī;
Sòng abolished the office of Sīkōng because of Duke Wǔ;
our former lords Xiàn
and Wǔ
abolished two mountains;
therefore, great things
should not be used for names."
The Duke said:
"This child was born
on the same day as I.
Name him Tóng."
B2.6.7 In winter,
the Marquis of Jì came to court,
requesting a royal command to seek peace with Qí.
The Duke informed him he could not.
A2.7 The Classic of Duke Huán, Year Seven
A2.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year, in the second month, on Jǐhài,
they burned Xiánqiū.
A2.7.2 In summer,
Gǔ Bó Suí came to court.
Dèng Hóu Wúlí came to court.
B2.7 The Commentary of Duke Huán, Year Seven
B2.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
Gǔ Bó and
Dèng Hóu came to court.
Recording their names
shows contempt for them.
B2.7.2 In summer,
Méng and Xiàng sought peace with Zhèng,
but later broke it.
B2.7.3 In autumn,
men of Zhèng, Qí, and Wèi
attacked Méng and Xiàng.
The King moved the people of Méng and Xiàng to Jiá.
B2.7.4 In winter,
the Earl of Qūwò enticed Jìn's young lord Hóu
and killed him.
A2.8 The Classic of Duke Huán, Year Eight
A2.8.1 In the eighth year, spring, the first month, on the Jǐmǎo day,
the winter sacrifice was held.
A2.8.2 The Heavenly King sent Jiāfù to pay a courtesy visit.
A2.8.3 In summer, the fifth month, on the Dīngchǒu day,
the winter sacrifice was held.
A2.8.4 In autumn,
they attacked Zhū.
A2.8.5 In winter, the tenth month,
it snowed.
A2.8.6 Duke Zhài came,
and then went to Jì to welcome the queen for the king.
B2.8 The Commentary of the Eighth Year of Duke Huán
B2.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
Yì was destroyed.
B2.8.2 The Junior Tutor of Suí was favored.
Dòu Bóbǐ of Chǔ said:
"The time is right.
The enemy has a flaw,
we must not miss this opportunity."
In summer,
the Viscount of Chǔ assembled the feudal lords at Shěnlù.
Huáng and Suí did not attend.
He sent Wěi Zhāng to reprimand Huáng.
The Viscount of Chǔ attacked Suí.
He stationed his army between the Hàn
and Huái rivers.
Jì Liáng requested to submit to them:
"If they do not agree and then we fight,
it will anger our troops and make the enemy lax."
The Junior Tutor said to the Marquis of Suí:
"We must fight quickly.
Otherwise,
we will miss the Chǔ army."
The Marquis of Suí went out to meet them.
Observing the Chǔ army,
Jì Liáng said:
"The Chǔ people honor the left,
so you, my lord, must take the left,
and avoid encountering the king.
Moreover, attack their right.
The right has no good commanders,
so it will surely be defeated.
If one wing is defeated,
the masses will scatter."
The Junior Tutor said:
"If we do not face the king,
it is not a proper battle."
They did not follow Jì Liáng's advice.
They fought at Sùqǐ.
The Suí army was defeated.
The Marquis of Suí escaped.
Dòu Dān captured his war chariot
and his chariot warrior, the Junior Tutor.
In autumn,
Suí made peace with Chǔ.
The Viscount of Chǔ was about to refuse.
Dòu Bóbǐ said:
"Heaven has removed their trouble,
so Suí cannot be conquered."
So they made a covenant and returned.
B2.8.3 In winter,
the king commanded Guó Zhòng to establish Mín, the younger brother of Marquis Āi of Jìn, in Jìn.
B2.8.4 Duke Zhài came,
and then went to Jì to welcome the queen for the king,
which was according to ritual.
A2.9 The Spring and Autumn Annals of the Ninth Year of Duke Huán
A2.9.1 In the ninth year, spring,
Jì Jìjiāng returned to the capital.
A2.9.2 In summer, the fourth month.
A2.9.3 In autumn, the seventh month.
A2.9.4 In winter,
the Earl of Cáo sent his heir apparent, Shègū, to pay a court visit.
B2.9 The Commentary of the Ninth Year of Duke Huán
B2.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
Jì Jìjiāng returned to the capital.
When daughters of feudal lords leave to marry,
only the queen is recorded.
B2.9.2 The Viscount of Bā sent Hán Fú to inform Chǔ,
requesting to establish friendly relations with Dèng.
The Viscount of Chǔ sent Dào Shuò to escort the Bā envoy
on a courtesy visit to Dèng.
The people of Yōu, on the southern border of Dèng, attacked
and seized their gifts,
killing Dào Shuò and the Bā envoy.
The Viscount of Chǔ sent Wěi Zhāng to reprimand Dèng.
The people of Dèng did not accept the reprimand.
In summer,
Chǔ sent Dòu Lián to lead troops and, together with the Bā army, besiege Yōu.
Dèng's Yǎngshēng
and Dānshēng led troops to rescue Yōu.
They three times drove back the Bā army,
but could not overcome them.
Dòu Lián arranged his troops in a horizontal formation within the Bā army
to engage in battle,
and then feigned retreat.
The Dèng troops pursued them,
turning their backs to the Bā army;
and were attacked from both sides.
The Dèng army was greatly defeated.
The people of Yōu fled under cover of night.
B2.9.3 In autumn,
Guó Zhòng, Ruì Bó, Liáng Bó, Xún Hóu, and Jiǎ Bó attacked Qūwò.
B2.9.4 In winter,
the heir apparent of Cáo came to pay a court visit.
He was treated as a high minister,
which was according to ritual.
They feasted the heir apparent of Cáo.
At the first offering,
music was played, and he sighed.
Shīfù said:
"The heir apparent of Cáo must have worries!
This is not the place to sigh."
A2.10 The Spring and Autumn Annals of the Tenth Year of Duke Huán
A2.10.1 In the tenth year, spring,
the king's first month, on the Gēngshēn day,
the Earl of Cáo, Zhōngshēng, died.
A2.10.2 In summer, the fifth month,
Duke Huán of Cáo was buried.
A2.10.3 In autumn,
the duke was to meet the Marquis of Wèi at Táoqiū,
but they did not meet.
A2.10.4 In winter, the twelfth month, on the Bǐngwǔ day,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Earl of Zhèng came to fight at Láng.
B2.10 The Commentary of the Tenth Year of Duke Huán
B2.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year,
Duke Huán of Cáo died.
B2.10.2 Guó Zhòng slandered his grandee Zhān Fǔ to the king.
Zhān Fǔ had a justification,
and with the king's army attacked Guó.
In summer,
the Duke of Guó fled to Yú.
B2.10.3 In autumn,
the people of Qín reinstated Ruì Bó Wàn in Ruì.
B2.10.4 Earlier,
Yú Shū had a piece of jade,
and the Duke of Yú requested it.
He did not present it.
Later he regretted this,
saying:
"There is a Zhōu proverb:
'A common man is innocent,
but harboring a jade makes him guilty.'
Why should I keep this,
only to buy myself trouble?"
So he presented it.
The duke again requested his precious sword.
Yú Shū said:
"This is insatiable.
Insatiability
will bring disaster upon me."
So he attacked the Duke of Yú.
Therefore, the Duke of Yú fled to Gòngchí.
B2.10.5 In winter,
Qí, Wèi,
and Zhèng came to fight at Láng,
because we had a justification.
Earlier,
the Northern Róng troubled Qí,
and the feudal lords rescued them.
Zhèng's Gōngzǐ Hū had merit in this.
The people of Qí supplied provisions to the feudal lords,
and had Lǔ arrange the order.
Lǔ placed Zhèng last according to the Zhōu ranking.
The people of Zhèng were angry,
and requested troops from Qí.
The people of Qí used Wèi troops to assist them,
therefore it is not called an invasion.
Qí and Wèi are written first,
according to the king's ranking.
A2.11 The Spring and Autumn Annals of the Eleventh Year of Duke Huán
A2.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring, the first month,
the people of Qí,
the people of Wèi,
and the people of Zhèng made a covenant at Ècáo.
A2.11.2 In summer, the fifth month, on the Guǐwèi day,
the Earl of Zhèng, Wùshēng, died.
A2.11.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng was buried.
A2.11.4 In the ninth month,
a man of Sòng seized Zhòng of Zhèng.
Tū returned to Zhèng.
Hū of Zhèng fled and went to Wèi.
A2.11.5 Róu met with the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
and Shū of Cài and made a covenant at Zhé.
A2.11.6 The Duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Fūzhōng.
A2.11.7 In winter, in the twelfth month,
the Duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Kàn.
B2.11 The Commentary of Duke Huán's Eleventh Year
B2.11.1 In the spring of the eleventh year,
Qí, Wèi,
Zhèng, and Sòng made a covenant at Ècáo.
B2.11.2 Qūxiá of Chǔ was about to make a covenant with Èr and Zhěn.
The people of Yún had their army at Púsāo,
intending to join Suí, Jiǎo, Zhōu, and Liǎo in attacking the army of Chǔ.
The Mò'áo was troubled by this.
Dòu Lián said:
"The people of Yún have stationed their army in their suburbs,
and will certainly not be on guard.
Moreover, they daily anticipate the arrival of the four cities.
You, my lord, should take up position at Jiāoyǐng,
to resist the four cities,
while I lead crack troops to attack Yún by night.
The people of Yún are apprehensive
and rely on their city walls,
so they will have no will to fight.
If we defeat the army of Yún,
the four cities are sure to disperse."
The Mò'áo said:
"Why not request reinforcements from the king?"
He replied:
"An army's victory lies in harmony,
not in numbers.
That Shāng and Zhōu were not matched,
you, my lord, have heard of.
Once the army is formed and sets out,
what need is there for reinforcements?"
The Mò'áo said:
"Should we divine?"
He replied:
"Divination is used to resolve doubts.
Where there is no doubt,
why divine?"
Thereupon they defeated the army of Yún at Púsāo,
and finally made the covenant and returned.
B2.11.3 When Duke Zhāo of Zhèng had defeated the Northern Róng,
the people of Qí wanted to give him a wife.
Duke Zhāo declined.
Zhòng of Zhèng said:
"You must take her.
Our ruler has many favored ladies within,
and you, his son, have no powerful external support,
so you will not be established.
The three princes are all potential rulers."
He did not listen.
In summer,
Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng died.
Formerly,
Zhòng Zú, the border warden of Zhài,
had been favored by Duke Zhuāng,
who made him a minister.
He arranged for the duke to marry Dèng Màn,
who gave birth to Duke Zhāo.
Therefore, Zhòng of Zhèng established him.
The Yōng clan of Sòng gave a daughter to Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng,
named Yōng Jí,
who gave birth to Duke Lì.
The Yōng clan was influential
and favored by Duke Zhuāng of Sòng,
so they lured Zhòng of Zhèng and seized him,
saying:
"If you do not establish Tū,
you will die."
They also seized Duke Lì
and demanded bribes.
Zhòng of Zhèng made a covenant with the men of Sòng,
and returned with Duke Lì and established him.
In autumn, on the dīnghài day of the ninth month,
Duke Zhāo fled to Wèi.
On the jǐhài day,
Duke Lì was established.
A2.12 The Spring and Autumn Annals of Duke Huán's Twelfth Year
A2.12.1 In the spring of the twelfth year, in the first month.
A2.12.2 In summer, on the rényín day of the sixth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qǐ
and the Viscount of Jǔ and made a covenant at Qūchí.
A2.12.3 In autumn, on the dīnghài day of the seventh month,
the Duke met with the Duke of Sòng
and a man of Yān and made a covenant at Gǔqiū.
A2.12.4 In the eighth month, on the rénchén day,
the Marquis Yuè of Chén died.
A2.12.5 The Duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Xū.
A2.12.6 In winter, in the eleventh month,
the Duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Guī.
