A2.12.7 On the bǐngxū day,
the Duke met with the Earl of Zhèng,
and made a covenant at Wǔfǔ.
A2.12.8 On the bǐngxū day,
the Marquis Jìn of Wèi died.
A2.12.9 In the twelfth month,
[our army] joined with the army of Zhèng to attack Sòng.
On the dīngwèi day,
they fought at Sòng.
B2.12 The Commentary of Duke Huán's Twelfth Year
B2.12.1 In the summer of the twelfth year,
the covenant at Qūchí
was to make peace between Qǐ
and Jǔ.
B2.12.2 The Duke wanted to make peace between Sòng and Zhèng.
In autumn,
the Duke and the Duke of Sòng made a covenant at Gōudòu Hill.
It was not yet known whether Sòng would come to terms,
so they met again at Xū.
In winter,
they met again at Guī.
The Duke of Sòng declined to make peace,
so [the Duke] made a covenant with the Earl of Zhèng at Wǔfǔ,
and then led an army to attack Sòng,
and fought there,
because Sòng was untrustworthy.
A gentleman said:
"If good faith is not maintained,
covenants are of no benefit.
The Book of Songs says:
'When gentlemen frequently make covenants,
disorder is thereby prolonged.'
This is because of lack of good faith."
B2.12.3 Chǔ attacked Jiǎo,
and stationed its army at its southern gate.
The Mò'áo Qūxiá said:
"Jiǎo is small and frivolous;
being frivolous, it lacks strategy.
I request that we do not guard our woodcutters, to lure them out."
This was followed.
The men of Jiǎo captured thirty men.
The next day,
the men of Jiǎo competed to come out,
driving the Chu laborers into the mountains.
The men of Chǔ sat at their northern gate,
and set an ambush below the mountain.
They greatly defeated them.
They made a covenant under the city walls and returned.
B2.12.4 During the campaign against Jiǎo,
the army of Chǔ forded the Péng River in separate groups.
The men of Luó wanted to attack them.
They sent Bó Jiā to spy on them.
He made three circuits and counted them.
A2.13 The Spring and Autumn Annals of Duke Huán's Thirteenth Year
A2.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year, in the second month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jì
and the Earl of Zhèng.
On the jǐsì day,
[they] joined with the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and a man of Yān in battle.
The armies of Qí,
Sòng,
Wèi,
and Yān were defeated.
A2.13.2 In the third month,
Duke Xuān of Wèi was buried.
A2.13.3 In summer,
there was a great flood.
A2.13.4 In autumn, in the seventh month.
A2.13.5 In winter, in the tenth month.
B2.13 The Commentary of Duke Huán's Thirteenth Year
B2.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
Chǔ's Qū Xiá attacked Luó.
Dòu Bóbǐ saw him off.
Upon returning,
he said to his charioteer:
"The Mò'áo is certain to be defeated.
He lifts his feet high,
his mind is not steadfast."
Then he went to see the ruler of Chǔ,
and said:
"You must reinforce the army!"
The ruler of Chǔ declined.
He went in and told his consort, Dèng Màn.
Dèng Màn said:
"The great officer is not speaking of numbers of men.
He means that you should pacify the common people with good faith,
instruct the various officers with virtue,
and awe the Mò'áo with punishments.
The Mò'áo is complacent from the victory at Pú Sāo,
and will act on his own judgment.
He is certain to underestimate Luó.
If you do not restrain and pacify him,
will he not fail to make preparations?
He surely means that you should instruct the troops
and be good at restraining and pacifying them,
summon the various officers
and encourage them with virtuous commands,
see the Mò'áo
and warn him that Heaven does not grant easy success.
Otherwise,
does he not know that the Chǔ army has marched out in full force?"
The ruler of Chǔ sent a man from Lài to pursue them,
but he did not catch up.
The Mò'áo sent a proclamation through the army, saying:
"Anyone who remonstrates will be punished!"
When they reached Yān,
they crossed in disorderly ranks,
and so had no order.
Moreover, they made no preparations.
When they reached Luó,
Luó and the Lú Róng attacked them with two armies,
and inflicted a great defeat on them.
The Mò'áo hanged himself in Huānggǔ.
The other commanders were imprisoned in Yěfù
to await punishment.
The ruler of Chǔ said:
"This is my crime."
And he pardoned them all.
B2.13.2 Sòng made many demands for bribes from Zhèng.
Zhèng could not endure these demands,
and therefore fought with Jì,
Lǔ, and Qí against Sòng,
Wèi, and Yān.
The record does not state where the battle was fought,
because they arrived late.
B2.13.3 Men of Zhèng came to request the restoration of friendly relations.
A2.14 The Classic of Duke Huán's Fourteenth Year
A2.14.1 In the fourteenth year, in spring, the first month,
the duke met with the earl of Zhèng at Cáo.
A2.14.2 There was no ice.
A2.14.3 In summer, in the fifth month,
the earl of Zhèng sent his younger brother Yǔ to come and covenant.
A2.14.4 In autumn, in the eighth month, on Rénshēn,
the royal granaries were destroyed by fire.
A2.14.5 On Yǐhài,
the autumn sacrifice was offered.
A2.14.6 In winter, in the twelfth month, on Dīngsì,
the marquis of Qí, Lùfù, died.
A2.14.7 Men of Sòng, together with men of Qí,
Cài,
Wèi,
and Chén, attacked Zhèng.
B2.14 The Tradition of Duke Huán's Fourteenth Year
B2.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
they met at Cáo.
The men of Cáo presented provisions,
which was according to ritual.
B2.14.2 In summer,
Zhèng's Zǐrén came to renew the covenant,
and also to confirm the meeting at Cáo.
B2.14.3 In autumn, in the eighth month, on Rénshēn,
the royal granaries were destroyed by fire.
On Yǐhài,
the autumn sacrifice was offered.
It is recorded,
because there was no harm done.
B2.14.4 In winter,
men of Sòng, leading the various lords, attacked Zhèng,
in retaliation for the battle at Sòng.
They burned the Qú Gate.
They entered,
and reached the Great Thoroughfare.
They attacked the eastern suburbs,
and took Niúshǒu.
They took the rafters of the Grand Temple back with them,
to use as rafters for the Lú Gate.
A2.15 The Classic of Duke Huán's Fifteenth Year
A2.15.1 In the fifteenth year, in spring, the second month,
the Son of Heaven sent Jiāfù to come and request chariots.
A2.15.2 In the third month, on Yǐwèi,
the Son of Heaven passed away.
A2.15.3 In summer, in the fourth month, on Jǐsì,
Duke Xī of Qí was buried.
A2.15.4 In the fifth month,
the earl of Zhèng, Tū, fled to Cài.
A2.15.5 The heir of Zhèng, Hū, returned again to Zhèng.
A2.15.6 Shǔ of Xǔ entered Xǔ.
A2.15.7 The duke met with the marquis of Qí at Ài.
A2.15.8 Men of Zhū,
Móu,
and Gé came to court.
A2.15.9 In autumn, in the ninth month,
the earl of Zhèng, Tū, entered Lì.
A2.15.10 In winter, in the eleventh month,
the duke met with the duke of Sòng,
the marquis of Wèi,
and the marquis of Chén at Chǐ,
to attack Zhèng.
B2.15 The Tradition of Duke Huán's Fifteenth Year
B2.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
the Son of Heaven sent Jiāfù to come and request chariots,
which was contrary to ritual.
The feudal lords do not present tribute of chariots
or robes,
and the Son of Heaven does not privately seek wealth.
B2.15.2 Zhài Zhòng was autocratic,
and the earl of Zhèng was troubled by this,
so he sent his son-in-law Yōng Jiū to kill him.
He was about to feast him in the suburbs.
Yōng Jī, his daughter, learned of this,
and said to her mother:
"Which is closer, father or husband?"
Her mother said:
"Any man can be a husband,
but father is only one,
how can they be compared?"
So she informed Zhài Zhòng, saying:
"The Yōng family has left his house
and is about to feast you in the suburbs.
I am suspicious of this,
and so I report it."
Zhài Zhòng killed Yōng Jiū,
and exposed his corpse at the pond of the Zhōu family.
The duke loaded the body in his carriage and went out,
saying:
"To scheme with a woman,
his death was fitting."
In summer,
Duke Lì fled to Cài.
B2.15.3 In the sixth month, on Yǐhài,
Duke Zhāo entered.
B2.15.4 Shǔ of Xǔ entered Xǔ.
B2.15.5 The duke met with the marquis of Qí at Ài,
to plan the settlement of Xǔ.
B2.15.6 In autumn,
the earl of Zhèng, with the help of the men of Lì, killed Tán Bó,
and then took up residence in Lì.
B2.15.7 In winter,
they met at Chǐ,
to plan an attack on Zhèng,
intending to restore Duke Lì.
They were unsuccessful and returned.
A2.16 The Classic of Duke Huán's Sixteenth Year
A2.16.1 In the sixteenth year, in spring, the first month,
the duke met with the duke of Sòng,
the marquis of Cài,
and the marquis of Wèi at Cáo.
A2.16.2 In summer, the fourth month,
the duke met with the duke of Sòng,
the marquis of Wèi,
the marquis of Chén,
and the marquis of Cài to attack Zhèng.
A2.16.3 In autumn, the seventh month,
the duke arrived from the attack on Zhèng.
A2.16.4 In winter,
a wall was built at Xiàng.
A2.16.5 In the eleventh month,
the Marquis of Wèi, Shuò, fled to Qí.
B2.16 Commentary on the Sixteenth Year of Duke Huán
B2.16.1 In the spring of the sixteenth year, in the first month,
a meeting was held at Cáo,
to plan an attack on Zhèng.
B2.16.2 In summer,
they attacked Zhèng.
B2.16.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
the Duke returned from the attack on Zhèng,
and held the "yǐnzhì" ceremony.
B2.16.4 In winter,
a wall was built at Xiàng.
It was recorded
because it was done in the proper season.
B2.16.5 Earlier,
Duke Xuān of Wèi had an illicit relationship with Yí Jiāng,
and she gave birth to Jí Zǐ,
whom he entrusted to the Yòu Gōngzǐ.
He arranged a marriage for him with a woman from Qí,
but she was beautiful,
so the Duke took her for himself.
She gave birth to Shòu and Shuò.
He entrusted Shòu to the Zuǒ Gōngzǐ.
Yí Jiāng hanged herself.
Xuān Jiāng and Gōngzǐ Shuò slandered Jí Zǐ to the Duke.
The Duke sent him on a mission to Qí.
He had bandits wait for him at Shēn,
intending to kill him.
Shòu Zǐ warned him,
urging him to flee.
He refused,
saying:
"To abandon my father's command—
what use is a son then?
Unless there is a land without fathers,
it cannot be done."
When he was about to depart,
Shòu Zǐ plied him with wine.
Shòu Zǐ then took his banner and went ahead,
and the bandits killed him.
When Jí Zǐ arrived,
he said:
"It was I they sought—
what crime had he committed?
Please kill me instead!"
So they killed him too.
Because of this, the two Gōngzǐ harbored resentment against Duke Huì.
In the eleventh month,
Zuǒ Gōngzǐ Xiè
and Yòu Gōngzǐ Zhí installed Gōngzǐ Qiánmóu as ruler.
Duke Huì fled to Qí.
A2.17 The Text of the Seventeenth Year of Duke Huán
A2.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year, in the first month, on the bǐngchén day,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí
and the Marquis of Jǐ, and made a covenant at Huáng.
A2.17.2 In the second month, on the bǐngwǔ day,
the Duke met with Zhū Yífù,
and made a covenant at Cuǐ.
A2.17.3 In the fifth month, on the bǐngwǔ day,
they fought with the army of Qí at Xī.
A2.17.4 In the sixth month, on the dīngchǒu day,
the Marquis of Cài, Fēngrén, died.
A2.17.5 In autumn, in the eighth month,
Cài Jì returned from Chén to Cài.
A2.17.6 On the guǐsì day,
Cài Huánhóu was buried.
A2.17.7 They, together with men of Sòng
and men of Wèi, attacked Zhū.
A2.17.8 In winter, on the first day of the tenth month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
B2.17 Commentary on the Seventeenth Year of Duke Huán
B2.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
they made a covenant at Huáng,
to bring peace between Qí
and Jǐ,
and also to plan regarding Wèi.
B2.17.2 The covenant with Zhū Yífù at Cuǐ
renewed the covenant made at Miè.
B2.17.3 In summer,
the battle with the army of Qí at Xī
was a border incident.
At that time, men of Qí invaded the borders of Lǔ,
and the border officials came to report it.
The Duke said:
"In matters of borders,
carefully guard your own territory,
and prepare for the unexpected.
For now, make all necessary preparations.
When the situation arises, then fight—
what need is there to report further?"
B2.17.4 Cài Huánhóu died.
The people of Cài summoned Cài Jì from Chén.
B2.17.5 In autumn,
Cài Jì returned from Chén to Cài,
because the people of Cài approved of him.
B2.17.6 The attack on Zhū
was at the instigation of Sòng.
B2.17.7 In winter, on the first day of the tenth month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
The day was not recorded
due to an error by the officials.
The Son of Heaven has a Rìguān,
and the feudal lords have Rìyù.
The Rìguān holds a ministerial position to determine the dates—
this is according to ritual.
The Rìyù does not miss the dates,
and announces them to all officials at court.
B2.17.8 Earlier,
the Earl of Zhèng intended to make Gāo Qúmí a minister,
but Duke Zhāo disliked him,
and firmly remonstrated against it,
but he was not heeded.
When Duke Zhāo was established as ruler,
Gāo Qúmí, fearing he would kill him,
on the xīnmǎo day,
assassinated Duke Zhāo,
and installed Gōngzǐ Wěi.
The gentleman says
"Duke Zhāo knew whom to dislike."
Gōngzǐ Dá said:
"Gāo Bó will likely be executed!
His retaliation for being disliked was excessive."
A2.18 The Text of the Eighteenth Year of Duke Huán
A2.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year, in the royal first month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Luò.
The Duke and his wife, Lady Jiāng, then proceeded to Qí.
A2.18.2 In summer, in the fourth month, on the bǐngzǐ day,
the Duke died in Qí.
A2.18.3 On the dīngyǒu day,
the Duke's coffin arrived from Qí.
A2.18.4 In autumn, in the seventh month.
A2.18.5 In winter, in the twelfth month, on the jǐchǒu day,
our ruler, Duke Huán, was buried.
B2.18 Commentary on the Eighteenth Year of Duke Huán
B2.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year,
the Duke was about to travel,
and then went with Lady Jiāng to Qí.
Shēn Xū said:
"Women have their homes,
men have their chambers;
they should not defile each other.
This is called propriety.
To violate this
is sure to bring ruin."
The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Luò,
and then proceeded with Wén Jiāng to Qí.
The Marquis of Qí had an affair with her.
The Duke reproached her.
She reported this.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the bǐngzǐ day,
a feast was held for the Duke.
He had Gōngzǐ Péngshēng assist the Duke into his carriage,
and the Duke died in the carriage.
The people of Lǔ reported to Qí, saying:
"Our ruler, in awe of Your Lordship's majesty,
dared not remain idle at home,
and came to renew our old friendship.
The ceremonies were completed, yet he did not return;
we have no one to blame,
and it brings shame among the feudal lords.
We ask that Péngshēng be used to remove this disgrace."
The men of Qí executed Péngshēng.
B2.18.2 In autumn,
the Marquis of Qí stationed his army at Shǒuzhǐ;
Zǐ Wěi went to meet him,
with Gāo Qúmí as his assistant.
In the seventh month, on the wùxū day,
the men of Qí killed Zǐ Wěi,
and had Gāo Qúmí torn apart by chariots.
Zhòng Zhòng welcomed the Zhèng heir from Chén
and established him.
Regarding this journey,
Zhòng Zhòng knew about it,
so he claimed illness and did not go.
People said:
"Zhòng Zhòng used his wisdom to avoid disaster."
Zhòng said:
"Indeed it is so."
B2.18.3 The Duke of Zhōu intended to assassinate King Zhuāng
and establish Prince Kè.
Xīn Bó informed the king,
and together with the king, they killed the Duke of Zhōu Hēijiān.
Prince Kè fled to Yān.
Earlier,
Zǐ Yí had been favored by King Huán,
and King Huán entrusted him to the Duke of Zhōu.
Xīn Bó remonstrated, saying:
"Having two queens, matching heirs, dual administrations, and paired capitals
are the roots of chaos."
The Duke of Zhōu did not follow this advice,
and thus met his end.
A3.1 The Spring and Autumn Annals, First Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.1.1 First year, spring,
royal first month.
A3.1.2 Third month,
the lady fled to Qí.
A3.1.3 Summer,
Shàn Bó escorted the royal princess.
A3.1.4 Autumn,
built the royal princess's residence outside the capital.
A3.1.5 Winter, tenth month, yǐhài day,
Marquis Lín of Chén died.
A3.1.6 The king sent Róng Shū to confer a posthumous honorific upon Duke Huán.
A3.1.7 The royal princess returned to Qí.
A3.1.8 The Qí army relocated Jì's Píng,
Zī, and Wú.
B3.1 The Commentary, First Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.1.1 First year, spring,
not recorded as ascending the throne,
due to Wén Jiāng's departure.
B3.1.2 Third month,
the lady fled to Qí.
Not recorded as Jiāng Shì,
severing ties, not treating as kin,
is according to ritual.
B3.1.3 Autumn,
built the royal princess's residence outside the capital.
Making it outside,
is according to ritual.
A3.2 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Second Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.2.1 Second year, spring,
royal second month,
buried Duke Zhuāng of Chén.
A3.2.2 Summer,
Prince Qìngfǔ led troops to attack Yúqiū.
A3.2.3 Autumn, seventh month,
the royal princess of Qí died.
A3.2.4 Winter, twelfth month,
Lady Jiāng Shì met with the Marquis of Qí at Zhuó.
A3.2.5 Yǐyǒu day,
Duke Féng of Sòng died.
B3.2 The Commentary, Second Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.2.1 Second year, winter,
Lady Jiāng Shì met with the Marquis of Qí at Zhuó.
Recorded
as illicit.
A3.3 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Third Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.3.1 Third year, spring,
royal first month,
Nì joined with Qí troops to attack Wèi.
A3.3.2 Summer, fourth month,
buried Duke Zhuāng of Sòng.
A3.3.3 Fifth month,
buried King Huán.
A3.3.4 Autumn,
Jì Jì entered Qí with Xī.
A3.3.5 Winter,
the duke stationed at Huá.
B3.3 The Commentary, Third Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.3.1 Third year, spring,
Nì joined with Qí troops to attack Wèi,
disapproved of him.
B3.3.2 Summer, fifth month,
buried King Huán,
delayed.
B3.3.3 Autumn,
Jì Jì entered Qí with Xī,
Jì then began to split.
B3.3.4 Winter,
the duke stationed at Huá,
intending to meet with the Earl of Zhèng,
to plan regarding Jì.
The Earl of Zhèng declined due to difficulties.
Generally, for troops,
one night's stay is called shè,
two nights' stay is called xìn,
beyond xìn is called cì.
A3.4 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Fourth Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.4.1 Fourth year, spring,
royal second month,
Lady Jiāng Shì feasted with the Marquis of Qí at Zhùqiū.
A3.4.2 Third month,
Jì Bó Jī died.
A3.4.3 Summer,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Marquis of Chén,
and the Earl of Zhèng met at Chuí.
A3.4.4 The Marquis of Jì greatly left his state.
A3.4.5 Sixth month, yǐchǒu day,
the Marquis of Qí buried Jì Bó Jī.
A3.4.6 Autumn, seventh month.
A3.4.7 Winter,
the duke and men of Qí hunted at Zhuó.
B3.4 The Commentary, Fourth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.4.1 Fourth year, spring,
royal first month,
King Wǔ of Chǔ performed the Jīngshī ritual,
issued single-edged weapons to the troops,
to attack Suí.
About to perform the purification rite,
he entered and told his wife Dèng Màn:
"My heart is unsettled."
Dèng Màn sighed and said:
"The king's fortune is exhausted.
Fullness leads to unsettlement,
such is the way of heaven.
Our former lord likely knew this,
so before military affairs,
when about to issue great commands,
he unsettled the king's heart.
If the army suffers no loss,
and the king passes away on the march,
it would be the state's blessing."
The king then set out,
and died beneath a mánmù tree.
The Prime Minister Dòu Qí and the Mó'áo Qū Chóng
cleared the roads and bridged the Zhà River,
deployed troops facing Suí,
the people of Suí feared,
and sought peace.
The Mó'áo entered with the king's command
to swear a covenant with the Marquis of Suí,
and requested a meeting at Hàn Ruì,
then returned.
After crossing the Hàn River
they announced the mourning.
B3.4.2 The Marquis of Jì could not submit to Qí,
and handed over to Jì Jì.
Summer,
the Marquis of Jì greatly left his state,
avoiding the Qí threat.
A3.5 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Fifth Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.5.1 Fifth year, spring,
royal first month.
A3.5.2 Summer,
Lady Jiāng Shì went to the Qí army.
A3.5.3 Autumn,
Ní Lílái came for an audience.
A3.5.4 In winter,
the Duke joined with men of Qí,
Sòng,
Chén,
and Cài to attack Wèi.
B3.5 The Commentary to Duke Zhuāng Year 5
B3.5.1 In autumn of the fifth year,
Lílái of Ní came to court.
He is recorded by his personal name
because he had not yet received the king's mandate.
B3.5.2 In winter,
they attacked Wèi
to install Duke Huì.
A3.6 The Spring and Autumn Annals of Duke Zhuāng Year 6
A3.6.1 In spring of the sixth year,
the first month of the royal calendar,
Zǐ Tū, an officer of the king, rescued Wèi.
A3.6.2 In summer, the sixth month,
the Marquis of Wèi, Shuò, entered Wèi.
A3.6.3 In autumn,
the Duke arrived from the campaign against Wèi.
A3.6.4 There were rice borers.
A3.6.5 In winter,
men of Qí came to present captives from Wèi.
B3.6 The Commentary to Duke Zhuāng Year 6
B3.6.1 In spring of the sixth year,
officers of the king rescued Wèi.
In summer,
the Marquis of Wèi entered,
banished Prince Qiánmóu to Zhōu,
banished Níng Guì to Qín,
killed the Left Prince Xiè
and the Right Prince Zhí,
and then ascended the throne.
The gentleman considers that the two princes' establishment of Qiánmóu was not according to proper measure.
Those who can firmly secure a position
must measure the root and branches,
and only then establish the central, appropriate one.
If one does not know the root,
one does not plan;
knowing that the root has no branches,
one does not force it.
The Odes say:
' "Root and branches for a hundred generations." '
B3.6.2 In winter,
men of Qí came to present the treasures of Wèi,
which Wén Jiāng had requested.
B3.6.3 King Wén of Chǔ attacked Shēn.
He passed through Dèng.
Marquis Qí of Dèng said:
"He is my nephew."
He detained him and feasted him.
The nephews Zhuī, Dān, and Yǎng
requested to kill the Viscount of Chǔ.
The Marquis of Dèng did not permit it.
The three nephews said:
"The one who will destroy the state of Dèng
is certainly this man.
If you do not plan early,
later you will bite your navel [i.e., regret it too late].
Should you not plan it now!
To plan it,
this is the time."
The Marquis of Dèng said:
"People will not eat my leftovers."
They replied:
"If you do not follow your three ministers,
then indeed the altars of soil and grain will receive no blood sacrifice,
and from where will you, my lord, get leftovers?"
He did not follow them.
In the year of his return,
the Viscount of Chǔ attacked Dèng.
In the sixteenth year,
Chǔ again attacked Dèng,
and destroyed it.
A3.7 The Spring and Autumn Annals of Duke Zhuāng Year 7
A3.7.1 In spring of the seventh year,
the Lady Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Fáng.
A3.7.2 In summer, the fourth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
at night, the fixed stars were not seen.
At midnight,
stars fell like rain.
A3.7.3 In autumn,
there was a great flood.
A3.7.4 There was no wheat
or young grain.
A3.7.5 In winter,
the Lady Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Gǔ.
B3.7 The Commentary to Duke Zhuāng Year 7
B3.7.1 In spring of the seventh year,
Wén Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Fáng,
which was Qí's intention.
B3.7.2 In summer,
the fixed stars were not seen,
because the night was bright.
Stars fell like rain,
because they fell together with rain.
B3.7.3 In autumn,
there was no wheat
or young grain,
but it did not harm the good grain.
A3.8 The Spring and Autumn Annals of Duke Zhuāng Year 8
A3.8.1 In spring of the eighth year,
the first month of the royal calendar,
the army encamped at Láng,
to await the men of Chén
and Cài.
A3.8.2 On the jiǎwǔ day,
they conducted military exercises.
A3.8.3 In summer,
our army together with the army of Qí besieged Chéng.
Chéng surrendered to the army of Qí.
A3.8.4 In autumn,
the army returned.
A3.8.5 In winter, the eleventh month, on the guǐwèi day,
Wúzhī of Qí assassinated his lord, Zhú'ér.
B3.8 The Commentary to Duke Zhuāng Year 8
B3.8.1 In spring of the eighth year,
they conducted military exercises at the ancestral temple,
which was according to ritual.
B3.8.2 In summer,
our army together with the army of Qí besieged Chéng.
Chéng surrendered to the army of Qí.
Zhòng Qìngfǔ requested to attack the army of Qí.
The Duke said:
"It cannot be.
It is truly I who am without virtue,
what crime has the army of Qí committed?
The crime lies with me.
The Book of Xià says:
' "Gāo Yáo diligently sowed virtue,
and virtue
then descended." '
Let us for now devote ourselves to cultivating virtue
and await the proper time!"
In autumn,
the army returned.
The gentleman therefore praised Duke Zhuāng of Lǔ.
B3.8.3 The Marquis of Qí sent Lián Chēng
and Guǎn Zhìfù to garrison Kuíqiū.
They went at the time of melons,
and he said:
"When the melons come again, you will be relieved."
When the garrison period was due,
no inquiry from the duke arrived.
They requested relief,
but it was not granted.
Therefore they plotted to start a rebellion.
The full younger brother of Duke Xī's mother was named Yí Zhòngnián,
and he begot Gōngsūn Wúzhī,
who was favored by Duke Xī,
and his clothing, rituals, and rank were like those of the heir.
Duke Xiāng degraded him.
The two men [Lián and Guǎn] relied on him to start a rebellion.
Lián Chēng had a younger female cousin in the duke's palace,
who was not favored,
and he had her spy on the duke.
He said:
"If you succeed,
I will make you my lady."
In winter, the twelfth month,
the Marquis of Qí was traveling at Gūfén,
and then hunted at Bèiqiū.
He saw a great boar.
His attendants said:
"It is Prince Péngshēng."
The duke was angry,
and said:
"Péngshēng dares to appear!"
He shot at it.
The boar stood like a man and cried.
The duke was frightened,
fell from his chariot,
injured his foot,
and lost his shoe.
Upon returning, he ordered the search for a shoe from the attendant Fèi.
Not finding it,
he had him flogged,
until blood was drawn.
Fèi fled outside,
where he encountered the assassins at the gate.
They seized and bound him.
Fèi said:
"Why would I resist?"
He bared his back to show them.
They believed him.
Fèi requested to enter first.
He hid the duke and then went out,
fought,
and died within the gate.
Shí Zhī Fēnrú died at the base of the steps.
The assassins then entered,
killed Mèng Yáng on the bed.
They said:
"This is not the ruler,
he does not resemble him."
Seeing the duke's feet beneath the door,
they then assassinated him,
and set up Wúzhī as ruler.
Earlier,
when Duke Xiāng was established as ruler,
he was unpredictable.
Bào Shūyá said:
"The ruler treats the people with contempt,
disorder is about to arise."
He escorted the young lord Xiǎo Bái to flee to Jǔ.
When disorder arose,
Guǎn Yíwú and Shào Hū escorted the young lord Jiū to come seeking refuge.
B3.8.4 Earlier,
Gōngsūn Wúzhī was cruel to Yōng Lǐn.
A3.9 《The Spring and Autumn Annals: Duke Zhuang Year 9》
A3.9.1 In the ninth year, spring,
the people of Qí killed Wúzhī.
A3.9.2 The duke made a covenant with the great officers of Qí at Jì.
A3.9.3 In summer,
the duke attacked Qí,
to install Zǐ Jiū.
Qí's Xiǎo Bái entered Qí.
A3.9.4 In autumn, the seventh month, on the dīngyǒu day,
Duke Xiāng of Qí was buried.
A3.9.5 In the eighth month, on the gēngshēn day,
[our army] engaged the Qí army in battle at Gānshí,
and our army was defeated.
A3.9.6 In the ninth month,
the people of Qí captured Zǐ Jiū and killed him.
A3.9.7 In winter,
the Zhū River was dredged.
B3.9 《The Commentary of Zuo: Duke Zhuang Year 9》
B3.9.1 In the ninth year, spring,
Yōng Lǐn killed Wúzhī.
B3.9.2 The duke made a covenant with the great officers of Qí at Jì,
because Qí had no ruler.
B3.9.3 In summer,
the duke attacked Qí,
to install Zǐ Jiū.
Duke Huán entered first from Jǔ.
B3.9.4 In autumn,
our army engaged the Qí army in battle at Gānshí,
and our army was defeated.
The duke lost his war chariot,
and returned by changing to another carriage.
Qínzǐ and Liángzǐ used the duke's banner
to divert [the enemy] to a side road,
and thus were both captured.
B3.9.5 Bào Shū led the army and came to say:
"Zǐ Jiū,
is a close relative,
we request that you, lord, punish him.
Guǎn [Zhòng] and Shào [Hū] are our enemies,
we request to receive them to satisfy our hearts."
So they killed Zǐ Jiū at Shēngdòu.
Shào Hū died for him.
Guǎn Zhòng requested to be taken prisoner,
Bào Shū accepted him,
and at Tángfù released him.
Upon returning, he reported, saying:
"Guǎn Yíwú's governance surpasses that of Gāo Xī,
he may be made prime minister."
The duke followed his advice.
A3.10 《The Spring and Autumn Annals: Duke Zhuang Year 10》
A3.10.1 In the tenth year, spring,
the royal first month,
the duke defeated the Qí army at Chángsháo.
A3.10.2 In the second month,
the duke invaded Sòng.
A3.10.3 In the third month,
the people of Sòng moved the capital of Sù.
A3.10.4 In summer, the sixth month,
the Qí army
and the Sòng army were stationed at Láng.
The duke defeated the Sòng army at Chéngqiū.
A3.10.5 In autumn, the ninth month,
Jīng defeated the Cài army at Shēn,
and took Cài Hóu Xiànwǔ back with them.
A3.10.6 In winter, the tenth month,
the Qí army destroyed Tán.
The Viscount of Tán fled to Jǔ.
B3.10 《The Commentary of Zuo: Duke Zhuang Year 10》
B3.10.1 In the tenth year, spring,
the Qí army attacked us.
The duke was about to engage in battle.
Cáo Guì requested an audience.
His fellow villager said:
"Those who eat meat will plan for it,
why involve yourself?"
Guì said:
"Those who eat meat are shallow,
they cannot plan far ahead."
He then entered for an audience,
and asked on what basis they would fight.
The duke said:
"Clothing and food that bring comfort,
I dare not keep for myself alone,
but must share with others."
He replied:
"Such small favors are not widespread,
the people will not follow you."
The duke said:
"Sacrificial animals and jade and silk offerings,
I dare not exaggerate,
but must be presented with sincerity."
He replied:
"Such small sincerity is not yet convincing,
the spirits will not bless you."
The duke said:
"In lawsuits, big or small,
though I cannot investigate everything thoroughly,
I must decide based on the actual circumstances."
He replied:
"This is an aspect of loyalty,
you may fight one battle.
When you fight,
then I request to accompany you."
The duke rode with him in the same chariot.
They fought at Chángsháo.
The duke was about to order the drums to beat.
Guì said:
"Not yet."
The Qí people beat the drums three times.
Guì said:
"Now it is permissible!"
The Qí army was defeated.
The duke was about to pursue them.
Guì said:
"Not yet."
He got down,
examined their wheel tracks,
climbed onto the chariot handrail and looked out,
and said:
"Now it is permissible!"
They then pursued the Qí army.
After the victory,
the duke asked the reason.
He replied:
"In battle, it is a matter of courage.
The first drumbeat rouses the spirit,
the second causes it to decline,
the third exhausts it.
Their spirit was exhausted while ours was full,
therefore we overcame them.
As for a great state,
it is difficult to gauge,
I feared there might be an ambush.
I saw their wheel tracks were disordered,
and observed their banners drooping,
therefore I pursued them."
B3.10.2 In summer, the sixth month,
the Qí army and the Sòng army were stationed at Láng.
Gōngzǐ Yǎn said:
"The Sòng army is not in good order,
it can be defeated.
If Sòng is defeated,
Qí will certainly withdraw.
I request to attack them."
The Duke did not permit it.
He secretly went out through the Yú Gate,
covered himself with a tiger skin and led the charge.
The Duke followed him,
and heavily defeated the Sòng army at Chéngqiū.
The Qí army then withdrew.
B3.10.3 Cài Āihóu took a wife from Chén,
and Xīhóu also took a wife from there.
When Xī Guī was returning to her state,
she passed through Cài.
The Marquis of Cài said:
"She is my wife's sister."
He detained her and met with her,
and did not treat her with proper respect.
When the Marquis of Xī heard of this,
he was angry,
and sent a message to King Wén of Chǔ, saying:
"Attack me,
and I will seek help from Cài, and then you can attack them."
The Viscount of Chǔ complied.
In autumn, in the ninth month,
Chǔ defeated the Cài army at Shēn,
and took the Marquis of Cài, Xiànwǔ, back as a captive.
B3.10.4 When the Marquis of Qí was in exile,
he passed through Tán,
and Tán did not treat him with courtesy.
When he returned to his state,
all the feudal lords came to congratulate him,
but Tán again did not come.
In winter,
the Qí army extinguished Tán,
because Tán had been discourteous.
The Viscount of Tán fled to Jǔ,
because they were allies.
A3.11 *The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang, Year 11*
A3.11.1 In the eleventh year, in spring,
the royal first month.
A3.11.2 In summer, in the fifth month,
on Wùyín,
the Duke defeated the Sòng army at Zī.
A3.11.3 In autumn,
there was a great flood in Sòng.
A3.11.4 In winter,
the royal princess went to Qí.
B3.11 *The Commentary of Zuo, Duke Zhuang, Year 11*
B3.11.1 In the eleventh year, in summer,
because of the battle at Chéngqiū,
Sòng invaded us.
The Duke defended against them.
The Sòng army had not yet formed its battle lines when he pressed an attack,
and defeated them at Zī.
In general, regarding armies,
if the enemy has not yet formed its lines, it is called
"defeating such-and-such army."
If both sides have formed their lines, it is called a battle.
If there is a great collapse, it is called a rout.
If a distinguished commander is captured, it is called an overcoming.
If they are ambushed and defeated, it is called taking such-and-such army.
If the royal army is defeated, it is called
"the royal army was routed at such-and-such place."
B3.11.2 In autumn,
there was a great flood in Sòng.
The Duke sent someone to convey condolences,
saying:
"Heaven has sent excessive rains,
harming the grain for sacrifice.
How can we not express sympathy?"
The reply was:
"I, the orphan, have indeed been disrespectful,
so Heaven has sent down this disaster.
That it has also become a concern for you, my lord,
makes me bow in acknowledgment of your gracious command."
Zāng Wénzhòng said:
"Sòng is likely to rise again!
Yǔ and Tāng blamed themselves,
and their rise was sudden.
Jié and Zhòu blamed others,
and their fall was swift.
Moreover, when a feudal state suffers misfortune,
its ruler refers to himself as 'the orphan,'
which is in accordance with ritual.
His words show fear and his title accords with ritual;
he is close to it!"
Later he heard it said:
"These were the words of the prince, Yù Yuè."
Zāngsūn Dá said:
"This man is fit to be ruler;
he has a heart that cares for the people."
B3.11.3 In winter,
the Marquis of Qí came to meet the princess Gòng Jī.
B3.11.4 In the battle at Chéngqiū,
the Duke shot Nángōng Chángwàn with a golden arrow named Púgū,
and the Duke's chariot warrior, Chuán Sūn, captured him alive in hand-to-hand combat.
The people of Sòng requested his return.
The Duke of Sòng mocked him,
saying:
"At first I respected you;
now you,
are a prisoner of Lǔ,
I no longer respect you."
He resented this.
A3.12 *The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang, Year 12*
A3.12.1 In the twelfth year, in spring,
the royal third month,
Jì Shū Jī went to Xī.
A3.12.2 In summer, the fourth month.
A3.12.3 In autumn, in the eighth month, on Jiǎwǔ,
Sòng Wàn assassinated his ruler, Jié, and his great officer, Qiú Mù.
A3.12.4 In winter, in the tenth month,
Sòng Wàn fled to Chén.
B3.12 *The Commentary of Zuo, Duke Zhuang, Year 12*
B3.12.1 In the twelfth year, in autumn,
Sòng Wàn assassinated Duke Mǐn at Méngzé.
He encountered Qiú Mù at the gate,
struck and killed him.
He encountered the Grand Steward Dū to the west of the Eastern Palace,
and killed him also.
He set up Zǐ Yóu as ruler.
The other princes fled to Xiāo,
and Prince Yù Yuè fled to Bó.
Nángōng Niú and
Měng Huó led troops to besiege Bó.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the uncle of Xiāo, Dàxīn, and the clans of Dài, Wǔ, Xuān, Mù, and Zhuāng
attacked them with the army of Cáo.
They killed Nángōng Niú in the army,
killed Zǐ Yóu in Sòng,
and set up Duke Huán.
Měng Huó fled to Wèi.
Nángōng Wàn fled to Chén,
transporting his mother in a carriage,
arriving in a single day.
The people of Sòng requested Měng Huó from Wèi.
The people of Wèi wished not to hand him over.
Shí Qízǐ said:
"That will not do.
Evil is the same everywhere in the world.
If he is detested by Sòng and we protect him,
what good does protecting him do?
To gain one man and lose a state,
to side with evil and abandon good relations,
is not good policy."
The people of Wèi returned him.
They also requested Nángōng Wàn from Chén
with bribes.
The people of Chén had women give him wine to drink,
and then wrapped him in rhinoceros hide.
By the time he reached Sòng,
his hands and feet had pierced through.
The people of Sòng minced them both into paste.
A3.13 *The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang, Year 13*
A3.13.1 In the thirteenth year, in spring,
the Marquis of Qí,
a man of Sòng,
a man of Chén,
a man of Cài,
and a man of Zhū met at Běixìng.
A3.13.2 In summer, in the sixth month,
the men of Qí extinguished Suì.
A3.13.3 In autumn, the seventh month.
A3.13.4 In winter,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and made a covenant at Kē.
B3.13 *The Commentary of Zuo, Duke Zhuang, Year 13*
B3.13.1 In the thirteenth year, in spring,
they met at Běixìng,
to bring peace to the disorder in Sòng.
Suì did not attend.
In summer,
the men of Qí extinguished Suì and garrisoned it.
B3.13.2 In winter,
they made a covenant at Kē,
beginning peaceful relations with Qí.
B3.13.3 The men of Sòng broke the covenant of Běixìng.
A3.14 *The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang, Year 14*
A3.14.1 In the fourteenth year, in spring,
men of Qí,
men of Chén,
and men of Cáo attacked Sòng.
A3.14.2 In summer,
Dān Bó joined in the attack on Sòng.
A3.14.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
Jīng invaded Cài.
A3.14.4 In winter,
Dān Bó met with the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Earl of Zhèng at Juàn.
B3.14 Commentary on Duke Zhuāng, Year 14
B3.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
the feudal lords attacked Sòng.
Qí requested troops from Zhōu.
In summer,
Dān Bó joined them.
They secured a covenant with Sòng and then returned.
B3.14.2 Duke Lì of Zhèng invaded Zhèng from Yuè,
reaching Dàlíng,
where he captured Fù Xiá.
Fù Xiá said:
"If you spare me,
I will request to restore you as ruler."
He made a covenant with him and pardoned him.
On the jiǎzǐ day of the sixth month,
Fù Xiá killed Zhèngzǐ and his two sons,
and restored Duke Lì.
Earlier,
an inner snake and an outer snake fought at the southern gate of Zhèng,
and the inner snake died.
Six years later, Duke Lì entered.
The Duke heard of this,
and asked Shēn Xū, saying:
"Is there still such a portent?"
He replied:
"What a man fears,
his own aura attracts.
Portents arise from men.
If men create no opening,
portents do not arise by themselves.
When men abandon the constant norms,
then portents arise;
hence there are portents."
When Duke Lì entered,
he then killed Fù Xiá.
He sent a message to Yuán Fán, saying:
"Fù Xiá was disloyal;
Zhōu has constant punishments,
and he has already suffered his crime.
Those who restored me without disloyalty,
I have all promised them the positions of high ministers.
I wish to discuss this with my uncle.
Moreover, when I was in exile,
my uncle sent no secret messages.
When I entered,
you again showed no regard for me;
I resent this."
He replied:
"The former ruler, Duke Huán, commanded my ancestors to be in charge of the ancestral temple.
When the altars of soil and grain have a ruler,
yet one's heart is turned outward,
what disloyalty could be greater than this?
If one presides over the altars of soil and grain,
the people within the state,
who among them would not be a subject?
A subject's lack of disloyalty
is the decree of Heaven.
Zǐyí was on the throne
for fourteen years;
yet those who plotted to summon you, my lord,
were they not disloyal?
There are still eight sons of Duke Zhuāng;
if all were to use offices and ranks to offer bribes and encourage disloyalty
in order to accomplish their affairs,
what would you, my lord, do about it?
I have heard your command."
He then hanged himself and died.
B3.14.3 Duke Āi of Cài, because of the affair at Shēn,
praised Xī Guī to the ruler of Chǔ.
The ruler of Chǔ went to Xī,
entered to feast with food offerings,
and then destroyed Xī.
He took Xī Guī back with him,
and she bore Dǔ Áo and King Chéng.
She did not speak.
The ruler of Chǔ asked her about it.
She replied:
"I am but one woman,
yet I have served two husbands.
Even if I could not die,
what more is there to say?"
The ruler of Chǔ, because Duke Āi of Cài had caused the destruction of Xī,
then attacked Cài.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Chǔ entered Cài.
The gentleman says:
"What the Shāng Shū says,
'The ease with which evil spreads,
is like a fire blazing across the plains;
one cannot face it or approach it;
how could it still be stamped out?'
this applies to Duke Āi of Cài!"
B3.14.4 In winter,
they met at Juàn,
because Sòng had submitted.
A3.15 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuāng, Year 15
A3.15.1 In the fifteenth year, in spring,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Earl of Zhèng met at Juàn.
A3.15.2 In summer,
the Lady Jiāng shì went to Qí.
A3.15.3 In autumn,
men of Sòng,
men of Qí,
and men of Zhū attacked Ní.
A3.15.4 Men of Zhèng invaded Sòng.
A3.15.5 In winter, in the tenth month.
B3.15 Commentary on Duke Zhuāng, Year 15
B3.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
they met again there,
and Qí began its hegemony.
B3.15.2 In autumn,
the feudal lords attacked Ní for Sòng's sake.
Zhèng took advantage of this to invade Sòng.
A3.16 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuāng, Year 16
A3.16.1 In the sixteenth year, in spring,
the royal first month.
A3.16.2 In summer,
men of Sòng,
men of Qí,
and men of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
A3.16.3 In autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
A3.16.4 In winter, in the twelfth month,
they met with the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Zhèng,
the Baron of Xǔ,
the Earl of Huá,
and the Viscount of Téng, and made a covenant together at Yōu.
A3.16.5 The Viscount of Zhū, Kè, died.
B3.16 Commentary on Duke Zhuāng, Year 16
B3.16.1 In the summer of the sixteenth year,
the feudal lords attacked Zhèng,
because of Sòng.
B3.16.2 The Earl of Zhèng entered from Yuè,
and was slow to report to Chǔ.
In autumn,
Chǔ attacked Zhèng,
reaching Yuè,
because of this discourtesy.
B3.16.3 The Earl of Zhèng dealt with those involved in the rebellion of Yōng Jiū.
In the ninth month,
he killed the nobleman È,
and amputated the feet of Qiáng Chú.
Gōngfǔ Dìngshū fled to Wèi.
After three years, he restored him,
saying:
"We cannot let Gòng Shū be without descendants in Zhèng."
He had him enter in the tenth month,
saying:
"It is an auspicious month,
completing the full number."
The gentleman says of Qiáng Chú
that he could not protect his own feet.
B3.16.4 In winter,
they made a covenant together at Yōu,
because Zhèng had submitted.
B3.16.5 The King sent the Duke of Guó to command the Earl of Qūwò
to lead one army and become the Marquis of Jìn.
B3.16.6 In the beginning,
Duke Wǔ of Jìn attacked Yí,
and captured Yí Guǐzhū.
Wěi Guó interceded and secured his release.
Later, [Yí Guǐzhū] did not repay [the favor],
so Zǐ Guó [i.e., Wěi Guó] rebelled,
and said to the men of Jìn:
"Join me in attacking Yí and taking its land."
He then used the Jìn army to attack Yí,
and killed Yí Guǐzhū.
Zhōu Gōng Jìfǔ fled to Guó.
King Huì was established and restored him.
A3.17 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 17 of Duke Zhuāng
A3.17.1 In the seventeenth year, spring,
men of Qí captured Zhèng Zhān.
A3.17.2 Summer,
men of Qí were annihilated at Suì.
A3.17.3 Autumn,
Zhèng Zhān escaped from Qí and came [to Lǔ].
A3.17.4 Winter,
there were many deer.
B3.17 The Commentary of Zuo, Year 17 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.17.1 In the seventeenth year, spring,
men of Qí captured Zhèng Zhān,
because Zhèng did not come to court.
B3.17.2 Summer,
the Yīn,
Hé,
Gōnglóu,
and Xūsuì clans of Suì feasted the Qí garrison,
got them drunk, and killed them;
the men of Qí were annihilated there.
A3.18 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 18 of Duke Zhuāng
A3.18.1 In the eighteenth year, spring,
in the king's third month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
A3.18.2 Summer,
the duke pursued the Róng west of the Jǐ River.
A3.18.3 Autumn,
there were yù [venomous insects].
A3.18.4 Winter, the tenth month.
B3.18 The Commentary of Zuo, Year 18 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.18.1 In the eighteenth year, spring,
the Duke of Guó and
the Marquis of Jìn had audience with the king.
The king entertained them with sweet wine,
and commanded them to partake.
He bestowed on each five pairs of jade and
four teams of horses.
This was contrary to ritual.
When the king commands the feudal lords,
since their names and ranks differ,
the rituals and measures also differ;
one does not lend ritual to others.
B3.18.2 The Duke of Guó, the Marquis of Jìn, and the Earl of Zhèng
sent Duke Zhuāng of Yuán to meet the king's bride in Chén.
The lady Guī of Chén returned to the capital,
she was Queen Huì.
B3.18.3 Summer,
the duke pursued the Róng west of the Jǐ River.
It is not stated that they came,
to conceal it.
B3.18.4 Autumn,
there were yù,
which caused disaster.
B3.18.5 In the beginning,
King Wǔ of Chǔ conquered Quán,
and appointed Dòu Mín to administer it.
He rebelled,
[the king] besieged and killed him.
He moved Quán to Nàchù,
and appointed Yán Áo to administer it.
When King Wén came to the throne,
he attacked Shēn together with the Bā people,
but alarmed their army.
The Bā people rebelled against Chǔ and attacked Nàchù,
captured it,
and then attacked the gates of Chǔ.
Yán Áo was swimming in Yǒng and fled.
The Viscount of Chǔ killed him.
His clan rebelled.
Winter,
the Bā people took advantage of this to attack Chǔ.
A3.19 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 19 of Duke Zhuāng
A3.19.1 In the nineteenth year, spring,
the king's first month.
A3.19.2 Summer, the fourth month.
A3.19.3 Autumn,
Gōngzǐ Jié escorted a bride for a man of Chén to Juàn,
and then made a covenant with
the Marquis of Qí and
the Duke of Sòng.
A3.19.4 The lady Jiāng, the wife [of Duke Zhuāng], went to Jǔ.
A3.19.5 Winter,
men of Qí,
Sòng,
and Chén attacked our western borders.
B3.19 The Commentary of Zuo, Year 19 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.19.1 In the nineteenth year, spring,
the Viscount of Chǔ resisted them,
but was greatly defeated at Jīn.
On his return,
Yùquán would not admit him,
so he attacked Huáng.
He defeated the Huáng army at Jí Líng.
On his return,
when he reached Jiǎo,
he fell ill.
In summer, on the gēngshēn day of the sixth month,
he died.
Yùquán buried him in the Xī Chamber.
He also committed suicide,
and was buried at Diéhuáng.
In the beginning,
Yùquán forcefully remonstrated with the Viscount of Chǔ.
The Viscount of Chǔ would not listen.
[Yùquán] confronted him with weapons,
[the Viscount] became afraid and complied.
Yùquán said:
"I made my lord afraid with weapons,
no crime is greater than this."
He then amputated his own foot.
The people of Chǔ made him Chief Gatekeeper,
calling him Dà Bó.
They made his descendants hold the office.
The gentleman says:
"Yùquán can be said to have loved his lord:
he remonstrated so as to bring punishment upon himself,
and even after being punished, he did not forget to guide his lord towards goodness."
B3.19.2 In the beginning,
Wáng Yáo was favored by King Zhuāng,
and gave birth to Zǐ Tuí.
Zǐ Tuí was favored,
and Wěi Guó became his tutor.
When King Huì came to the throne,
he took Wěi Guó's garden to make a park.
Biān Bó's palace was near the king's palace,
and the king took it.
The king seized the fields of Zǐ Qín Zhùguì and Zhān Fù,
and stopped the stipend of the royal cook.
Therefore, Wěi Guó, Biān Bó, Shí Sù, Zhān Fù, and Zǐ Qín Zhùguì rebelled,
relying on the Sū clan.
Autumn,
the five great officers supported Zǐ Tuí in attacking the king,
but were unsuccessful,
and fled to Wēn.
Zǐ of Sū supported Zǐ Tuí and fled to Wèi.
The armies of Wèi
and Yān attacked Zhōu.
Winter,
they established Zǐ Tuí [as king].
A3.20 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 20 of Duke Zhuāng
A3.20.1 In the twentieth year, spring,
the king's second month,
the lady Jiāng, the wife [of Duke Zhuāng], went to Jǔ.
A3.20.2 Summer,
there was a great disaster in Qí.
A3.20.3 Autumn, the seventh month.
A3.20.4 Winter,
men of Qí attacked the Róng.
B3.20 The Commentary of Zuo, Year 20 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.20.1 In the twentieth year, spring,
the Earl of Zhèng mediated peace in the royal house,
but was unsuccessful.
He captured Yàn Zhòngfù.
Summer,
the Earl of Zhèng then escorted the king back.
The king resided at Lì.
Autumn,
the king and the Earl of Zhèng entered Wū.
They then entered Chéngzhōu,
took its precious vessels, and returned.
Winter,
Prince Tuí entertained the five great officers,
and the music included dances from all [the former kings].
The Earl of Zhèng heard of this,
and meeting Guó Shū, said:
"I have heard that:
when sorrow and joy are untimely,
calamity and misfortune are sure to arrive.
Now Prince Tuí sings and dances without weariness—
this is delighting in calamity.
Ah!
When the Minister of Justice carries out an execution,
the ruler refrains from feasting;
how much less dare one delight in calamity?
To usurp the king's position—
what calamity could be greater?
To face calamity yet forget sorrow,
sorrow is sure to reach him.
Why not restore the king?"
The Duke of Guó said:
"That is my wish."
A3.21 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 21 of Duke Zhuāng
A3.21.1 In the twenty-first year, in spring,
the royal first month.
A3.21.2 In summer, in the fifth month, on the xīnyǒu day,
the Earl of Zhèng, Tū, died.
A3.21.3 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the wùxū day,
the lady Jiāng Shì passed away.
A3.21.4 In winter, in the twelfth month,
we buried Duke Lì of Zhèng.
B3.21 The Commentary of Zuǒ, Year 21 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.21.1 In the twenty-first year, in spring,
they made a verbal agreement at Mǐ.
In summer,
they jointly attacked the royal capital.
The Earl of Zhèng escorted the king, entering through the Yǔ Gate.
Guó Shū entered through the north gate.
They killed Prince Tuí and five senior ministers.
The Earl of Zhèng feasted the king at the western side-tower of the palace gate,
with all the music performed.
The king gave him the lands that had belonged to Duke Wǔ,
from Hǔláo eastward.
Yuán Bó said:
"The Earl of Zhèng is imitating faults;
he too will have misfortune."
In the fifth month,
Duke Lì of Zhèng died.
The king made an inspection tour of Guó's territory.
The Duke of Guó built a palace for the king at Bàng,
and the king gave him Jiǔquán.
When the Earl of Zhèng feasted the king,
the king gave him the queen's pánjiàn mirror.
The Duke of Guó requested vessels,
and the king gave him a jué goblet.
From this, the Earl of Zhèng began to bear resentment toward the king.
In winter,
the king returned from Guó.
A3.22 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 22 of Duke Zhuāng
A3.22.1 In the twenty-second year, in spring,
the royal first month,
there was a general amnesty.
A3.22.2 On the guǐchǒu day,
we buried our lesser ruler, Wén Jiāng.
A3.22.3 The people of Chén killed their prince, Yùkòu.
A3.22.4 In summer, in the fifth month.
A3.22.5 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the bǐngshēn day,
we made a covenant with Qí's Gāo Xī at Fáng.
A3.22.6 In winter,
our duke went to Qí to present betrothal gifts.
B3.22 The Commentary of Zuǒ, Year 22 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.22.1 In the twenty-second year, in spring,
the people of Chén killed their crown prince, Yùkòu.
Chén's prince, Wán, and Zhuānsūn fled to Qí.
Zhuānsūn came to us from Qí.
The Marquis of Qí wished to make Jìngzhòng a minister.
He declined, saying:
"I, a wandering minister, am fortunate if I obtain pardon,
and come under lenient governance,
being forgiven for my lack of training in instruction,
and spared from crimes and faults,
relieved of my burdens—
this is your lordship's kindness.
What I have obtained is already much;
how dare I disgrace a high position
and hasten official criticism?
I beg to report this with my life.
The Odes say:
'High and lofty is the carriage,
they summon me with a bow.
Is it that I do not wish to go?
I fear my friends.'"
He was made Director of Artisans.
He drank wine with Duke Huán,
and there was music.
The duke said:
"Let us continue by lamplight."
He declined, saying:
"I divined for the day,
but did not divine for the night;
I dare not."
The gentleman says:
"Wine is to complete the rites;
not to continue into excess—
this is righteousness.
To cause his lord to complete the rites,
and not lead him into excess—
this is benevolence."
Earlier,
the Yì family divined about marrying their daughter to Jìngzhòng.
His wife interpreted the omen,
saying:
"Auspicious.
This is called:
'The male and female phoenixes fly together,
their harmonious cries clanging.
The descendants of Guī,
will be nurtured among Jiāng.
In the fifth generation they will flourish,
and rank alongside the chief ministers.
After eight generations,
none will match their greatness.'"
Duke Lì of Chén
was born of a woman from Cài;
therefore the men of Cài killed Wǔfù
and set him up.
He begot Jìngzhòng.
When he was young,
a Zhou historian came to see the Marquis of Chén with the Zhōuyì,
and the Marquis of Chén had him perform a divination by stalks.
He obtained Guān changing to Pǐ,
and said:
"This is called
'viewing the light of the state,
beneficial to be a guest of the king.'
Does this mean he will replace Chén and possess a state?
Not in this state,
but in another state;
not in his own person,
but in his descendants.
Light—
is something that shines from afar and from other places.
Kūn
is earth;
Xùn
is wind;
Qián
is heaven;
wind becomes heaven; above earth,
there is mountain.
Having the materials of the mountain,
and shining upon them with the light of heaven,
thus dwelling above earth—
therefore it is said:
'viewing the light of the state,
beneficial to be a guest of the king.'
The courtyard offerings number a hundred,
presented with jades and silks—
the beauties of heaven and earth are all there,
therefore it is said:
'beneficial to be a guest of the king.'
There is still viewing,
therefore it is said it will be in later times!
Wind blows and settles upon earth,
therefore it is said it will be in another state!
If in another state,
it must be of the Jiāng surname.
Jiāng
are descendants of the great mountain.
Mountain peaks match heaven.
No thing can have two greats.
When Chén declines,
this one will flourish!"
When Chén was first destroyed,
Chén Huánzǐ first became great in Qí;
when it was later destroyed,
Chéngzǐ obtained government.
A3.23 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 23 of Duke Zhuāng
A3.23.1 In the twenty-third year, in spring,
our duke arrived from Qí.
A3.23.2 Zhài Shū came on a friendly mission.
A3.23.3 In summer,
our duke went to Qí to observe the shè sacrifice.
A3.23.4 Our duke arrived from Qí.
A3.23.5 People from Jīng came on a diplomatic visit.
A3.23.6 The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Gǔ.
A3.23.7 Shū, the lord of Xiāo, paid a court visit to the Duke.
A3.23.8 In autumn,
the pillars of Duke Huán's temple were painted red.
A3.23.9 In winter, in the eleventh month,
Earl Shègū of Cáo died.
A3.23.10 In the twelfth month, on the jiǎyín day,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and made a covenant at Hù.
B3.23 The Commentary of Duke Zhuāng's 23rd Year
B3.23.1 In the summer of the 23rd year,
the Duke went to Qí to observe the shè sacrifice,
which was contrary to ritual.
Cáo Guì remonstrated, saying:
"You must not.
Now ritual
is that by which the people are regulated.
Therefore, assemblies
are to instruct the rules for superiors and inferiors,
and to regulate the measures for the use of wealth;
court visits are to rectify the principles of rank and nobility,
and to lead the order of elders and juniors;
punitive campaigns are to chastise those who are not compliant.
The feudal lords have their duties to the king,
and the king has his tours of inspection,
by which these are greatly practiced.
If it is not for these purposes,
a ruler does not undertake such actions.
A ruler's actions are necessarily recorded;
if they are recorded but are not in accordance with the model,
what will later generations look upon?"
B3.23.2 The clans of Huán and Zhuāng in Jìn were pressing upon [the ducal house],
and Duke Xiàn was troubled by them.
Shì Wěi said:
"If we remove Fùzǐ,
then the other princes can be dealt with."
The Duke said:
"You try the matter."
Shì Wěi conspired with the princes,
and slandered Fùzǐ to remove him.
B3.23.3 In autumn,
the pillars of Duke Huán's temple were painted red.
A3.24 The Annals of Duke Zhuāng's 24th Year
A3.24.1 In the 24th year, in spring,
in the king's third month,
the rafters of Duke Huán's temple were carved.
A3.24.2 Duke Zhuāng of Cáo was buried.
A3.24.3 In summer,
the Duke went to Qí to meet his bride.
A3.24.4 In autumn,
the Duke arrived from Qí.
A3.24.5 In the eighth month, on the dīngchǒu day,
Lady Jiāng entered.
A3.24.6 On the wùyín day,
the great officers and the wives of the ducal clan had an audience,
using silk as gifts.
A3.24.7 There was a great flood.
A3.24.8 In winter,
the Róng invaded Cáo.
A3.24.9 Jī of Cáo fled to Chén.
A3.24.10 Chì returned to Cáo.
A3.24.11 The Lord of Guō.
B3.24 The Commentary of Duke Zhuāng's 24th Year
B3.24.1 In the spring of the 24th year,
the rafters were carved,
which was also contrary to ritual.
Yù Sūn remonstrated, saying:
"I have heard it said:
'Frugality
is the commonality of virtue,
extravagance
is the greatest of evils.'
Our former ruler possessed this common virtue,
yet you, my lord, are placing yourself among great evils;
is this not unacceptable?"
B3.24.2 In autumn,
when Āi Jiāng arrived,
the Duke had the wives of the ducal clan have an audience,
using silk as gifts,
which was contrary to ritual.
Yù Sūn said:
"For men's presentation gifts,
the greater ones are jade and silk,
the lesser ones are birds and animals,
to distinguish the ranks.
For women's presentation gifts,
they do not go beyond hazelnuts, chestnuts, dates, and dried meat,
to show reverence.
Now men and women use the same gifts;
this is to make no distinction.
The distinction between men and women
is a great principle of the state;
and to have it thrown into disorder by the lady,
is this not unacceptable?"
B3.24.3 Shì Wěi of Jìn again conspired with the princes,
and had them kill the two sons of the Yóu clan.
Shì Wěi reported to the Marquis of Jìn, saying:
"It is possible now.
In no more than two years,
you will certainly have no more trouble."
A3.25 The Annals of Duke Zhuāng's 25th Year
A3.25.1 In the 25th year, in spring,
the Marquis of Chén sent Nǚshū to come on a diplomatic visit.
A3.25.2 In summer, in the fifth month, on the guǐchǒu day,
Marquis Shuò of Wèi died.
A3.25.3 In the sixth month, on the xīnwèi day,
the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse,
drums were beaten and a sacrifice of animals was made at the altar of the soil.
A3.25.4 Bó Jī went to her home in Qǐ.
A3.25.5 In autumn,
there was a great flood,
drums were beaten and a sacrifice of animals was made at the altar of the soil
and at the gate.
A3.25.6 In winter,
Prince Yǒu went to Chén.
B3.25 The Commentary of Duke Zhuāng's 25th Year
B3.25.1 In the spring of the 25th year,
Nǚshū of Chén came on a diplomatic visit,
beginning the establishment of friendly relations with Chén.
He was praised,
therefore his personal name is not recorded.
B3.25.2 In summer, in the sixth month, on the xīnwèi day,
the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse,
drums were beaten and a sacrifice of animals was made at the altar of the soil,
which was not according to regular practice.
Only on the first day of the first month,
when evil has not yet arisen,
if there is a solar eclipse,
then silk is used at the altar of the soil,
and drums are beaten at the court.
B3.25.3 In autumn,
there was a great flood,
drums were beaten and a sacrifice of animals was made at the altar of the soil
and at the gate,
which was also not according to regular practice.
In general, for heavenly disasters,
there is silk,
but no animal sacrifice.
Drums are not beaten except for the calamities of the sun and moon.
B3.25.4 Shì Wěi of Jìn had the princes completely exterminate the Yóu clan,
and then built the city of Jù and settled them there.
In winter,
the Marquis of Jìn besieged Jù,
and killed all the princes.
A3.26 The Annals of Duke Zhuāng's 26th Year
A3.26.1 In the 26th year, in spring,
the Duke attacked the Róng.
A3.26.2 In summer,
the Duke arrived from attacking the Róng.
A3.26.3 Cáo put its great officer to death.
A3.26.4 In autumn,
the Duke joined with men of Sòng
and men of Qí in attacking Xú.
A3.26.5 In winter, in the twelfth month, on the guǐhài day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
B3.26 The Commentary of Duke Zhuāng's 26th Year
B3.26.1 In the spring of the 26th year,
Shì Wěi of Jìn became the Grand Minister of Works.
B3.26.2 In summer,
Shì Wěi fortified Jiàng,
to deepen its palace.
B3.26.3 In autumn,
the people of Guó invaded Jìn.
In winter,
the people of Guó invaded Jìn again.
A3.27 The Twenty-seventh Year of Duke Zhuāng – The Classic
A3.27.1 In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the duke met with Lady Jì, the wife of the Earl of Qǐ, at Táo.
A3.27.2 In summer, in the sixth month,
he met with the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
and the Earl of Zhèng,
and they formed a covenant together at Yōu.
A3.27.3 In autumn,
the duke's son Yǒu went to Chén
to attend the burial of Yuán Zhòng.
A3.27.4 In winter,
Lady Jì of Qǐ came.
A3.27.5 Qìng of Jǔ came to meet Shū Jī.
A3.27.6 The Earl of Qǐ came for an audience.
A3.27.7 The duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Chéngpú.
B3.27 The Twenty-seventh Year of Duke Zhuāng – The Commentary
B3.27.1 In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the duke met with Lady Jì, the wife of the Earl of Qǐ, at Táo.
This was not a matter of state affairs.
The Son of Heaven does not tour the domains except to display righteousness;
the feudal lords do not undertake actions except for the people's affairs;
a minister does not cross the border except by his lord's command.
B3.27.2 In summer,
they formed a covenant together at Yōu,
because Chén and Zhèng had submitted.
B3.27.3 In autumn,
the duke's son Yǒu went to Chén
to attend the burial of Yuán Zhòng.
This was contrary to ritual.
Yuán Zhòng
was an old friend of Jì Yǒu.
B3.27.4 In winter,
Lady Jì of Qǐ came.
It was to return to her natal state to visit her parents.
In general, when a daughter of a feudal lord returns to her natal state to visit her parents, it is called "coming";
when she is divorced and returns, it is called "coming back";
when a wife returns to her natal state to visit her parents, it is called "going to such-and-such";
when she is divorced and returns, it is called "returning to such-and-such."
B3.27.5 The Marquis of Jìn was about to attack Guó.
Shì Wěi said:
"It cannot be done.
The Duke of Guó is arrogant.
If he suddenly wins a victory over us,
he will certainly abandon his people.
When he has no multitude, then attack him.
If he wishes to resist us,
who will be with him?
Ritual, music, kindness, and love
are what warfare stores up.
The people
must be deferential in service, joyful in harmony, loving to their kin, and mournful in bereavement,
and only then can they be used.
Guó does not store these up,
and is eager for war;
it will face famine."
B3.27.6 The King sent Shào Bó Liáo to confer a command on the Marquis of Qí,
and requested him to attack Wèi,
because it had set up Zǐ Tuí.
A3.28 The Twenty-eighth Year of Duke Zhuāng – The Classic
A3.28.1 In the twenty-eighth year, in spring,
in the third month of the royal calendar, on the jiǎyín day,
the men of Qí attacked Wèi.
The men of Wèi fought with the men of Qí,
and the men of Wèi were utterly defeated.
A3.28.2 In summer, in the fourth month, on the dīngwèi day,
Zǐ Suǒ, the Viscount of Zhū, died.
A3.28.3 In autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
The duke joined the men of Qí
and the men of Sòng
to rescue Zhèng.
A3.28.4 In winter,
they built fortifications at Méi.
A3.28.5 There was a great failure of wheat
and millet. Zāngsūn Chén requested grain from Qí.
B3.28 The Twenty-eighth Year of Duke Zhuāng – The Commentary
B3.28.1 In the twenty-eighth year, in spring,
the Marquis of Qí attacked Wèi.
They fought,
and he defeated the army of Wèi.
He enumerated their offenses in the name of the King's command,
took bribes, and returned.
B3.28.2 Duke Xiàn of Jìn took a wife from Jiǎ,
but she had no son.
He had relations with Qí Jiāng,
who gave birth to the Lady of Duke Mù of Qín and the heir apparent Shēnshēng.
He also took two daughters from the Róng tribes:
the elder, Hú Jī of the Dà Róng, gave birth to Chóng'ěr;
the younger, Zǐ of the Xiǎo Róng, gave birth to Yíwú.
Jìn attacked the Lí Róng,
and the men of the Lí Róng offered their daughter Lí Jī.
She was brought back
and gave birth to Xī Qí.
Her younger sister gave birth to Zhuó Zǐ.
Lí Jī was favored
and wished to establish her own son.
She bribed the outside favorites Liáng Wǔ and Dōngguān Wǔ,
and had them speak to the duke, saying:
"Qūwò
is your ancestral city;
Pú and the two Qū
are your borders.
They cannot be without a ruler.
If an ancestral city has no ruler,
then the people will not be in awe;
if the borders have no ruler,
then it will open the minds of the Róng to encroach;
if the Róng conceive such thoughts,
and the people become lax in their governance,
it will be a calamity for the state.
If you send the heir apparent to rule Qūwò,
and Chóng'ěr
and Yíwú to rule Pú and Qū,
then you can awe the people and make the Róng fearful,
and moreover display your achievements."
She had them both say:
"The vast wilderness of the Dí
could become cities for Jìn.
For Jìn to open up territory,
would that not be fitting!"
The Marquis of Jìn was pleased with this.
In summer,
he sent the heir apparent to reside at Qūwò,
Chóng'ěr to reside at Púchéng,
and Yíwú to reside at Qū.
All the other ducal sons were sent to border towns.
Only the sons of the two Jī
remained at Jiàng.
The two Wǔ in the end joined Lí Jī in slandering the other ducal sons
and establishing Xī Qí.
The people of Jìn called them "the pair of Wǔ."
B3.28.3 Zǐ Yuán, the Prime Minister of Chǔ, wished to seduce Lady Wén.
He built a lodge beside her palace
and performed the Wàn dance there.
The lady heard of it
and wept, saying:
"The former lord used this dance
to practice military preparations.
Now the Prime Minister does not seek it from our enemies,
but performs it beside this widow,
is it not strange!"
Her attendant reported this to Zǐ Yuán.
Zǐ Yuán said:
"A woman does not forget to attack the enemy,
yet I have forgotten it!"
In autumn,
Zǐ Yuán attacked Zhèng with six hundred chariots
and entered through the Júdié Gate.
Zǐ Yuán, Dòu Yùqiáng, Dòu Wú, and Gěng Zhībùbǐ formed the vanguard with their banners,
while Dòu Bān, Wángsūn Yóu, and Wángsūn Xǐ brought up the rear.
The mass of chariots entered through the Chún Gate
and reached the market at the crossroads.
The suspended gate was not lowered.
They spoke in the Chǔ dialect and withdrew.
Zǐ Yuán said:
"There are capable men in Zhèng."
The feudal lords came to rescue Zhèng.
The Chǔ army fled by night.
The people of Zhèng were about to flee to Tóngqiū
when a spy reported:
"There are crows on the tents of Chǔ."
Then they stopped.
B3.28.4 In winter,
there was famine.
Zāngsūn Chén requested grain from Qí.
This was according to ritual.
B3.28.5 They built fortifications at Méi.
It was not a capital.
In general, a settlement
that has the ancestral temple and the spirit tablets of the former lords
is called a capital;
if it does not, it is called a settlement.
For a settlement, it is called "building";
for a capital, it is called "walling."
A3.29 The Twenty-ninth Year of Duke Zhuāng – The Classic
A3.29.1 In the twenty-ninth year, in spring,
the Yán stable was renewed.
A3.29.2 In summer,
men of Zhèng invaded Xǔ.
A3.29.3 In autumn,
there were fěi insects.
A3.29.4 In winter, in the twelfth month,
Shū Jī of Jì died.
A3.29.5 The cities of Zhū and Fáng were walled.
B3.29 The Commentary of the Twenty-ninth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.29.1 In the twenty-ninth year, in spring,
the Yán stable was newly built.
It was recorded
because it was not the proper season.
In all cases regarding horses,
they are let out at the mid-spring equinox,
and brought in at the mid-autumn equinox.
B3.29.2 In summer,
men of Zhèng invaded Xǔ.
In all cases of military operations,
those with bells and drums are called 'fá' (an attack),
those without are called 'qīn' (an invasion),
and light, rapid ones are called 'xí' (a raid).
B3.29.3 In autumn,
there were fěi insects,
because they caused a calamity.
In all cases of creatures,
if they do not cause a calamity,
they are not recorded.
B3.29.4 In winter, in the twelfth month,
the cities of Zhū and Fáng were walled.
It was recorded
because it was the proper season.
In all cases of earthworks,
when the Dragon constellation appears and all tasks are finished, it is time to prepare for them;
when the Fire constellation appears, tools are distributed;
when the Water constellation is visible at dusk and correctly positioned, the frames are set up;
and they are completed by the winter solstice.
B3.29.5 Fán Pí rebelled against the king.
A3.30 The Spring and Autumn Annals of the Thirtieth Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.30.1 In the thirtieth year, in spring,
it was the king's first month.
A3.30.2 In summer,
[the army] halted at Chéng.
A3.30.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
men of Qí subdued Zhāng.
A3.30.4 In the eighth month, on Guǐhài,
Shū Jī of Jì was buried.
A3.30.5 In the ninth month, on Gēngwǔ, the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
Drums were beaten and a sacrifice was offered at the altar of the soil.
A3.30.6 In winter,
the duke and the marquis of Qí met at Lǔ Jì.
A3.30.7 Men of Qí attacked the Shānróng.
B3.30 The Commentary of the Thirtieth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.30.1 In the thirtieth year, in spring,
the king commanded the duke of Guó to punish Fán Pí.
In summer, in the fourth month, on Bǐngchén,
the duke of Guó entered Fán,
captured Fán Zhòngpí,
and took him back to the capital.
B3.30.2 The Qīng of Chǔ, Gōngzǐ Yuán, returned from attacking Zhèng
and took up residence in the king's palace.
Dòu Shèshī remonstrated,
and [Gōngzǐ Yuán] had him seized and put in fetters.
In autumn,
Shēn Gōng Dòu Bān killed Zǐ Yuán.
Dòu Gòuwūtú became the Lìngyǐn.
He ruined his own family
to relieve the difficulties of the state of Chǔ.
B3.30.3 In winter,
they met at Lǔ Jì,
to plan about the Shānróng,
because they were harassing Yān.
A3.31 The Spring and Autumn Annals of the Thirty-first Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.31.1 In the thirty-first year, in spring,
a terrace was built at Láng.
A3.31.2 In summer, in the fourth month,
the earl of Xuē died.
A3.31.3 A terrace was built at Xuē.
A3.31.4 In the sixth month,
the marquis of Qí came to present spoils from the Róng.
A3.31.5 In autumn,
a terrace was built at Qín.
A3.31.6 In winter,
there was no rain.
B3.31 The Commentary of the Thirty-first Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.31.1 In the thirty-first year, in summer, in the sixth month,
the marquis of Qí came to present spoils from the Róng.
This was contrary to propriety.
In all cases where the feudal lords achieve merit against the barbarians of the four quarters,
they present the spoils to the king,
and the king uses them to warn the barbarians.
Within the central states, it is not so.
Feudal lords do not present captives to each other.
A3.32 The Spring and Autumn Annals of the Thirty-second Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.32.1 In the thirty-second year, in spring,
the city of Xiǎogǔ was walled.
A3.32.2 In summer,
the duke of Sòng
and the marquis of Qí met at Liángqiū.
A3.32.3 In autumn, in the seventh month, on Guǐsì,
Gōngzǐ Yá died.
A3.32.4 In the eighth month, on Guǐhài,
the duke died in the Lùqǐn chamber.
A3.32.5 In winter, in the tenth month, on Jǐwèi,
Zǐ Bān died.
A3.32.6 Gōngzǐ Qìngfǔ went to Qí.
A3.32.7 The Dí attacked Xíng.
B3.32 The Commentary of the Thirty-second Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.32.1 In the thirty-second year, in spring,
the city of Xiǎogǔ was walled,
for Guǎn Zhòng's sake.
B3.32.2 Because the marquis of Qí had attacked Zhèng for Chǔ,
he requested a meeting with the feudal lords.
The duke of Sòng requested to first have an interview with the marquis of Qí.
In summer,
they met at Liángqiū.
B3.32.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
a spirit descended at Shēn.
King Huì asked Nèishǐ Guò about it, saying:
"What is the reason for this?"
He replied:
"When a state is about to rise,
a bright spirit descends upon it,
to oversee its virtue.
When it is about to perish,
a spirit again descends upon it,
to observe its wickedness.
Therefore, there are those who obtain a spirit and rise,
and also those who because of it perish.
Yú, Xià,
Shāng, and Zhōu all had such cases."
The king said:
"What should be done about it?"
He replied:
"Sacrifice to it with the appropriate offerings.
On the day of its arrival,
the offerings should also correspond to it."
The king followed this.
Nèishǐ Guò went,
and heard that Guó was requesting a mandate [from the spirit].
Returning, he said:
"Guó is sure to perish.
It is cruel and listens to spirits."
The spirit dwelt at Shēn for six months.
The duke of Guó sent Zhù Yìng, Zōng Ōu, and Shǐ Yín to sacrifice to it.
The spirit bestowed fields upon him.
Shǐ Yín said:
"Is Guó about to perish?
I have heard that:
when a state is about to rise,
it listens to the people;
when it is about to perish,
it listens to spirits.
Spirits are
intelligent, upright, and of one mind,
and they act in accordance with men.
Guó has much cold virtue;
what fields can it obtain?"
B3.32.4 Formerly,
the duke built a terrace,
overlooking the Dǎng family.
He saw Mèng Rén
and pursued her.
She shut [the door].
And because of the lady's words,
he agreed,
cut his arm and made a covenant with the duke,
and gave birth to Ziban.
At the rain sacrifice,
a ceremony was held at the Liáng family,
and the young lady went to watch it.
The groom Luò from outside the wall
flirted with her.
Ziban was angry,
and ordered him to be whipped.
The duke said:
"Better to kill him;
this is not a man to be whipped.
Luò has great strength,
and can throw a chariot cover over the Jì Gate."
The duke fell ill,
and asked about his successor from Shūyá.
He replied:
"Qìngfǔ is capable."
He asked Jìyǒu.
He replied:
"I will serve Bān to the death."
The duke said:
"Just now Yá said
'Qìngfǔ is capable.'"
Chéngjì sent him with the ruler's order
to order Xīshū to wait at Qián Wū's house,
and had Qián Jì poison him.
He said:
"Drink this,
and you will have descendants in the state of Lǔ;
if not,
you will die and have no descendants."
He drank it,
returned,
and died upon reaching Kuíquán.
He established the Shūsūn family.
B3.32.5 In the eighth month, on Guǐhài,
the duke died in the main chamber.
Ziban ascended the throne,
and stayed at the Dǎng family.
In winter, the tenth month, on Jǐwèi,
Gòngzhòng
sent the groom Luò
to assassinate Ziban at the Dǎng family.
Chéngjì fled to Chén. Mǐngōng was established.
A4.1 "The Classic of the First Year of Mǐngōng"
A4.1.1 First year, spring,
the royal first month.
A4.1.2 The people of Qí rescued Xíng.
A4.1.3 Summer, sixth month, on Xīnyǒu,
we buried our ruler, Duke Zhuāng.
A4.1.4 Autumn, eighth month,
the duke and the marquis of Qí made a covenant at Luògū.
Jìzǐ came back.
A4.1.5 Winter,
Zhòngsūn of Qí came.
B4.1 "The Commentary of the First Year of Mǐngōng"
B4.1.1 First year, spring,
it is not recorded that he ascended the throne,
due to the disorder.
B4.1.2 The Dí people attacked Xíng.
Guǎn Jìngzhòng said to the marquis of Qí:
"The Róng and Dí are jackals and wolves,
and cannot be satisfied;
the various Xià are close and intimate,
and cannot be abandoned.
Ease and comfort are like poison,
and cannot be cherished.
The Odes say:
'Do I not long to return?
But I fear this bamboo slip.'
The bamboo slip
refers to sharing hatred and showing compassion.
I request to rescue Xíng
in accordance with the bamboo slip."
The people of Qí rescued Xíng.
B4.1.3 Summer, sixth month,
Duke Zhuāng was buried.
Due to the disorder,
it was therefore delayed.
B4.1.4 Autumn, eighth month,
the duke and the marquis of Qí made a covenant at Luògū,
to request the return of Jìyǒu.
The marquis of Qí agreed,
and sent to summon him from Chén.
The duke stayed at Láng to await him.
"Jìzǐ came back"
is to praise him.
B4.1.5 Winter,
Zhòngsūn Jiǎo of Qí came to inquire about the disaster.
It is recorded as
"Zhòngsūn"
also to praise him.
Zhòngsūn returned,
and said:
"If Qìngfǔ is not removed,
the troubles of Lǔ will not cease."
The duke said:
"How can we remove him?"
He replied:
"If the troubles do not cease,
he will bring about his own downfall.
May you, my lord, wait for it!"
The duke said:
"Can Lǔ be taken?"
He replied:
"It cannot.
It still upholds the rites of Zhōu.
The rites of Zhōu
are the foundation.
I have heard it said:
'When a state is about to perish,
its foundation must first collapse,
and then the branches and leaves follow.'
Lǔ has not abandoned the rites of Zhōu,
and cannot be moved.
May you, my lord, strive to pacify the troubles of Lǔ
and befriend it.
Befriend those with ritual,
rely on the stable and strong,
sow discord among the divided,
overthrow the benighted and chaotic—
these are the tools of a hegemon or king."
B4.1.6 The marquis of Jìn created two armies.
The duke commanded the upper army,
and the heir apparent Shēnshēng commanded the lower army.
Zhào Sù drove the chariot,
Bì Wàn served as the right-hand guard,
and they destroyed Gěng, destroyed Huò, and destroyed Wèi.
Upon returning,
they built a city at Qūwò for the heir apparent,
granted Zhào Sù Gěng,
granted Bì Wàn Wèi,
and made them grand officers.
Shì Wěi said:
"The heir apparent will not be established.
Dividing off a capital city for him,
and giving him the position of a minister,
he is first brought to the extreme,
so how can he still be established?
It would be better for him to flee,
and not let the crime reach him.
To become like Wú Tàibó,
would that not be acceptable?
He would still have a good name,
compared with meeting disaster.
Moreover, the proverb says:
'If the heart is without flaw,
why worry about having no home?'
If Heaven blesses the heir apparent,
would he not be without Jìn?"
Bǔ Yǎn said:
"The descendants of Bì Wàn will surely be great.
Wàn
is a full number;
Wèi
is a great name.
To begin the reward with this
is Heaven opening the way.
The Son of Heaven is called 'the myriad people,'
the feudal lords are called 'the ten thousand people.'
Now his name is great,
and he follows a full number,
he is sure to have a multitude."
Earlier,
Bì Wàn divined by milfoil about serving in Jìn,
and encountered Zhūn changing to Bǐ
Xīn Liào interpreted it,
and said:
"Auspicious.
Zhūn means firmness, Bǐ means entry,
what could be more auspicious than this?
He is sure to flourish.
Zhèn becomes earth,
the chariot follows the horse,
the feet stand on it,
the elder brother nurtures it,
the mother covers it,
the multitude returns to it,
the six forms do not change,
united and able to be firm,
peaceful and able to kill,
this is the hexagram of a duke or marquis.
The descendants of a duke or marquis
are sure to return to their beginnings."
A4.2 "The Classic of the Second Year of Mǐngōng"
A4.2.1 In the second year, in spring,
in the king's first month,
the men of Qí moved Yáng.
A4.2.2 In summer, in the fifth month, on the Yǐyǒu day,
the auspicious Dì sacrifice was performed to Duke Zhuāng.
A4.2.3 In autumn, in the eighth month, on the Xīnchǒu day,
the duke died.
A4.2.4 In the ninth month,
the lady, Jiāng Shì, fled to Zhū.
A4.2.5 The duke's son, Qìngfù, fled to Jǔ.
A4.2.6 In winter,
Gāo Zǐ of Qí came to make a covenant.
A4.2.7 In the twelfth month,
the Dí entered Wèi.
A4.2.8 Zhèng abandoned its army.
B4.2 The Commentary, Second Year of Duke Mǐn
B4.2.1 In the second year, in spring,
the Earl of Guó defeated the Quǎnróng at the bend of the Wèi River.
Zhōu Zhīqiáo said:
"To receive emolument without virtue
is calamity.
Calamity is about to arrive."
Thereupon he fled to Jìn.
B4.2.2 In summer,
the auspicious Dì sacrifice was performed to Duke Zhuāng;
it was premature.
B4.2.3 Formerly,
the duke's tutor seized the fields of Bǔ Yǐ,
and the duke did not stop him.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the Xīnchǒu day,
Gòngzhòng had Bǔ Yǐ assassinate the duke at the Wǔ Gate.
Chéng Jì took Duke Xí to Zhū.
Gòngzhòng fled to Jǔ.
Then they returned,
and established him.
They sent bribes to Jǔ to demand Gòngzhòng,
and the men of Jǔ sent him back.
When they reached Mì,
he sent the duke's son, Yú, to plead.
It was not permitted,
and he went weeping.
Gòngzhòng said:
