A9.1 *The Classic Text of the First Year of Duke Xiāng*
A9.1.1 First year, spring,
the royal first month,
the Duke ascended the throne.
A9.1.2 Zhòngsūn Miè met with Luán Yǎn of Jìn,
Huà Yuán of Sòng,
Níng Zhí of Wèi,
the people of Cáo,
the people of Jǔ,
the people of Zhū,
the people of Téng,
and the people of Xuē to besiege Péngchéng of Sòng.
A9.1.3 Summer,
Hán Jué of Jìn led troops to attack Zhèng,
Zhòngsūn Miè met with Cuī Zhù of Qí,
the people of Cáo,
the people of Zhū,
and the people of Qǐ and stationed at Zēng.
A9.1.4 Autumn,
Prince Rénfū of Chǔ led troops to invade Sòng.
A9.1.5 In the ninth month, on Xīnyǒu,
the Heavenly King passed away.
A9.1.6 The Viscount of Zhū came for an audience.
A9.1.7 Winter,
the Marquis of Wèi sent Gōngsūn Piào to come on a friendly mission.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Xún Yīng to come on a friendly mission.
B9.1 *The Commentary Text of the First Year of Duke Xiāng*
B9.1.1 First year, spring, on Jǐhài,
they besieged Péngchéng of Sòng.
It was not Sòng territory,
it is recorded retrospectively.
At this time, they were attacking Lǔ Shí on behalf of Sòng,
therefore it is referred to as Sòng,
and also to not elevate the rebels,
it is called the intention of Sòng.
Péngchéng surrendered to Jìn,
the people of Jìn took the five great officers of Sòng
who were in Péngchéng and returned,
placing them at Hùqiū.
The people of Qí did not join the siege of Péngchéng,
the people of Jìn considered this an offense.
In the second month,
Prince Guāng of Qí became a hostage in Jìn.
B9.1.2 Summer, fifth month,
Hán Jué and Xún Yǎn of Jìn led the troops of the feudal lords to attack Zhèng,
entered its outer city,
and defeated its infantry at Wěishàng.
At this time, the troops of the eastern feudal lords were stationed at Zēng,
awaiting the Jìn army.
The Jìn army, from Zhèng, together with the troops from Zēng, invaded Chǔ's Jiāo and Yí, and Chén.
The Marquis of Jìn and the Marquis of Wèi stationed at Qī,
to provide support.
B9.1.3 Autumn,
Zǐ Xīn of Chǔ rescued Zhèng,
and invaded Sòng's Lǚ and Liú.
Zǐ Rán of Zhèng invaded Sòng,
and took Quǎnqiū.
B9.1.4 In the ninth month,
the Viscount of Zhū came for an audience,
which was according to propriety.
B9.1.5 Winter,
Zǐ Shū of Wèi and Zhì Wǔzǐ of Jìn came on a friendly mission,
which was according to propriety.
Whenever a feudal lord ascends the throne,
small states come to court,
great states send missions,
to continue friendship, establish trust,
discuss affairs, and remedy deficiencies,
these are the great aspects of propriety.
A9.2 *The Classic Text of the Second Year of Duke Xiāng*
A9.2.1 Second year, spring,
the royal first month,
they buried King Jiǎn.
A9.2.2 The army of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
A9.2.3 Summer, fifth month, on Gēngyín,
Lady Jiāngshì passed away.
A9.2.4 Sixth month, on Gēngchén,
Earl Gùn of Zhèng died.
A9.2.5 The army of Jìn,
the army of Sòng,
and Níng Zhí of Wèi invaded Zhèng.
A9.2.6 Autumn, seventh month,
Zhòngsūn Miè met with Xún Yīng of Jìn,
Huà Yuán of Sòng,
Sūn Línfǔ of Wèi,
the people of Cáo,
and the people of Zhū at Qī.
A9.2.7 On Jǐchǒu,
we buried our lesser ruler, Qí Jiāng.
A9.2.8 Shūsūn Bào went to Sòng.
A9.2.9 Winter,
Zhòngsūn Miè met with Xún Yīng of Jìn,
Cuī Zhù of Qí,
Huà Yuán of Sòng,
Sūn Línfǔ of Wèi,
the people of Cáo,
the people of Zhū,
the people of Téng,
the people of Xuē,
and the people of Xiǎozhū at Qī,
and then fortified Hǔláo.
A9.2.10 Chǔ executed its great officer, Prince Shēn.
B9.2 *The Commentary Text of the Second Year of Duke Xiāng*
B9.2.1 Second year, spring,
the army of Zhèng invaded Sòng,
on the orders of Chǔ.
B9.2.2 The Marquis of Qí attacked Lái,
the people of Lái sent Zhèng Yúzǐ to bribe Sùshā Wèi with selected horses and oxen,
one hundred of each,
and the Qí army then withdrew.
The gentleman therefore knew why Duke Líng of Qí was given
the posthumous title "Líng".
B9.2.3 Summer,
Qí Jiāng passed away.
Earlier,
Mù Jiāng had ordered the selection of fine catalpa wood,
to make her own inner coffin and a eulogy zither,
Jì Wénzǐ took them to bury her.
The gentleman said:
"This is contrary to propriety.
Propriety admits no inversion.
A wife
is one who serves her mother-in-law.
To harm the mother-in-law to complete the wife's arrangements,
there is no greater inversion than this.
The *Book of Songs* says:
'Only the wise man,
when told good words,
follows virtuous conduct.'
Jì Sūn in this was unwise.
Moreover, Lady Jiāng
was the ruler's grandmother.
The *Book of Songs* says:
'We make the spirits and the sweet wine,
to present to our ancestors, male and female,
to complete all the rites,
and bring down blessings in full measure.'"
B9.2.4 The Marquis of Qí sent the various Jiāng women
and wives of the same clan to attend the funeral,
and summoned the Viscount of Lái.
The Viscount of Lái did not attend,
so Yàn Ruò fortified Dōngyáng to pressure him.
B9.2.5 Duke Chéng of Zhèng was ill,
Zǐ Sì requested to shift the burden to Jìn.
The Duke said:
"The ruler of Chǔ, because of Zhèng,
personally gathered arrows in his eye,
it was not for another's responsibility,
but for me.
If we betray him,
this is to discard his effort and his word,
who then would befriend me?
To spare me,
it is up to you few gentlemen."
In autumn, in the seventh month, on Gēngchén,
the Earl of Zhèng, Gùn, died.
At that time, Zǐhǎn was in charge of the state,
Zǐsì administered the government,
and Zǐguó was the Minister of War.
The army of Jìn invaded Zhèng.
The various great officers wished to follow Jìn.
Zǐsì said:
"The official orders have not yet been changed."
They met at Qì,
to deliberate on the matter of Zhèng.
Mèng Xiànzǐ said:
"I request that we fortify Hǔláo to pressure Zhèng."
Zhì Wǔzǐ said:
"Excellent.
At the meeting of Zēng,
you, sir, heard the words of Cuīzǐ,
and now he does not come.
That Téng, Xuē, and Xiǎo Zhū did not arrive
was all due to Qí.
My ruler's worries are not only about Zhèng.
Yīng will report back to my ruler,
and make a request to Qí.
If the request is granted and we are informed,
it will be your merit, sir.
If the request is not granted,
military action will be directed against Qí.
Your request, sir,
is a blessing for the various lords.
How could only my ruler rely on it?"
B9.2.6 Mù Shū paid a courtesy visit to Sòng,
to announce the accession of the new ruler.
B9.2.7 In winter,
they met again at Qì.
Cuī Wǔzǐ of Qí and the great officers of Téng, Xuē, and Xiǎo Zhū all attended the meeting,
due to the words of Zhì Wǔzǐ.
Thereupon they fortified Hǔláo.
The people of Zhèng then made peace.
B9.2.8 The Chǔ nobleman Gōngzǐ Shēn served as Right Minister of War.
He received many bribes from small states,
in order to pressure Zǐchóng and Zǐxīn.
The people of Chǔ killed him.
Therefore, the record states:
"Chǔ killed its great officer Gōngzǐ Shēn."
A9.3 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Third Year of Duke Xiāng
A9.3.1 In the third year, in spring,
the Chǔ nobleman Gōngzǐ Yīngqí led an army to attack Wú.
A9.3.2 The Duke went to Jìn.
A9.3.3 In summer, in the fourth month, on Rénxū,
the Duke and the Marquis of Jìn made a covenant at Chángchū.
A9.3.4 The Duke arrived from Jìn.
A9.3.5 In the sixth month,
the Duke met with the Viscount of Shàn,
the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Zhèng,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
the Viscount of Zhū,
and the heir apparent Guāng of Qí.
On Jǐwèi,
they made a covenant together at Jīzé.
A9.3.6 The Marquis of Chén sent Yuán Qiáo to the meeting.
A9.3.7 On Wùyín,
Shūsūn Bào and the great officers of the various lords made a covenant with Yuán Qiáo of Chén.
A9.3.8 In autumn,
the Duke arrived from the meeting.
A9.3.9 In winter,
Xún Yīng of Jìn led an army to attack Xǔ.
B9.3 The Commentary of Zuo, Third Year of Duke Xiāng
B9.3.1 In the third year, in spring,
Zǐchóng of Chǔ attacked Wú,
raising a select army.
He captured Jiūzī,
and advanced to Héngshān.
He sent Dèng Liào to lead three hundred men in linked armor
and three thousand in silk-quilted armor
to invade Wú.
The men of Wú intercepted and attacked them,
capturing Dèng Liào.
Those who managed to escape
were only eighty in linked armor and three hundred in silk-quilted armor.
When Zǐchóng returned,
after the customary three-day drinking ceremony to celebrate his return,
the men of Wú attacked Chǔ,
and captured Jià.
Jià
was an excellent city,
and Dèng Liào
was also an excellent man of Chǔ.
The gentleman says:
"In this campaign, Zǐchóng
gained less than he lost."
The people of Chǔ on this account blamed Zǐchóng.
Zǐchóng was distressed by this,
and then suffered a heart ailment and died.
B9.3.2 The Duke went to Jìn,
for his first court visit.
In summer,
they made a covenant at Chángchū.
Mèng Xiànzǐ acted as assistant.
The Duke bowed his head to the ground.
Zhì Wǔzǐ said:
"The Son of Heaven is present,
and yet you, my lord, demean yourself by bowing your head to the ground.
My ruler is alarmed."
Mèng Xiànzǐ said:
"Because our humble state is situated in the eastern borderlands,
and lies close to our enemies,
my ruler looks to you, my lord, for support.
How dare he not bow his head to the ground?"
B9.3.3 Because Zhèng had submitted,
and also wishing to cultivate friendly relations with Wú,
Jìn intended to assemble the various lords.
They sent Shì Gào to announce to Qí:
"My ruler has sent Gào,
because the year is troubled and we are unprepared for unforeseen events.
My ruler wishes to meet with one or two of his brothers,
to deliberate on matters of discord.
I request that you, my lord, attend,
and have Gào beg for a covenant."
The Marquis of Qí wished not to consent,
but found it difficult to appear discordant,
so he made a covenant outside Ér.
B9.3.4 Qí Xī requested to retire due to age.
The Marquis of Jìn asked him about a successor.
He recommended Xiè Hú,
who was his personal enemy.
Just as he was about to be appointed, he died.
The Marquis asked again.
He replied:
"Wǔ would be suitable."
At that time, Yángshé Zhí had died.
The Marquis of Jìn said:
"Who can replace him?"
He replied:
"Chì would be suitable."
Thereupon, they made Qí Wǔ Commandant of the Central Army,
with Yángshé Chì as his assistant.
The gentleman says of Qí Xī:
"In this he was able to promote the worthy.
Recommending his enemy
was not flattery;
establishing his son
was not favoritism;
promoting his subordinate
was not factionalism.
The Book of Shāng says:
'Without partiality, without faction,
the King's way is broad and level.'
This describes Qí Xī, does it not?
Xiè Hú was recommended,
Qí Wǔ obtained his position,
and Bó Huá obtained his office.
Establishing one office and achieving three good things—
this is being able to promote the worthy.
Only one who is worthy himself
can promote those of his own kind.
The Odes say:
'Only because he possesses it himself,
therefore he resembles it.'
Qí Xī possessed this."
B9.3.5 In the sixth month,
the Duke met with Viscount Qīng of Shàn and the various lords.
On Jǐwèi,
they made a covenant together at Jīzé.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Xún Huì to meet the Viscount of Wú north of the Huái River,
but the Viscount of Wú did not arrive.
B9.3.6 Zǐxīn of Chǔ became Prime Minister.
He encroached upon and desired the possessions of small states.
Duke Chéng of Chén sent Yuán Qiáo to the meeting to seek peace.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Hé Zǔfù to announce to the various lords.
In autumn,
Shūsūn Bào and the great officers of the various lords made a covenant with Yuán Qiáo of Chén,
because Chén requested to submit.
B9.3.7 The younger brother of the Marquis of Jìn, Yánggān,
disrupted the ranks at Qūliáng.
Wèi Jiàng executed his charioteer.
The Marquis of Jìn was angry.
He said to Yángshé Chì:
"Assembling the various lords
is for the sake of glory.
That Yánggān was shamed—
what disgrace could be greater than this?
You must kill Wèi Jiàng,
without fail!"
He replied:
"Wèi Jiàng has no disloyal intent.
In serving his ruler he does not avoid hardship,
and if guilty he does not flee punishment.
He will likely come to explain himself;
why trouble to summon him?"
As he finished speaking,
Wèi Jiàng arrived,
handed a letter to the attendant,
and was about to fall upon his sword.
Shì Fáng and Zhāng Lǎo stopped him.
The duke read his letter,
which said:
"Previously, when Your Lordship was short of servants,
you appointed me as Marshal.
I have heard that
'for an army, obedience is valor;
in military affairs,
to die without offense is respect.'
Your Lordship assembled the feudal lords;
how dare I not be respectful?
If Your Lordship's army lacked valor,
or your officers lacked respect,
no crime could be greater.
I feared this would lead to my death,
and it involved Yáng Gān,
so I cannot escape guilt.
Failing to give proper instruction,
resulting in the use of the axe—
my crime is grave.
How dare I disobey and anger Your Lordship's heart?
I beg to return and die before the Minister of Justice."
The duke rushed out barefoot and said:
"My words
were spoken out of affection;
your punishment
was a matter of military discipline.
I have a younger brother
whom I could not instruct properly,
causing him to violate the great command—
this is my fault.
Do not compound my error;
I venture to make this request."
The Marquis of Jìn considered Wèi Jiàng capable
of using punishments to assist the people.
Upon returning from the campaign,
he feasted him with full ceremony
and made him assistant commander of the New Army.
Zhāng Lǎo was made Marshal of the Central Army,
and Shì Fù was made Scout Commander.
B9.3.8 The Chǔ Marshal, Prince Hé Jì, invaded Chén
because Chén had rebelled.
B9.3.9 Lord Líng of Xǔ served Chǔ,
so he did not attend the meeting at Jīzé.
In winter,
Zhì Wǔzǐ of Jìn led an army to attack Xǔ.
A9.4 *The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 4 of Duke Xiāng*
A9.4.1 In the fourth year, spring,
the third month of the royal calendar, on Jǐyǒu,
Marquis Wǔ of Chén died.
A9.4.2 In summer,
Shūsūn Bào went to Jìn.
A9.4.3 In autumn, the seventh month, on Wùzǐ,
Lady Sìshì died.
A9.4.4 Burial of Duke Chéng of Chén.
A9.4.5 In the eighth month, on Xīnhài,
we buried our late ruler's consort, Dìng Sì.
A9.4.6 In winter,
the duke went to Jìn.
A9.4.7 The people of Chén besieged Dùn.
B9.4 *The Commentary of Zuo, Year 4 of Duke Xiāng*
B9.4.1 In the fourth year, spring,
the army of Chǔ, because of Chén's rebellion,
was still at Fányáng.
Hán Xiànzǐ was troubled by this
and said at court:
"King Wén led the rebellious states of Yīn to serve Zhòu—
this was because he understood the times.
Now we act contrary to this;
how difficult it is!"
B9.4.2 In the third month,
Duke Chéng of Chén died.
The people of Chǔ were about to attack Chén,
but upon hearing of the mourning, they stopped.
The people of Chén did not obey their orders.
Zāng Wǔzhòng heard of this
and said:
"If Chén does not submit to Chǔ,
it will surely perish.
When a great state acts with propriety
and yet they do not submit—
even for a great state there would be blame,
let alone a small one?"
In summer,
Péng Míng of Chǔ invaded Chén
because Chén had been discourteous.
B9.4.3 Mù Shū (Shūsūn Bào) went to Jìn
to return Zhì Wǔzǐ's courtesy visit.
The Marquis of Jìn entertained him.
When the metal instruments played the three pieces of *Sìxià*,
he did not bow.
When the musicians sang the three pieces of *Wénwáng*,
he again did not bow.
When they sang the three pieces of *Lùmíng*,
he bowed three times.
Hán Xiànzǐ sent the messenger Zǐ Yuán to ask him,
saying:
"You have condescended to visit our humble state on your ruler's orders.
We have used the rites of our former rulers,
accompanied by music,
to honor you.
Yet you neglect the greater
and repeatedly bow for the lesser.
May I ask what ritual this is?"
He replied:
"The *Sānxià*
is what the Son of Heaven uses to entertain the leading feudal lords;
I dare not presume to hear it.
*Wénwáng*
is music for when two rulers meet;
I dare not participate.
*Lùmíng*
is what you, my lord, use to praise my humble ruler;
how dare I not bow in gratitude?
*Sìmǔ*
is what you, my lord, use to reward your envoy;
how dare I not bow repeatedly?
*Huánghuáng Zhě Huá*
is where you, my lord, instruct your envoy, saying:
'You must consult comprehensively.'
I have heard that:
'Consulting the good is called *zī*;
consulting relatives is called *xún*;
consulting about rites is called *duó*;
consulting about affairs is called *zōu*;
consulting about difficulties is called *móu*.'
I have gained five good things;
how dare I not bow repeatedly?"
B9.4.4 In autumn,
Dìng Sì died.
She was not laid in the ancestral temple,
had no inner coffin,
and no post-burial sacrifice was held.
Jiàng Qìng said to Jì Wénzǐ:
"You are the chief minister,
yet the funeral of the ruler's consort is not properly conducted—
this is not seeing your ruler's affairs to completion.
When the ruler grows up,
who will bear the blame?"
Earlier,
Jì Sūn had planted six catalpa trees for himself
east of the gate at Púpǔ.
Jiàng Qìng requested timber,
and Jì Sūn said:
"Take whatever."
Jiàng Qìng used the catalpas from Púpǔ,
and Jì Sūn did not stop him.
The gentleman remarks:
"As the *Record* says:
'He who often acts without propriety
will surely bring it upon himself'—
this is what it means!"
B9.4.5 In winter,
the duke went to Jìn to receive administrative instructions.
The Marquis of Jìn entertained the duke,
and the duke requested that Zēng be attached to Lǔ.
The Marquis of Jìn refused.
Mèng Xiànzǐ said:
"Though our humble ruler is close to his enemies,
he wishes steadfastly to serve you, my lord,
and not to fail your official commands.
Zēng pays no tribute to your Marshal,
yet your officers issue commands to our humble state morning and night.
Our state is small and narrow;
if we fall short and incur guilt,
our humble ruler therefore wishes to seek assistance."
The Marquis of Jìn agreed.
B9.4.6 The people of Chǔ used Dùn to create trouble for Chén
and then invaded it,
so the people of Chén besieged Dùn.
B9.4.7 Jiāfù, ruler of Wúzhōng, sent Mèng Lè to Jìn,
and through Wèi Zhuāngzǐ
presented tiger and leopard skins
to request peace with all the Róng tribes.
The Marquis of Jìn said:
"The Róng and Dí have no affection and are greedy;
it would be better to attack them."
Wèi Jiàng said:
"The feudal lords have newly submitted,
Chén has newly come to make peace,
and they will observe our actions.
If we are virtuous,
they will be amicable;
if not,
they will become disloyal and turn away.
To exhaust our troops in campaigns against the Róng,
while Chǔ attacks Chén,
we will certainly be unable to rescue them,
thus abandoning Chén.
The various Huá states will surely rebel.
The Róng are like beasts.
To gain the Róng but lose the Huá—
is that not unacceptable!
The 'Xià Xùn' says:
'There was Hòu Yì of Yǒuqióng.'"
The Duke said:
"What about Hòu Yì?"
He replied:
"In the past, when the Xià dynasty was in decline,
Hòu Yì moved from Chú to Qióngshí,
and relying on the support of the Xià people, he usurped the Xià government.
Relying on his skill in archery,
he did not attend to the affairs of the people,
but indulged excessively in hunting wild beasts.
He dismissed Wǔ Luó, Bó Yīn, Xióng Kūn, and Méng Yǔ,
and employed Hán Zhuó.
Hán Zhuó
was a slanderous son of the Bómíng clan.
Bómíng Hòu Hán expelled him,
but Yí Yì took him in,
trusted him, and employed him,
making him his chief minister.
Zhuó flattered and pleased within the palace,
and distributed bribes outside,
deceiving and manipulating the people,
while deluding Yì with hunting.
He cultivated treachery and wickedness,
to seize the state and its ruling house,
and both inside and outside, all submitted to him.
Yì still did not reform.
As he was returning from the hunt,
his household retainers killed and cooked him,
and served his flesh to his son.
His son could not bear to eat it,
and died at the Qióng Gate.
Mí fled to the Yǒugé clan.
Zhuó took over Yì's household,
and begot Ào and Yì.
Relying on his slander, wickedness, deceit, and falseness,
and showing no virtue toward the people,
he sent Ào with an army
to destroy the Zhēnguàn and Zhēnxún clans.
He settled Ào in Guō,
and settled Yì in Gé.
Mí, from the Yǒugé clan,
gathered the remnants of the two states,
destroyed Zhuó, and established Shào Kāng.
Shào Kāng destroyed Ào in Guō,
Hòu Zhù destroyed Yì in Gé.
Thus Yǒuqióng perished,
because they lost the support of the people.
In the past, during the Zhōu,
when Xīn Jiǎ was Grand Historian,
he commanded all officials
to admonish the king about his faults.
In the 'Admonition of the Gamekeeper' it says:
'Vast are the traces of Yǔ,
who divided the land into nine provinces,
and opened up the nine roads.
The people have their homes and temples,
the beasts have their lush grasses;
each has its proper place,
and thus virtue is not disturbed.
But the Emperor Yí Yì
was obsessed with wild beasts,
forgot the troubles of his state,
and thought only of his stags and does.
Hunting should not be overdone,
lest it not enlarge the house of Xià.
I, your servant in charge of the wilds,
dare to report this to your attendants.'
Such is the 'Admonition of the Gamekeeper'—
can we not take warning from it?"
At that time, the Marquis of Jìn was fond of hunting,
hence Wèi Jiàng spoke of this.
The Duke said:
"Then is there nothing better than making peace with the Róng?"
He replied:
"Making peace with the Róng has five advantages:
The Róng and Dí dwell in one place after another,
they value goods and despise land,
so land can be purchased from them—
this is the first.
The border regions will not be alarmed,
the people will be at ease in their fields,
and the farmers will achieve success—
this is the second.
If the Róng and Dí serve Jìn,
the four neighbors will be shaken,
and the feudal lords will be awed and drawn to us—
this is the third.
By using virtue to pacify the Róng,
the army will not be toiled,
and armor and weapons will not be worn out—
this is the fourth.
Taking warning from Hòu Yì,
and employing virtue and proper measures,
those far off will come, and those nearby will be at peace—
this is the fifth.
May Your Lordship consider it!"
The Duke was pleased,
and sent Wèi Jiàng to make a covenant with the various Róng tribes.
He attended to the affairs of the people,
and hunted only in season.
B9.4.8 In winter, the tenth month,
men of Zhū and Jǔ attacked Zēng.
Zāng Hé went to rescue Zēng,
invaded Zhū,
but was defeated at Hútái.
Those of the capital who went to meet the funeral procession
all wore their hair in a mourning knot.
Thus in Lǔ they began to wear the mourning knot.
The people of the capital chanted about it:
"Zāng in his fox-fur robe,
caused our defeat at Hútái.
Our lord, a mere youth,
employs these dwarfs.
Dwarfs, dwarfs,
caused our defeat by Zhū."
A9.5 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Fifth Year of Duke Xiāng
A9.5.1 Fifth year, spring,
the Duke arrived from Jìn.
A9.5.2 Summer,
the Earl of Zhèng sent his son, Fā, to come on a friendly mission.
A9.5.3 Shūsūn Bào
and Wū, heir of Zēng, went to Jìn.
A9.5.4 Zhòngsūn Miè
and Sūn Línfǔ of Wèi met with Wú at Shàndào.
A9.5.5 Autumn,
the great rain sacrifice was held.
A9.5.6 Chǔ put to death its great officer, Prince Rénfū.
A9.5.7 The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Zhèng,
the Earl of Cáo,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
the Viscount of Zhū,
the Viscount of Téng,
the Earl of Xuē,
Guāng, heir of Qí,
a man of Wú,
and a man of Zēng, at Qī.
A9.5.8 The Duke arrived from the meeting.
A9.5.9 Winter,
they garrisoned Chén.
A9.5.10 Prince Zhēn of Chǔ led an army to attack Chén.
A9.5.11 The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Zhèng,
the Earl of Cáo,
and Guāng, heir of Qí, to rescue Chén.
A9.5.12 In the twelfth month,
the Duke arrived from the rescue of Chén.
A9.5.13 On Xīnwèi,
Jìsūn Xíngfǔ died.
B9.5 The Commentary of Zuo, Fifth Year of Duke Xiāng
B9.5.1 Fifth year, spring,
the Duke arrived from Jìn.
B9.5.2 The King sent Wángshū Chénshēng to complain to Jìn about the Róng,
but the men of Jìn detained him.
Shì Fáng went to the capital,
to explain that Wángshū was double-dealing with the Róng.
B9.5.3 Summer,
Zǐ Guó of Zhèng came on a friendly mission,
to establish relations on behalf of his new ruler.
B9.5.4 Mù Shū (Shūsūn Bào) met with the crown prince of Zēng in Jìn,
to complete the affiliation of Zēng (to Lǔ).
The record says
"Shūsūn Bào and Crown Prince Wū of Zēng went to Jìn",
indicating they were treated as equivalent to Lǔ's great officers.
B9.5.5 The Viscount of Wú sent Shòu Yuè to Jìn,
to apologize for not attending the meeting at Jīzé,
and to request to join the friendly relations among the feudal lords.
The men of Jìn were about to convene a meeting of the feudal lords for him,
and had Lǔ and Wèi first meet with Wú,
to inform them of the meeting date.
Therefore, Mèng Xiànzǐ (Mèng Xiànzǐ) and Sūn Wénzǐ (Sūn Línfù)
met with Wú at Shàndào.
B9.5.6 In autumn,
there was a great rain-seeking sacrifice (yú),
due to drought.
B9.5.7 The men of Chǔ investigated the reason for Chén's rebellion,
saying:
"It was because the Lingyǐn Zǐ Xīn (Gōngzǐ Rènfū) truly encroached with desires."
They then killed him.
The record says
"Chǔ killed its great officer Gōngzǐ Rènfū",
because of his greed.
The gentleman says
"King Gòng of Chǔ in this did not apply punishments correctly.
The Odes say:
'The way of Zhōu is straight and upright,
My heart is anxious and troubled.
Deliberating affairs without good results,
Gather men to come and settle it.'
He himself was without good faith,
yet killed men to gratify himself,
is this not difficult?
The Book of Xià says:
'Accomplish trustworthiness, accomplish achievements.'"
B9.5.8 In the ninth month, on the bǐngwǔ day,
a covenant was made at Qī,
to meet with Wú,
and also to order the defense of Chén.
Mù Shū (Shūsūn Bào) considered the affiliation of Zēng to be disadvantageous,
and had the great officers of Zēng receive orders at the meeting.
B9.5.9 Chǔ's Zǐ Náng became Lingyǐn.
Fàn Xuānzǐ (Shì Xiè) said:
"We have lost Chén.
The men of Chǔ have punished disloyalty
and established Zǐ Náng,
he will certainly change his conduct,
and swiftly punish Chén.
Chén is near to Chǔ,
its people will be in constant urgency,
can they not go over?
To have Chén
is not our affair;
it is only acceptable to not have it."
In winter,
the feudal lords defended Chén.
Zǐ Náng attacked Chén.
In the eleventh month, on the jiǎwǔ day,
they met at Chéngdì to rescue it.
B9.5.10 Jì Wénzǐ (Jì Sūnxíngfù) died.
When the great officers entered to lay him in the coffin,
the duke was in position.
The steward prepared the household vessels
for the burial provisions.
He had no concubines clothed in silk,
no horses fed on grain,
no stored gold or jade,
no duplicate sets of vessels.
The gentleman therefore knew
that Jì Wénzǐ was loyal to the ducal house:
"He served three rulers,
yet had no private accumulation,
can he not be called loyal?"
A9.6 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 6 of Duke Xiāng
A9.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring,
in the king's third month, on the rénwǔ day,
the Earl of Qǐ, Gūróng, died.
A9.6.2 In summer,
Huà Ruò of Sòng came fleeing.
A9.6.3 In autumn,
they buried Duke Huán of Qǐ.
A9.6.4 The Viscount of Téng came to court.
A9.6.5 The men of Jǔ extinguished Zēng.
A9.6.6 In winter,
Shūsūn Bào went to Zhū.
A9.6.7 Jìsūn Sù went to Jìn.
A9.6.8 In the twelfth month,
the Marquis of Qí extinguished Lái.
B9.6 The Commentary of Zuo, Year 6 of Duke Xiāng
B9.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring,
Duke Huán of Qǐ died.
For the first time, the death announcement used his personal name,
because he was in covenant.
B9.6.2 Huà Ruò of Sòng and Yuè Zhòu (Zǐ Dàng) were familiar with each other from childhood,
teased each other when grown,
and also slandered each other.
Zǐ Dàng (Yuè Zhòu) became angry,
and in court fettered Huà Ruò with a bow.
Duke Píng saw it,
and said:
"The Marshal of War fettered in court,
it will be difficult to achieve victory."
He then banished him.
In summer,
Huà Ruò of Sòng came fleeing.
Sīchéng Zǐ Hǎn (Xiàng Tú) said:
"The same offense with different punishments,
is not proper penalty.
To arbitrarily humiliate in court,
what offense is greater than this?"
He also banished Zǐ Dàng.
Zǐ Dàng shot an arrow at Zǐ Hǎn's gate,
saying:
"In a few days you will follow me!"
Zǐ Hǎn treated him as well as before.
B9.6.3 In autumn,
Duke Chéng of Téng came to court,
for the first time paying court to our duke.
B9.6.4 The men of Jǔ extinguished Zēng,
because Zēng relied on bribes.
B9.6.5 In winter,
Mù Shū (Shūsūn Bào) went to Zhū
on a courtesy visit,
and to renew peace.
B9.6.6 The men of Jìn came
to reproach
because of the affair of Zēng,
saying:
"Why did you let Zēng perish?"
Jì Wǔzǐ (Jìsūn Sù) went to Jìn for an audience,
and to receive orders.
B9.6.7 In the eleventh month,
the Marquis of Qí extinguished Lái,
because Lái relied on stratagems.
When Zǐ Guó of Zhèng came on a courtesy visit,
in the fourth month,
Yàn Ruò walled Dōngyáng,
and then besieged Lái.
On the jiǎyín day,
they built mounds encircling the city,
reaching up to the battlements.
In the month when Duke Huán of Qǐ died,
on the yǐwèi day,
Wáng Qiū led troops and, together with Zhèng Yúzǐ and the army of Táng, attacked the Qí army,
and the Qí army greatly defeated them.
On the dīngwèi day,
they entered Lái.
Duke Gòng of Lái, Fú Róu, fled to Táng.
Zhèng Yúzǐ and Wáng Qiū fled to Jǔ,
and the men of Jǔ killed them.
In the fourth month,
Chén Wúyǔ presented the ancestral vessels of Lái in the temple of Duke Xiāng.
Yàn Ruò besieged Táng,
and in the eleventh month, on the bǐngchén day, extinguished it.
They moved the people of Lái to Ní.
Gāo Hòu and Cuī Zhù apportioned their lands.
A9.7 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 7 of Duke Xiāng
A9.7.1 In the seventh year, in spring,
the Viscount of Tán came to court.
A9.7.2 In summer, in the fourth month,
they divined three times for the suburban sacrifice,
and it was not favorable,
so they released the sacrificial animal.
A9.7.3 The Viscount of Xiǎo Zhū came to court.
A9.7.4 They walled Fèi.
A9.7.5 In autumn,
Jìsūn Sù went to Wèi.
A9.7.6 In the eighth month,
there were locusts.
A9.7.7 In winter, in the tenth month,
the Marquis of Wèi sent Sūn Línfù to come on a courtesy visit.
On the rénxū day,
they made a covenant with Sūn Línfù.
A9.7.8 Chǔ's Gōngzǐ Zhēn (Zǐ Náng) led troops and besieged Chén.
A9.7.9 In the twelfth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Cáo,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
and the Viscount of Zhū at Wěi.
The Earl of Zhèng, Kūnwán, was on his way to the meeting,
but before he could see the feudal lords,
on the bingxū day,
he died at Cào.
A9.7.10 The Marquis of Chén fled back to his state.
B9.7 The Commentary to the Seventh Year of Duke Xiāng
B9.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
the Viscount of Tán came to our court for an audience,
this being his first audience with our Duke.
B9.7.2 In the summer, in the fourth month,
the divination for the border sacrifice was performed three times,
but the omens were not favorable,
so the sacrificial animal was released.
Mèng Xiànzǐ said:
"It is only now that I
understand the purpose of divination by shell and by stalk.
The border sacrifice to Hòujì
is to pray for agricultural affairs.
Therefore, it is held when the insects awaken,
and after the sacrifice, plowing begins.
Now, plowing has already begun and then we divine for the sacrifice;
it is fitting that the omens are unfavorable."
B9.7.3 Nán Yí became the steward of Fèi.
Shūzhòng Zhāobó was the overseer of the tunnels,
and wishing to do good to the Jì family,
he sought to curry favor with Nán Yí.
He said to Yí:
"I request that we wall Fèi,
and I will provide you with many laborers."
Therefore, the Jì family walled Fèi.
B9.7.4 The Mù Duke of Xiǎo Zhū came to our court for an audience,
this also being his first audience with our Duke.
B9.7.5 In autumn,
Jì Wǔzǐ went to Wèi,
to return the courtesy of Zǐ Shū's diplomatic visit,
and also to apologize for the delay in the return visit,
explaining that it was not due to any duplicity.
B9.7.6 In winter, in the tenth month,
Hán Xiànzǐ of Jìn announced his retirement due to old age.
The Duke's clansman, Mùzǐ,
had a disabling illness,
and they intended to establish him [as successor].
He declined, saying:
"The *Book of Songs* says:
'Do I not go early and late?
But the path is full of dew.'
It also says:
'If you do not attend to things personally,
the common people will not trust you.'
Wújì is without talent;
to decline
would be permissible, would it not?
I request that Qǐ be established.
He associated with Tián Sū,
and Tián Sū said of him, 'He loves benevolence.'
The *Book of Songs* says:
'Quietly fulfill your duties,
love what is upright and correct.
The spirits, hearing this,
will grant you great happiness.'
Compassion for the people is virtue,
uprightness is correctness,
correcting the crooked is straightness,
and the combination of these three constitutes benevolence.
If it is thus,
then the spirits will hear it,
and great happiness will descend upon him.
To establish him,
would that not be permissible?"
On the gēngxū day,
they had Xuānzǐ attend court,
and then Hán Xiànzǐ retired.
The Marquis of Jìn considered Hán Wújì benevolent,
and put him in charge of the Grand Masters of the ducal clan.
B9.7.7 Sūn Wénzǐ of Wèi came on a diplomatic visit,
and also to acknowledge Wǔzǐ's words,
and to renew the covenant of Sūn Huánzǐ.
When our Duke ascended the steps, he ascended at the same time.
Shūsūn Mùzǐ was acting as assistant,
and he hurried forward,
saying:
"At meetings of the feudal lords,
our humble ruler has never been behind the ruler of Wèi.
Now you, sir, do not stay behind our humble ruler;
our humble ruler does not know what fault he has committed.
Might you, sir, please be a little more composed!"
Sūnzǐ offered no apology,
nor did he show any sign of remorse.
Mù Shū said:
"Sūnzǐ is sure to perish.
To act as a ruler while being a minister,
to commit a fault and not repent,
is the root of ruin.
The *Book of Songs* says:
'Returning from court to eat,
leisurely, leisurely,'
refers to those who are compliant.
To be arrogant and yet leisurely,
is sure to lead to a fall."
B9.7.8 The Viscount of Chǔ, Zǐ Náng, besieged Chén,
and a meeting was held at Wěi to rescue it.
B9.7.9 When Duke Xī of Zhèng was heir apparent,
in the sixteenth year of Duke Chéng,
he went to Jìn with Zǐ Hǎn,
and treated him disrespectfully.
He also went to Chǔ with Zǐ Fēng,
and treated him disrespectfully as well.
When it was the first year of his reign and he went to Jìn for an audience,
Zǐ Fēng wanted to accuse him before Jìn and have him deposed,
but Zǐ Hǎn stopped him.
When he was about to attend the meeting at Wěi,
Zǐ Sì acted as his assistant,
and again he treated him disrespectfully.
An attendant remonstrated with him,
but he would not listen;
when he remonstrated again,
the Duke killed him.
When they reached Cào,
Zǐ Sì had ruffians assassinate Duke Xī at night,
and then reported to the feudal lords that he had died of a malarial illness.
The Duke [his successor] was five years old at birth,
and they supported him and established him.
B9.7.10 The people of Chén were troubled by Chǔ.
Qìng Hǔ and Qìng Yín said to the men of Chǔ:
"We will send Gōngzǐ Huáng to you,
and you can detain him."
The men of Chǔ agreed.
The two Qìng sent a message to the Marquis of Chén at the meeting,
saying:
"The men of Chǔ have detained Gōngzǐ Huáng.
If you, my lord, do not return,
your ministers, unable to bear the thought for the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temples,
fear they may have other plans."
The Marquis of Chén fled back [to his state].
A9.8 The Text of the Eighth Year of Duke Xiāng
A9.8.1 In the eighth year, in spring,
the first month of the royal calendar,
the Duke went to Jìn.
A9.8.2 In summer,
the burial of Duke Xī of Zhèng took place.
A9.8.3 The men of Zhèng invaded Cài,
and captured Cài's Gōngzǐ Xiè.
A9.8.4 Jìsūn Sù met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Earl of Zhèng,
a man of Qí,
a man of Sòng,
a man of Wèi,
and a man of Zhū at Xíngqiū.
A9.8.5 The Duke arrived from Jìn.
A9.8.6 The men of Jǔ attacked our eastern borders.
A9.8.7 In autumn, in the ninth month,
there was a great rain sacrifice.
A9.8.8 In winter,
Chǔ's Gōngzǐ Zhēn led an army to attack Zhèng.
A9.8.9 The Marquis of Jìn sent Shì Gài on a diplomatic visit to our state.
B9.8 The Commentary to the Eighth Year of Duke Xiāng
B9.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
the Duke went to Jìn,
for an audience,
and also to hear the prescribed numbers for court visits and diplomatic missions.
B9.8.2 The various Gōngzǐ of Zhèng,
because of Duke Xī's death,
plotted against Zǐ Sì.
Zǐ Sì acted before them.
In summer, on the gēngchén day of the fourth month,
he lured and killed Zǐ Hú, Zǐ Xī, Zǐ Hóu, and Zǐ Dīng.
Sūn Jī and Sūn È fled and went to Wèi.
B9.8.3 On the gēngyín day,
Zhèng's Zǐ Guó and Zǐ Ěr invaded Cài,
and captured Cài's Minister of War, Gōngzǐ Xiè.
All the people of Zhèng were pleased,
only Zǐ Chǎn was not in accord,
saying:
"A small state without civil virtue,
yet possessing military achievements,
there is no greater misfortune than this.
When the men of Chǔ come to punish us,
will we be able to avoid submitting?"
If we follow them,
the Jin army will surely arrive.
When Jin and Chu attack Zheng,
from now on, the state of Zheng will not have peace for four or five years."
Zǐ Guó angrily said to him:
"What do you know!
The state has great commands,
and there are chief ministers;
for a youth to speak of them,
he will be executed!"
B9.8.4 In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
they met at Xíngqiū,
to determine the numbers for court visits and tributes,
and had the great officers of the various lords listen to the command.
Jìsūn Sù, Qí's Gāo Hòu, Sòng's Xiàng Xū, Wèi's Níng Zhí, and a great officer of Zhū attended the meeting.
The Earl of Zheng presented captives at the meeting,
so he personally listened to the command.
The great officers are not recorded,
to honor the Marquis of Jin.
B9.8.5 The people of Jǔ attacked our eastern borders,
to demarcate the fields of Zēng.
B9.8.6 In autumn, the ninth month,
there was a great rain-seeking sacrifice,
due to drought.
B9.8.7 In winter,
Chǔ's Zǐ Náng attacked Zheng,
to punish them for invading Cài.
Zǐ Sì, Zǐ Guó, and Zǐ Ěr wished to follow Chu,
while Zǐ Kǒng, Zǐ Jiǎo, and Zǐ Zhǎn wished to await Jin.
Zǐ Sì said:
"The Zhōu Odes have a verse that says:
'Waiting for the Yellow River to clear,
how long is a human lifespan?
Divinations and consultations are many,
they only compete to weave nets.'
When plans involve many clans,
the people often dissent,
and matters increasingly fail to succeed.
The people are in distress;
let us follow Chu for now,
to relieve our people.
When the Jin army arrives,
we will follow them instead.
Respectfully presenting silks and gifts,
to await those who come,
is the way for a small state.
With sacrificial animals and jades and silks,
waiting at both borders,
to await the strong
and shelter the people thereby.
If invaders cause no harm,
and the people are not exhausted or afflicted,
is that not acceptable?"
Zǐ Zhǎn said:
"What enables a small state to serve a great one
is trust.
If a small state lacks trust,
war and chaos will arrive daily,
and its destruction will not be far off.
The trust established in five meetings,
now we are about to betray it;
even if Chu rescues us,
what use will it be?
If they become intimate with us, it will not succeed;
they desire to make us their borderlands;
we cannot follow them.
It is better to await Jin.
The ruler of Jin is currently enlightened,
his four armies have no deficiencies,
his eight ministers are harmonious,
and he will surely not abandon Zheng.
The Chu army is far away,
their provisions will soon be exhausted,
they will surely return quickly;
what is there to worry about?
Shě Zhī has heard it said:
'No staff is as good as trust.'
Strengthen our defenses to weary Chu,
rely on trust to await Jin;
is that not acceptable?"
Zǐ Sì said:
"The Odes say:
'Planners are very many,
therefore nothing is accomplished.
Speeches fill the court,
who dares take the blame?
Like consulting about a journey without walking,
therefore one cannot reach the road.'
I request to follow Chu;
Fēi will bear the blame."
Thereupon they made peace with Chu,
and sent Wángzǐ Bópián to report to Jin,
saying:
"Your lordship commanded our humble city:
'Repair your chariots and equipment,
alert your officers and troops,
to punish rebellious aggression.'
The people of Cài did not comply;
the people of our humble city dared not rest peacefully;
we gathered all our humble resources,
to attack Cài,
captured Simǎ Xiè,
and presented him at Xíngqiū.
Now Chu has come to punish us, saying:
'Why did you raise troops against Cài?'
They burned our suburban strongholds,
and pressed upon our city walls.
The multitude of our humble city,
husbands and wives, men and women,
have no leisure to rest,
as they aid each other in rescue.
Cut down and overturned,
they have nowhere to appeal.
Among the people who have died or fled,
if not their fathers or elder brothers,
then their sons or younger brothers.
These men are grieved and pained,
not knowing where to find shelter.
The people, knowing their desperate straits,
accepted a covenant with Chu.
I, the orphan, and my two or three ministers could not prevent it;
we dare not fail to report it."
Zhì Wǔzǐ had the messenger Zǐ Yuán reply to him, saying:
"Your lordship received a command from Chu,
yet did not send even a single envoy
to report to our humble ruler,
but instead settled comfortably with Chu.
What your lordship desires,
who dares oppose you?
Our humble ruler will lead the various lords to meet you beneath the city walls.
May your lordship consider this."
B9.8.8 Jìn's Fàn Xuānzǐ came on a friendly visit,
and also to acknowledge our ruler's previous visit,
and to announce that troops would be used against Zheng.
Our ruler hosted a banquet for him.
Xuānzǐ recited 'Plucking the Plum.'
Jì Wǔzǐ said:
"Who would dare delay?
Now, comparing to plants and trees,
our humble ruler is to your lordship
as fragrance is to you.
Joyfully we receive your command;
what question of timing is there?"
Wǔzǐ recited 'Horned Bow.'
As the guest was about to leave,
Wǔzǐ recited 'Vermilion Bow.'
Xuānzǐ said:
"At the battle of Chéngpú,
our former ruler, Duke Wén,
presented achievements at Héngyōng,
and received the vermilion bow from King Xiāng,
to treasure for his descendants.
I, Gài,
am the successor to my former ruler's official post;
how dare I not accept the command?"
The gentleman considered this to be knowing ritual.
A9.9 The Classic of the Ninth Year of Duke Xiāng
A9.9.1 In the ninth year, spring,
there was a fire in Sòng.
A9.9.2 In summer,
Jìsūn Sù went to Jìn.
A9.9.3 In the fifth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Lady Jiāngshì died.
A9.9.4 In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
we buried our lesser ruler, Mù Jiāng.
A9.9.5 In winter,
our duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Cáo,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
the Viscount of Zhū,
the Viscount of Téng,
the Earl of Xuē,
the Earl of Qǐ,
the Lesser Viscount of Zhū,
and the heir of Qí, Guāng, to attack Zhèng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐhài,
they made a covenant together at Xì.
A9.9.6 The Viscount of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
B9.9 The Commentary of the Ninth Year of Duke Xiāng
B9.9.1 In the ninth year, spring,
there was a fire in Sòng.
Yuè Xǐ, as Minister of Works,
took charge of governance,
and had Bóshì oversee the inner city.
Where the fire had not yet reached,
they dismantled small houses,
and plastered large houses,
Prepare baskets and earth-moving tools;
have ready ropes and earthen jars,
prepare water vessels;
measure the weight [of materials],
store up rainwater,
accumulate earth and mud;
patrol the city walls,
repair defensive preparations,
mark the fire lanes.
Order Huà Chén to assemble the regular laborers,
command the tunnel officers to gather the suburban guards,
and rush to the site of the fire.
Order Huà Yuè to oversee the right officials, each official attending to his duties.
Order Xiàng Xū to oversee the left,
doing likewise.
Order Yuè Chuán to attend to the penal instruments,
also doing likewise.
Order Huáng Yún to command the horse officers to bring out the horses,
the work officers to bring out the chariots,
prepare armor and weapons,
and attend to military defense.
Order Xī Chúwú to attend to the treasury’s defense,
command the palace director and the alley overseer to guard the palace.
The two commanders ordered the four district chiefs
to reverently make offerings,
the invocators and ancestral priests to use horses at the four ramparts,
and sacrifice to Pán Gēng outside the western gate.
The Marquis of Jìn asked Shì Ruò, saying:
"I have heard that
the Sòng disaster thus shows they understand the Way of Heaven,
what is the reason?"
He replied:
"The ancient Fire Director,
some took their station at the Heart [constellation],
some at the Beak [constellation],
to regulate the kindling and extinguishing of fires.
Therefore the Beak is called the Quail Fire,
the Heart is called the Great Fire.
The Fire Director of the Táo Táng clan, È Bó,
dwelt at Shāng Qiū,
sacrificed to the Great Fire,
and used fire to mark the seasons.
Xiàng Tǔ succeeded him,
thus the Shāng people revered the Great Fire.
The Shāng people observe the signs of calamity and ruin,
which must begin with fire,
therefore they daily know there is the Way of Heaven."
The Duke said: "Is it certain?"
He replied:
"It lies in the Way.
When a state is disordered, there are no signs,
it cannot be known."
B9.9.2 In summer,
Jì Wǔzǐ went to Jìn,
to return Xuānzǐ’s courtesy visit.
B9.9.3 Mù Jiāng died in the Eastern Palace.
When she first went there, she divined by the stalks,
obtaining Gèn changing to the eighth [line]
The scribe said:
"This is called Gèn changing to Suí
Suí
means to go out.
You must quickly leave!"
Jiāng said:
"No!
This in the Zhōu Yì says:
'Suí:
Fundamental, penetrating, beneficial, steadfast,
without blame.'
Fundamental
is the chief of qualities,
penetrating
is the gathering of excellence,
beneficial
is the harmony of righteousness,
steadfast
is the stem of affairs.
Embracing benevolence suffices to lead others,
excellent virtue suffices to accord with ritual,
benefiting things suffices to harmonize with righteousness,
steadfast and firm suffices to manage affairs.
Thus,
it cannot be falsely claimed,
therefore even Suí is without blame.
Now I, a woman,
was involved in disorder.
Firmly in a low position,
and lacking benevolence,
cannot be called fundamental.
Not bringing peace to the state,
cannot be called penetrating.
Acting and harming myself,
cannot be called beneficial.
Abandoning my position and being wanton,
cannot be called steadfast.
One who possesses the four virtues,
with Suí is without blame.
I have none of them,
how could it be Suí?
I have taken wickedness,
can I be without blame?
I must die here,
and will not get out."
B9.9.4 Duke Jǐng of Qín sent Shì Qiān to request troops from Chǔ,
intending to attack Jìn,
the Viscount of Chǔ agreed.
Zǐ Náng said:
"It cannot be;
at present we cannot contend with Jìn.
The ruler of Jìn matches abilities and employs them,
appointments do not miss the right selection,
officials do not change their methods.
His ministers yield to the worthy,
his great officers do not neglect their duties,
his officers strive in instruction,
his common people labor at farming,
merchants, artisans, servants, and slaves do not think of changing occupations.
Hán Jué is old,
Zhì Yīng receives [authority] from him to govern.
Fàn Gài is younger than Zhōng Háng Yǎn, yet Zhōng Háng Yǎn yields to him,
making him assistant commander of the central army.
Hán Qǐ is younger than Luán Yǎn,
yet Luán Yǎn yields to him,
making him assistant commander of the upper army.
Wèi Jiàng has many achievements,
and considers Zhào Wǔ worthy
and serves as his assistant.
The ruler is enlightened, the ministers loyal,
superiors yield, inferiors strive.
At this time,
Jìn cannot be opposed,
serve them and then it may be possible.
May you consider this!"
The King said:
"I have already agreed,
though not equal to Jìn,
we must send out troops."
In autumn,
the Viscount of Chǔ stationed troops at Wǔ Chéng,
to serve as support for Qín.
The Qín people invaded Jìn.
Jìn suffered famine,
and could not retaliate.
B9.9.5 In winter, the tenth month,
the feudal lords attacked Zhèng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Jì Wǔzǐ, Qí Cuī Zhù, Sòng Huáng Yún followed Xún Yīng and Shì Gài to attack the Zhuān Gate,
Wèi Běi Gōng Kuò, the people of Cáo, the people of Zhū followed Xún Yǎn and Hán Qǐ to attack the Shīzhīliáng Gate,
the people of Téng, the people of Xuē followed Luán Yǎn and Shì Fáng to attack the North Gate,
the people of Qǐ, the people of Ní followed Zhào Wǔ and Wèi Jiàng to cut down the chestnut trees.
On the day Jiǎxū,
they encamped at Fàn.
An order was issued to the feudal lords:
"Repair weapons and equipment,
fill provisions,
send back the old and young,
place the sick at Hǔ Láo,
pardon offenses,
and besiege Zhèng."
The people of Zhèng were afraid,
and sought peace.
Zhōng Háng Xiànzǐ said:
"Then besiege them,
to await the rescue of the Chǔ people,
and fight them.
Otherwise,
there will be no achievement."
Zhì Wǔzǐ said:
"Agree to their covenant and withdraw the troops,
to weary the Chǔ people.
We divide our four armies into three parts,
along with the elite troops of the feudal lords,
to meet those who come,
for us it is not burdensome,
but Chǔ cannot manage it.
This is still better than fighting.
Exposing bones to achieve [victory],
is not the way to contend.
Great labors are not yet ended.
The nobleman labors with his mind,
the common man labors with his strength,
such was the system of the former kings."
The feudal lords all did not wish to fight,
so they agreed to Zhèng’s peace.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
they made a covenant together at Xì,
Zhèng submitted.
When about to make the covenant,
the six ministers of Zhèng—Gōngzǐ Fēi, Gōngzǐ Fā, Gōngzǐ Jiā, Gōngsūn Zhé, Gōngsūn Chài, Gōngsūn Shèzhī—and their great officers and sons of ministers, all followed the Earl of Zhèng.
Jìn’s Shì Zhuāngzǐ prepared the covenant document,
saying:
"From today after this covenant,
if the state of Zhèng does not obey only the commands of Jìn,
or has any other intentions,
may it be as this covenant!"
Gōngzǐ Fēi hurried forward and said:
"Heaven has brought calamity upon the State of Zhèng,
placing it between two great states.
The great states have not shown virtuous intent,
but instead have used disorder to coerce us,
so that its ghosts and spirits cannot enjoy their pure sacrifices,
and its people cannot enjoy the benefits of their land.
Husbands and wives toil in hardship and distress,
with nowhere to turn and plead.
From this day, after the covenant is sworn,
if the State of Zhèng does not follow only those who are ritually proper and strong enough to protect the people,
and dares to have other intentions,
may it be likewise!"
Xún Yǎn said:
"Alter the covenant text!"
Gōngsūn Shězhī said:
"We have made a solemn pledge before the great spirits.
If it can be altered,
then a great state can also be betrayed."
Zhì Wǔzǐ said to Xiànzǐ:
"In truth, we lack virtue,
yet we coerce others to covenant with us.
How can this be ritually proper?
If it is not ritually proper,
how can we preside over covenants?
Let us simply covenant and withdraw.
Cultivate virtue, rest the troops, and then return.
In the end, we will surely gain Zhèng.
Why must it be today?
If we lack virtue,
the people will abandon us.
How could it be only Zhèng?
If we can achieve peace and harmony,
people from afar will come.
What need do we have to rely on Zhèng?"
So they made the covenant and returned.
B9.9.6 The people of Jìn, failing to achieve their aims with Zhèng,
led the feudal lords to attack it again.
In the twelfth month, on the guǐhài day,
they attacked its three gates.
In the intercalary month, on the wùyín day,
they crossed at Yīnbǎn,
and invaded Zhèng.
They encamped at Yīnkǒu and then returned.
Zǐ Kǒng said:
"The Jìn army can be attacked.
Their army is worn and weary,
and moreover, they have the desire to return home.
We would certainly inflict a great defeat on them."
Zǐ Zhǎn said:
"It cannot be done."
B9.9.7 The Lord of Lǔ escorted the Marquis of Jìn.
The Marquis of Jìn entertained the Lord of Lǔ with a feast on the riverbank,
and asked the Lord of Lǔ's age.
Jì Wǔzǐ replied:
"It was in the year of the meeting at Shāsuí
that our ruler was born."
The Marquis of Jìn said: "Twelve years,
that is called one cycle,
a complete cycle of Jupiter.
A ruler of a state has a son at fifteen,
for it is proper to have a son after the capping ceremony.
My lord may be capped.
Why does the great officer not prepare the capping implements?"
Wǔzǐ replied:
"For a ruler's capping,
it must be performed with the ritual of the libation offering,
accompanied by the music of metal and stone instruments,
and held in the ancestral temple of a former ruler.
Now our ruler is on a journey,
and it cannot be fully prepared.
We ask to wait until we are among our fraternal states
and borrow the necessary provisions there."
The Marquis of Jìn said:
"Very well."
The Lord of Lǔ returned,
and reaching Wèi,
was capped in the temple of Duke Chéng,
borrowing the bells and chime stones there.
This was in accordance with ritual.
B9.9.8 The Viscount of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
Zǐ Sì was about to make peace with Chǔ.
Zǐ Kǒng and Zǐ Jiǎo said:
"We made a covenant with a great state.
The blood on our lips is not yet dry, and we would betray it.
Can this be done?"
Zǐ Sì and Zǐ Zhǎn said:
"Our covenant stated clearly
'We follow only the strong.'
Now the Chǔ army has arrived,
and Jìn does not come to our rescue.
Thus, Chǔ is strong.
As for the words of the covenant and oath,
how would we dare to betray them?
Moreover, a coerced covenant lacks sincerity,
and the spirits do not oversee it.
What they oversee is good faith.
Good faith
is the token of words,
the essence of goodness.
Therefore they oversee it.
The bright spirits do not cleanse a coerced covenant;
to betray it
is permissible."
So they made peace with Chǔ.
Gōngzǐ Bàróng entered to make the covenant,
and they covenanted together at Zhōngfēn.
The Lady of King Zhuāng of Chǔ died,
and the King, unable to secure Zhèng, returned home.
B9.9.9 The Marquis of Jìn returned
and planned how to give the people rest.
Wèi Jiàng requested that relief be distributed
and stores of accumulated grain be transported out for lending.
From the ruler down,
if anyone had stores,
they were to bring them all out.
Thus, the state had no stagnant stores,
and also no destitute people.
The ruler did not monopolize profits,
and there were also no greedy people.
Prayers were offered with silk instead of animals;
guests were received with a single beast;
new vessels were not made;
carriages and robes were supplied only as needed.
After practicing this for one full year,
the state then had regulated economy.
After three campaigns,
Chǔ could no longer contend with them.
A9.10 *The Tenth Year of Duke Xiāng - The Text*
A9.10.1 In the tenth year, in spring,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Cáo,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
the Viscount of Zhū,
the Viscount of Téng,
the Earl of Xuē,
the Earl of Qǐ,
the Viscount of Xiǎozhū,
and the Heir, Guāng, of Qí, to meet with Wú at Zhā.
A9.10.2 In summer, in the fifth month, on the jiǎwǔ day,
they thereupon extinguished Bīyáng.
A9.10.3 The Duke arrived from the meeting.
A9.10.4 The Chǔ Gōngzǐ Zhēn
and the Zhèng Gōngsūn Zhé led an army to attack Sòng.
A9.10.5 A Jìn army attacked Qín.
A9.10.6 In autumn,
men of Jǔ attacked our eastern borders.
A9.10.7 The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Cáo,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
the Viscount of Zhū,
the Heir, Guāng, of Qí,
the Viscount of Téng,
the Earl of Xuē,
the Earl of Qǐ,
and the Viscount of Xiǎozhū to attack Zhèng.
A9.10.8 In winter,
bandits killed the Zhèng Gōngzǐ Fēi,
Gōngzǐ Fā,
and Gōngsūn Zhé.
A9.10.9 They garrisoned Hǔláo of Zhèng.
A9.10.10 The Chǔ Gōngzǐ Zhēn led an army to rescue Zhèng.
A9.10.11 The Duke arrived from the attack on Zhèng.
B9.10 *The Tenth Year of Duke Xiāng - The Commentary*
B9.10.1 In the tenth year, in spring,
they met at Zhā,
to meet with the Viscount of Wú, Shòumèng.
In the third month, on the guǐchǒu day,
the Qí Gāo Hòu, as assistant to the Heir Guāng,
met first with the feudal lords at Zhōnglí,
and was disrespectful.
Shì Zhuāngzǐ said:
"Gāo Zǐ assists the Heir in meeting with the feudal lords,
his duty being to guard the altars of soil and grain.
Yet he is disrespectful;
this is to abandon the altars of soil and grain.
I fear he will not escape calamity!"
In summer, in the fourth month, on the wùwǔ day,
they met at Zhā.
B9.10.2 Xún Yǎn and Shì Gài of Jìn requested permission to attack Bīyáng,
in order to enfeoff Sòng's Xiàng Xū there.
Xún Yīng said:
"The city is small but strong.
To conquer it would not be a display of martial prowess,
and to fail to conquer it would be a laughingstock."
They insisted on their request.
On Bǐngyín,
they besieged it,
but did not capture it.
Qín Jǐnfǔ, a retainer of the Méng clan,
transported supplies by cart to the campaign.
The people of Bīyáng opened the city gates,
and the soldiers of the various lords charged at the gate.
The portcullis was released,
but Zōu Rén Hé held it up,
allowing those who had entered to exit.
Dí Sīmí erected a large cart wheel,
covered it with armor,
and used it as a shield.
Holding it in his left hand,
and wielding a halberd in his right,
he formed a single unit.
Méng Xiànzǐ said:
"This is what the *Book of Songs* calls
'having strength like a tiger.'"
The defenders hung down a cloth,
and Jǐnfǔ climbed it.
When he reached the battlements, they cut it.
He fell,
and they hung it again.
After
reviving, he climbed it three more times,
until the defenders expressed their admiration,
and he then withdrew.
He wore the severed piece
and paraded it through the army for three days.
The armies of the various lords had been at Bīyáng for a long time,
and Xún Yǎn
and Shì Gài requested of Xún Yīng:
"The rainy season is about to arrive,
and we fear we will not be able to return.
We request to withdraw the army."
Zhì Bó was furious,
threw a stool at them,
which passed between them,
and said:
"You completed the two matters,
and only then informed me.
I feared to disrupt the command,
so I did not oppose you.
You have already troubled our lord
and mobilized the various lords,
dragging this old man here.
Having achieved no military success,
you now wish to shift the blame onto me,
saying:
'It was truly the withdrawal of the army.
Otherwise,
we would have conquered it.'
I am weak and old;
can I bear such a heavy responsibility?
If you do not capture it within seven days,
I will surely hold you accountable!"
On the Gēngyín day of the fifth month,
Xún Yǎn and Shì Gài led their troops to attack Bīyáng,
personally enduring arrows and stones.
On Jiǎwǔ,
they destroyed it.
The record says, "They then destroyed Bīyáng,"
meaning it followed from the meeting.
They gave it to Xiàng Xū.
Xiàng Xū declined, saying:
"If you, my lord, still deign to pacify and govern the state of Sòng,
and use Bīyáng to expand the territory of our humble ruler,
then the ministers will be at peace.
What greater gift could there be!
If it is bestowed solely upon me,
then it would mean I mobilized the various lords for my own enfeoffment.
What greater crime could there be!
I dare to request this even at the risk of death."
So they gave it to the Duke of Sòng.
The Duke of Sòng hosted the Marquis of Jìn at Chǔqiū,
and requested to perform the *Sāng Lín* dance.
Xún Yīng declined.
Xún Yǎn and Shì Gài said:
"Among the various lords, Sòng and Lǔ
are where one observes the rites.
Lǔ has the Dì music,
which is used for guests and sacrifices.
For Sòng to use the *Sāng Lín* to entertain you, my lord,
is that not also acceptable?"
During the dance, the master of the dance displayed a banner with pheasant feathers.
The Marquis of Jìn, frightened, retreated into a side chamber.
They removed the banner,
and the feast concluded before he returned.
When they reached Zhùyōng,
he fell ill.
They divined,
and the spirit of Sāng Lín appeared.
Xún Yǎn and Shì Gài wished to rush and offer prayers,
but Xún Yīng would not allow it,
saying:
"I declined the ritual,
but they proceeded with it.
If there are ghosts and spirits,
let them add the blame to them."
The Marquis of Jìn recovered after some time,
and took the ruler of Bīyáng back with him,
presenting him at the Wǔ Palace,
calling him a barbarian captive.
Bīyáng
was of the Yún surname.
They had the Zhōu court historian select a member of its lineage to succeed,
and settled them in Huòrén,
which was in accordance with ritual.
When the army returned,
Méng Xiànzǐ made Qín Jǐnfǔ his chariot right.
He fathered Qín Pīzī,
who served Zhòngní.
B9.10.3 In the sixth month,
Chǔ's Zǐ Náng and Zhèng's Zǐ Ěr attacked Sòng,
stationing their army at Zīwú.
On Gēngwǔ,
they besieged Sòng,
attacking at the Tóng Gate.
B9.10.4 Xún Yīng of Jìn attacked Qín,
in retaliation for its invasion.
B9.10.5 The Marquis of Wèi came to Sòng's aid,
stationing his army at Xiāngniú.
Zǐ Zhǎn of Zhèng said:
"We must attack Wèi.
Otherwise,
it means we are not siding with Chǔ.
If we offend Jìn,
and also offend Chǔ,
what will become of our state?"
Zǐ Sì said:
"Our state is already exhausted."
Zǐ Zhǎn said:
"To offend two great states
surely means destruction.
Exhaustion
is still better than destruction, is it not?"
All the senior ministers agreed.
Therefore, Huáng Ěr of Zhèng led an army to invade Wèi,
in accordance with Chǔ's command.
Sūn Wénzǐ divined about pursuing them,
and presented the omen to Dìng Jiāng.
Jiāng asked for the interpretation.
It said:
"The omen resembles mountains and hills;
there is a man going on campaign,
who will lose his leader."
Jiāng said:
"The campaigner losing his leader
means it is advantageous for resisting the enemy.
Minister, plan for this!"
The men of Wèi pursued them,
and Sūn Kuǎi captured Huáng Ěr of Zhèng at Quǎnqiū.
B9.10.6 In autumn, the seventh month,
Chǔ's Zǐ Náng and Zhèng's Zǐ Ěr invaded our western borders.
On their return,
they besieged Xiāo.
On the Bǐngyín day of the eighth month,
they captured it.
In the ninth month,
Zǐ Ěr invaded the northern borders of Sòng.
Méng Xiànzǐ said:
"Zhèng is likely to have a disaster!
Their military campaigns are excessively competitive.
Even Zhōu could not bear such competitiveness,
let alone Zhèng!
If there is a disaster,
will it not befall the three ministers in charge of its governance!"
B9.10.7 The people of Jǔ, taking advantage of the involvement of the various lords in affairs,
attacked our eastern borders.
B9.10.8 The various lords attacked Zhèng.
Cuī Zhù of Qí sent his heir apparent, Guāng, ahead to the army,
so he took precedence over Téng.
On Jǐyǒu,
they stationed the army at Niúshǒu.
B9.10.9 Earlier,
Zǐ Sì had a dispute with Wèi Zhǐ.
When they were about to resist the armies of the various lords,
he reduced Wèi Zhǐ's chariots.
When Wèi Zhǐ captured enemies,
they argued again.
Zǐ Sì suppressed Wèi Zhǐ, saying:
"Your chariots are not in accordance with ritual."
He then did not allow him to present the captives.
Earlier,
when Zǐ Sì constructed field channels,
the Sī, Dǔ, Hóu, and Zǐshī clans all lost land because of it.
Therefore, these five clans gathered a crowd of discontented men
and, relying on the followers of the princes,
started a rebellion.
Thereupon, Zǐsì took charge of the state,
Zǐguó served as Minister of War,
Zǐ'ěr served as Minister of Works,
and Zǐkǒng served as Minister of Education.
In winter, on the wùchén day of the tenth month,
Wèi Zhǐ, Sī Chén, Hóu Jìn, Dǔ Nǚfù, and Zǐshī Pú led bandits to enter,
attacking the government officials in the morning at the court of the Western Palace,
killing Zǐsì, Zǐguó, and Zǐ'ěr,
and seizing Duke Bó of Zhèng to take him to the Northern Palace.
Zǐkǒng knew about it,
and therefore did not die.
The record says "bandits,"
indicating there were no high officials among them.
Zǐxī heard about the bandits,
and without taking precautions, went out,
collected the corpses and then pursued the bandits.
The bandits entered the Northern Palace,
so he returned,
distributed armor,
but many servants had fled,
and many utensils were lost.
Zǐchǎn heard about the bandits,
set guards at the gates,
organized the various offices,
sealed the treasuries,
carefully secured the stores,
completed the defensive preparations, formed ranks, and only then went out,
with seventeen war chariots.
He collected the corpses and attacked the bandits at the Northern Palace,
Zǐjiǎo led the people of the capital to assist him,
killing Wèi Zhǐ and Zǐshī Pú,
and all the bandits died.
Hóu Jìn fled to Jìn,
Dǔ Nǚfù, Sī Chén, Wèi Piān, and Sī Qí fled to Sòng.
Zǐkǒng took charge of the state,
drafted a covenant,
to establish positions and order, and to follow government laws.
The high officials, various officers, and sons of ministers were not compliant,
and he intended to execute them.
Zǐchǎn stopped him,
and requested to burn the covenant for him.
Zǐkǒng would not agree,
saying:
"Making the covenant to stabilize the state,
and burning it because of the people's anger,
this would mean the people are governing,
wouldn't the state be in difficulty?"
Zǐchǎn said:
"The people's anger is hard to oppose,
personal desires are hard to achieve,
combining these two difficulties to bring stability to the state,
is a path to danger.
It would be better to burn the covenant to calm the people,
you will get what you desire,
and the people will also be at peace,
wouldn't that be acceptable?
Personal desires cannot be achieved,
opposing the people brings disaster,
you must follow this!"
Then they burned the covenant outside the Cāngmén gate,
and the people were thereafter settled.
B9.10.10 The armies of the feudal lords fortified Hǔláo
and garrisoned it,
the Jìn army fortified Wú and Zhì,
Shì Fáng and Wèi Jiàng garrisoned them.
The record says "garrisoned Zhèng's Hǔláo,"
though it was not Zhèng territory,
indicating it would be returned to them.
Zhèng made peace with Jìn.
B9.10.11 Chǔ's Zǐnáng came to rescue Zhèng.
In the eleventh month,
the armies of the feudal lords circled around Zhèng and went south,
reaching Yánglíng.
The Chǔ army did not retreat.
Zhì Wǔzǐ wanted to retreat,
saying:
"If we now flee from Chǔ,
Chǔ will surely become arrogant,
and when arrogant, we can then fight them."
Luán Yǎn said:
"Fleeing from Chǔ,
is a disgrace for Jìn.
To gather the feudal lords and increase disgrace,
is worse than death.
I will advance alone."
The army then advanced.
On the jǐhài day,
they faced the Chǔ army across the Yǐng River and encamped.
Zǐjiǎo said:
"Since the feudal lords have already formed their ranks,
they surely will not fight.
If we follow them, they will retreat,
if we do not follow them, they will also retreat.
When they retreat,
Chǔ will surely surround us.
Since we will retreat anyway,
it would be better to follow Chǔ,
and also use this to make them retreat."
That night they crossed the Yǐng River,
and made a covenant with the people of Chǔ.
Luán Yǎn wanted to attack the Zhèng army,
but Xún Yīng would not agree,
saying:
"We truly cannot resist Chǔ,
nor can we protect Zhèng,
what crime has Zhèng committed?
It would be better to leave them with resentment and return.
If we now attack their army,
Chǔ will surely rescue them.
If we fight and do not win,
we will be laughed at by the feudal lords.
Victory cannot be commanded,
it would be better to return."
On the dīngwèi day,
the armies of the feudal lords returned,
invading the northern border of Zhèng and then going home.
The people of Chǔ also returned.
B9.10.12 Wángshū Chénshēng and Bóyú contended for governance,
and the king supported Bóyú.
Wángshū Chénshēng was angry and fled.
When he reached the river,
the king recalled him,
and killed Shǐ Jiǎo to please him.
He did not enter,
and so was settled there.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Shì Gài to mediate in the royal house,
and Wángshū and Bóyú brought their dispute before him.
The steward of Wángshū and the minister of Bóyú, Xiá Qín, sat in court before the king's hall,
and Shì Gài heard their case.
The steward of Wángshū said:
"People of wicker gates and small doors all encroach upon their superiors,
it is hard to be a superior."
Xiá Qín said:
"In the past, when King Píng moved east,
our seven clans followed the king,
sacrificial animals were fully prepared,
the king relied on us,
and bestowed upon us the covenant of the red ox,
saying:
'For generations, do not lose your offices.'
If we were people of wicker gates and small doors,
could we have come east and settled?
And what would the king have relied on?
Now since Wángshū has been chief minister,
government affairs are accomplished through bribes,
and punishments are set aside for the favored.
The officers and commanders
are excessively wealthy,
how could we not be people of wicker gates and small doors?
Let the great state consider this!
If those below have no justice,
then what can be called correct?"
Fàn Xuānzǐ said:
"Whom the Son of Heaven supports,
our ruler also supports;
whom he opposes,
our ruler also opposes."
He had Wángshū's clan and Bóyú present their case summaries,
and Wángshū's clan could not produce their contract.
Wángshū fled to Jìn.
It was not recorded,
because it was not reported.
Dān Jìnggōng served as chief minister
to assist the royal house.
A9.11 《The Eleventh Year of Duke Xiāng, the Classic》
A9.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring,
the royal first month,
they formed three armies.
A9.11.2 In summer, the fourth month,
they divined four times about the border sacrifice,
and it was not favorable,
so they did not perform the border sacrifice.
A9.11.3 Zhèng's Gōngsūn Shězhī led an army to invade Sòng.
A9.11.4 The duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Cáo,
the heir of Qí, Guāng,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
the Viscount of Zhū,
the Viscount of Téng,
the Earl of Xuē,
the Earl of Qǐ,
and the Viscount of Xiǎozhū to attack Zhèng.
A9.11.5 In autumn, the seventh month, on the jǐwèi day,
they made a covenant together north of Bóchéng.
A9.11.6 The duke returned from attacking Zhèng.
A9.11.7 The Viscount of Chǔ
and the Earl of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
A9.11.8 The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Cáo,
the heir of Qí, Guāng,
the Viscount of Jǔ,
the Viscount of Zhū,
the Viscount of Téng,
the Earl of Xuē,
the Earl of Qǐ,
and the Viscount of Xiǎozhū to attack Zhèng.
They met at Xiāoyú.
A9.11.9 The Duke returned from the meeting.
A9.11.10 The men of Chǔ seized the Zhèng envoy Liáng Xiāo.
A9.11.11 In winter,
the men of Qín attacked Jìn.
B9.11 The Commentary for the Eleventh Year of Duke Xiāng
B9.11.1 In the spring of the eleventh year,
Jì Wǔzǐ was about to form three armies.
He informed Shūsūn Mùzǐ, saying:
"I request to form three armies,
each levying its own troops."
Mùzǐ said:
"Administration will soon come to you,
you certainly will not be able to manage it."
Wǔzǐ firmly requested it.
Mùzǐ said:
"In that case, shall we swear a covenant?"
Then they swore a covenant at Xī Hóng
and made a curse at the crossroads of Wǔfù.
In the first month,
they formed three armies,
dividing the ducal house into three parts
so that each had one part.
The three ministers each disbanded their own private chariot forces.
The Jì clan made it so that for the people of their chariot forces,
those who joined with their service settlements
paid no taxes,
while those who did not join paid double taxes.
The Mèng clan made half serve as retainers,
whether sons or younger brothers.
The Shūsūn clan made all serve as retainers,
otherwise they would not be kept.
B9.11.2 The people of Zhèng were troubled by the situation with Jìn and Chǔ.
The various grand officers said:
"If we do not follow Jìn,
the state will nearly perish.
Chǔ is weaker than Jìn,
and Jìn does not press us urgently.
If Jìn presses urgently,
Chǔ will avoid them.
What can we do
to make the Jìn army fight to the death for us,
so that Chǔ dares not oppose them,
and then we can firmly align with Jìn?"
Zǐzhǎn said:
"If we provoke hostility with Sòng,
the feudal lords will certainly come,
and we will follow them in a covenant.
When the Chǔ army arrives,
we follow them again,
then Jìn will be greatly angered.
Jìn can come repeatedly,
while Chǔ will be unable to,
and we will then firmly align with Jìn."
The grand officers were pleased with this,
and had the border officials provoke Sòng.
Sòng's Xiàng Xū invaded Zhèng,
capturing much.
Zǐzhǎn said:
"Now we can raise an army and attack Sòng.
If we attack Sòng,
the feudal lords' attack on us will certainly be urgent,
we will then heed their command,
and also inform Chǔ.
When the Chǔ army arrives,
we will then make a covenant with them,
and heavily bribe the Jìn army,
and thus be spared."
In summer,
Zhèng's Zǐzhǎn invaded Sòng.
B9.11.3 In the fourth month,
the feudal lords attacked Zhèng.
On Jǐhài,
Qí's heir Guāng
and Sòng's Xiàng Xū
first arrived at Zhèng,
attacking the east gate.
That evening,
Jìn's Xún Yīng arrived at the western outskirts,
and invaded east to the old Xǔ territory.
Wèi's Sūn Línfǔ invaded its northern borders.
In the sixth month,
the feudal lords met at Běilín,
and stationed their army at Xiàng.
They turned right,
and encamped at Suǒ.
They besieged Zhèng,
displayed their troops at the south gate,
and crossed west at Jìsuì.
The people of Zhèng were afraid,
and sued for peace.
In autumn, the seventh month,
they made a covenant together at Bó.
Fàn Xuānzǐ said:
"If we are not careful,
we will certainly lose the feudal lords.
If the feudal lords are worn out from the journey
and achieve nothing,
can they be without disloyalty?"
Then they made the covenant.
The covenant document said:
"All of us who are in covenant,
do not hoard grain,
do not monopolize profits,
do not harbor the wicked,
do not shelter the evil,
relieve disaster and distress,
sympathize with misfortune and disorder,
share likes and dislikes,
and support the royal house.
If anyone violates this command,
may the Spirits of Scrutiny and of Covenants,
the famous mountains and great rivers,
the host of spirits and host of sacrifices,
the former kings and former lords,
the ancestors of the seven surnames and twelve states,
the bright spirits punish them,
causing them to lose their people,
fall from mandate and perish their clan,
and topple their state and family."
B9.11.4 Chǔ's Zǐnáng requested troops from Qín.
Qín's Right Grand Officer Zhān led troops to follow the ruler of Chǔ,
intending to attack Zhèng.
The Earl of Zhèng went to meet them.
On Bǐngzǐ,
they attacked Sòng.
B9.11.5 In the ninth month,
the feudal lords brought all their troops to attack Zhèng again.
The people of Zhèng sent Liáng Xiāo
and the Grand Steward Shí Chuò to Chǔ,
to announce they would submit to Jìn,
saying:
"I, for the sake of the altars of soil and grain,
cannot remain loyal to you, my lord.
If you, my lord, can use jade and silk to pacify Jìn,
if not, then use military might to overawe them.
This is my wish."
The men of Chǔ seized them.
The record says "envoy,"
meaning they were messengers.
The armies of the feudal lords displayed their troops at Zhèng's east gate.
The people of Zhèng sent Wángzǐ Bópián to sue for peace.
On Jiǎxū,
Jìn's Zhào Wǔ entered to make a covenant with the Earl of Zhèng.
In winter, the tenth month, on Dīnghài,
Zhèng's Zǐzhǎn went out to make a covenant with the Marquis of Jìn.
In the twelfth month, on Wùyín,
they met at Xiāoyú.
On Gēngchén,
they released the Zhèng prisoners,
all treating them with courtesy and sending them back;
they withdrew their scouts;
and forbade plundering.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Shū Xī
to announce to the feudal lords.
Our Duke sent Zāngsūn Hé to reply, saying:
"All of us who are in covenant,
if a small state commits an offense,
and a great state sends punishment,
if there is something to serve as a handle,
rarely is there no pardon and forgiveness.
My humble lord has heard the command."
The people of Zhèng bribed the Marquis of Jìn
with the musicians Kuī, Chù, and Juān; fifteen matched pairs of wide chariots and tún chariots,
fully equipped with armor and weapons,
making one hundred war chariots in total;
two sets of chiming bells,
along with their bó bells and stone chimes;
and two sets of eight female musicians.
The Marquis of Jìn gave half of the musical gifts to Wèi Jiàng,
saying:
"You taught me to harmonize with the various Róng and Dí tribes
in order to rectify the various Huá states.
Within eight years,
I have nine times assembled the feudal lords.
Like the harmony of music,
there is nothing not in accord.
I ask to share this pleasure with you."
He declined, saying:
"To make peace with the Róng and Dí
is a blessing for the state.
Within eight years,
you have assembled the feudal lords nine times,
and the feudal lords harbor no ill will—
this is due to your divine power,
and the efforts of your ministers.
What strength have I contributed?
Moreover, I wish that while you enjoy your pleasures,
you would also think of their end.
The Book of Songs says:
'Joyful is the nobleman,
who safeguards the Son of Heaven's domain.
Joyful is the nobleman,
sharing in blessings and emoluments.
Well-attended by his retinue,
they follow and obey.'
Now, joy serves to secure virtue,
righteousness to handle affairs,
ritual to conduct them,
good faith to preserve them,
and benevolence to encourage them.
Only then can one safeguard the state,
share blessings and emoluments,
and attract people from afar—
this is what is meant by joy.
The Book of Documents says:
'In security, think of danger.'
Thinking leads to preparedness,
and preparedness averts calamity.
I venture to offer this admonition."
The Duke said:
"Your instruction—
how dare I not accept it!
But without you,
I would have had no means to deal with the Róng,
and could not have crossed the Yellow River.
Rewards
are the statutes of the state,
preserved in the covenant repository—
they cannot be set aside.
You must accept them!"
From then on, Wèi Jiàng began to possess music of bells and chimes—
this was in accordance with ritual.
B9.11.6 The Qín grandees Bào and Wǔ led an army to attack Jìn in order to rescue Zhèng.
Bào first entered Jìn territory;
Shì Fáng defended against him,
but, underestimating the Qín army, he did not set up defenses.
On the rénwǔ day,
Wǔ crossed from Fǔshì
and joined Bào in attacking the Jìn army.
On the jǐchǒu day,
Qín and Jìn fought at Lì,
and the Jìn army was badly defeated—
this was because they had underestimated Qín.
A9.12 The Spring and Autumn Annals, Year 12 of Duke Xiāng
A9.12.1 In the twelfth year, in spring,
in the king's third month,
the people of Jǔ attacked our eastern borders,
besieging Tái.
A9.12.2 Jìsūn Sù led an army to relieve Tái
and then entered Yùn.
A9.12.3 In summer,
the Marquis of Jìn sent Shì Fáng to come on a courtesy visit.
A9.12.4 In autumn, in the ninth month,
the Viscount of Wú, Shèng, died.
A9.12.5 In winter,
the Chǔ prince Zhēn led an army to invade Sòng.
A9.12.6 The Duke went to Jìn.
B9.12 The Commentary, Year 12 of Duke Xiāng
B9.12.1 In the twelfth year, in spring,
the people of Jǔ attacked our eastern borders,
besieging Tái.
Jì Wǔzǐ relieved Tái,
then entered Yùn,
taking its bells to make a basin for the Duke.
B9.12.2 In summer,
Jìn's Shì Fáng came on a courtesy visit,
and also to acknowledge our army's assistance.
B9.12.3 In autumn,
the Viscount of Wú, Shòumèng, died.
We observed mourning at the Zhōu temple—
this was in accordance with ritual.
For all feudal lords' deaths,
those of different surnames
observe mourning outside;
those of the same surname
in the ancestral temple;
those of the same clan
in the founding ancestor's temple;
and those of the same lineage
in the father's temple.
Therefore, because Lǔ was of the Jī surname,
we observed mourning at the Zhōu temple.
For Xíng, Fán, Jiǎng, Máo, Zuò, and Zhài,
we observed mourning at Duke Zhōu's temple.
B9.12.4 In winter,
